chandigarh-goa-rape-rate-child-cases.en:
Ask which part of India has the highest registered rape rate, and the 2024 data gives a clear answer: Chandigarh, with 16.6 cases per lakh women, nearly four times the national rate of 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Goa is second at 13.3, ahead of Rajasthan's 12.2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Turn one page of the same report, to the rows that split victims by age, and the ranking starts to look less like a map of danger and more like a map of paperwork.

## The top of the table

NCRB's ten highest registered rape rates in 2024 were Chandigarh (16.6), Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2), Delhi (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (9.9), Haryana (9.6), Himachal Pradesh (8.7), Chhattisgarh (7.7), Madhya Pradesh (7.2) and Lakshadweep (6.7) [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Look at the counts behind them. Chandigarh's rate comes from 96 cases and Goa's from 105; Rajasthan's comes from 4,871, about fifty times as many [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rate makes a territory and a large state comparable, but it also hides how few cases can carry a small place up a table.

Across India, rape made up 6.7% of all registered crimes against women in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. In Goa, its 105 rape cases were almost three in ten of its 356 registered crimes against women. In Chandigarh, 96 of 452, about one in five [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Goa's overall rate of crime against women, 45.2 per lakh women, was below the national 64.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yet its rape rate was India's second-highest. That gap deserves a second look.

## Half the cases are children's cases

NCRB's rape table also records how many cases involved girls under 18. In Chandigarh, it was 47 of the 96 cases. In Goa, 64 of 105. In Himachal Pradesh, seventh on the table, 194 of 324 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Set that against India. Of the country's 29,536 registered rape cases in 2024, only 784 involved girls under 18, because most child rape is recorded under the POCSO Act: police registered 43,313 cases of penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault on girls under its Sections 4 and 6 that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chandigarh, Goa and Himachal Pradesh, home to a small fraction of India's women, account for almost two in five of those 784 cases.

Count only the cases with adult victims and the top of the table changes. Chandigarh's rate would roughly halve, and Goa's would fall by more than half. Neither would sit above Rajasthan.

Why are these children in the rape row at all? NCRB counts each FIR once, under the offence carrying the maximum punishment [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and an FIR that invokes POCSO Sections 4 or 6, alone or with the rape sections, goes into the POCSO table [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB also only compiles what state and union territory police send it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So these cases reached the rape row through the sections written into the FIRs, or through how local police classified them. The published tables do not say which.

## Tamil Nadu: the opposite habit

Tamil Nadu shows the habit most of India follows, taken to its limit. It registered 419 rape cases in 2024, a rate of 1.1 per lakh women, the third-lowest in the country, and every one of those cases had an adult victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The same year it registered 6,969 POCSO cases, the third-highest count of any state, at 33.7 per lakh children [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Put Chandigarh beside Tamil Nadu and you are not comparing two levels of safety. You are comparing a rape table that includes children with one that leaves them out entirely. The first will always look worse.

Imagine two 15-year-old girls, one in Panaji and one in Madurai, each abused by a relative, and each case reported to the police by a school counsellor, as the POCSO Act requires of anyone who knows of such abuse [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The first may be counted in Goa's rape row and push it up the national table. The second lands in Tamil Nadu's POCSO table and leaves its rape rate untouched. In law both are children, since POCSO covers everyone under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Only the ranking differs.

## Small numbers, big swings

Small territories have volatile rates. Lakshadweep is tenth on the national rape table because of 2 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. One more case would have put it in the top five; one fewer, and it would have dropped below the national rate. At the other end, Ladakh's rate of 0.8, the lowest in India, is a single case [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Chandigarh's 96 cases are a bigger base, but small enough that its 47 cases involving girls decide where it ranks. Two distortions stack: a small population, and a filing habit few other places share. NCRB itself warns that more crime registered in a city is "not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. For a small territory whose rape row holds children, that warning applies twice over.

## Reading rape and POCSO together

None of this means Chandigarh or Goa is safe. Behind each of those cases is a woman or a girl whose rape was reported to the police. But the rape rate alone cannot rank places. Read it like this.

1. **Find the rape row and its count.** In *Crime in India 2024*, Volume I, Table 3A.2(i) gives each state's cases and rate. Note how many cases sit behind it.
2. **Find the girls' rows.** The same table lists rape cases involving girls under 18. A large share, as in Chandigarh, Goa and Himachal Pradesh, means the rate includes cases most states file elsewhere.
3. **Find the POCSO table.** Table 4A.2(ii) lists POCSO cases by state. Read it beside the rape row, never instead of it.
4. **Only then compare**, knowing what each state put in each table.

For India as a whole, an honest picture needs both tables: 29,536 rape cases and 43,313 POCSO cases of penetrative assault on girls in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A territory that tops one table by putting children in it has not become the most dangerous place in India. It has shown how much a ranking depends on where the paperwork goes.
chandigarh-goa-rape-rate-child-cases.hg:
Poochhiye ki India ke kis hisse mein registered rape rate sabse zyada hai, toh 2024 ka data saaf jawab deta hai: Chandigarh, har ek lakh women par 16.6 cases ke saath, jo 4.3 ke national rate ka lagbhag chaar guna hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Goa 13.3 ke saath doosre number par hai, Rajasthan ke 12.2 se aage [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi report ka bas ek panna palatiye, un rows tak jo victims ko umar ke hisaab se baant-ti hain, aur yeh ranking khatre ka naksha kam aur paperwork ka naksha zyada lagne lagti hai.

## Table ka sabse upar wala hissa

2024 mein NCRB ke das sabse oonche registered rape rates the: Chandigarh (16.6), Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2), Delhi (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (9.9), Haryana (9.6), Himachal Pradesh (8.7), Chhattisgarh (7.7), Madhya Pradesh (7.2) aur Lakshadweep (6.7) [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab inke peechhe ke counts dekhiye. Chandigarh ka rate 96 cases se nikalta hai aur Goa ka 105 se; Rajasthan ka 4,871 se, yaani lagbhag pachaas guna zyada cases se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rate ki wajah se ek chhote territory aur ek bade state ki tulna mumkin hoti hai, par rate yeh bhi chhupa deta hai ki kitne kam cases kisi chhoti jagah ko table mein upar pahuncha sakte hain.

Poore India mein 2024 ke women ke khilaaf registered crimes mein rape ka hissa 6.7% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Goa mein uske 105 rape cases, women ke khilaaf darj uske 356 crimes ke lagbhag das mein se teen the. Chandigarh mein 452 mein se 96, yaani lagbhag paanch mein se ek [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Goa ka crime against women ka kul rate, har lakh women par 45.2, national 64.6 se kam tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]], phir bhi uska rape rate India mein doosra sabse oonchaa tha. Yeh farq dobara dekhne layak hai.

## Aadhe cases bachchon ke cases hain

NCRB ki rape table yeh bhi darj karti hai ki kitne cases mein victim 18 saal se kam ki ladki thi. Chandigarh mein 96 mein se 47 cases aise the. Goa mein 105 mein se 64. Table mein saatve number wale Himachal Pradesh mein 324 mein se 194 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab ise poore desh ke saath rakhiye. 2024 mein India ke 29,536 registered rape cases mein se sirf 784 mein victim 18 saal se kam ki ladki thi, kyunki bachchon ke zyadatar rape cases POCSO Act mein darj hote hain: us saal police ne iske Section 4 aur 6 ke tahat ladkiyon par penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke 43,313 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chandigarh, Goa aur Himachal Pradesh mein India ki women ka sirf chhota sa hissa rehta hai, phir bhi un 784 cases mein se lagbhag paanch mein se do inhi teen jagahon ke hain.

Sirf adult victims wale cases giniye, toh table ka upar wala hissa badal jaata hai. Chandigarh ka rate lagbhag aadha ho jaayega, aur Goa ka aadhe se bhi zyada gir jaayega. Dono mein se koi bhi Rajasthan se upar nahi rahega.

Yeh bachche rape wali row mein aaye hi kyun? NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, us offence ke naam par jiski saza sabse zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur jo FIR POCSO ke Section 4 ya 6 lagati hai, akele ya rape sections ke saath, woh POCSO table mein jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB sirf wahi data jodta hai jo states aur union territories ki police use bhejti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Matlab yeh cases rape row mein ya toh FIR mein likhe gaye sections ki wajah se pahunche, ya is wajah se ki local police ne unhe kaise classify kiya. Publish hui tables yeh nahi batati ki dono mein se kya hua.

## Tamil Nadu: bilkul ulti aadat

Tamil Nadu wahi aadat dikhata hai jo zyadatar India mein hai, bas apni aakhri had tak. 2024 mein wahan rape ke 419 cases register hue, yaani har ek lakh women par 1.1, jo desh mein teesra sabse kam rate tha, aur in sabhi cases mein victim adult thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal wahan POCSO ke 6,969 cases register hue, jo kisi bhi state mein teesra sabse bada count tha, yaani har ek lakh bachchon par 33.7 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Chandigarh ko Tamil Nadu ke bagal mein rakhiye, toh aap safety ke do levels compare nahi kar rahe. Aap ek aisi rape table ko, jismein bachche shamil hain, ek aisi table se compare kar rahe hain jismein bachche bilkul nahi hain. Pehli wali hamesha zyada buri dikhegi.

Sochiye, 15 saal ki do ladkiyan hain, ek Panaji mein aur ek Madurai mein. Dono ke saath kisi rishtedaar ne abuse kiya, aur dono ke case school counsellor ne police ko report kiye, jaisa POCSO Act har us insaan se maangta hai jise aise abuse ka pata ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Pehli ladki ka case Goa ki rape row mein gina ja sakta hai aur Goa ko national table mein upar dhakel sakta hai. Doosri ka case Tamil Nadu ki POCSO table mein jaata hai aur uske rape rate ko chhoota bhi nahi. Law ki nazar mein dono bachchiyan hain, kyunki POCSO 18 saal se kam umar ke har insaan ko cover karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Farq sirf ranking mein padta hai.

## Chhote numbers, bade jhatke

Chhote territories ke rates bahut tezi se upar-neeche hote hain. Lakshadweep national rape table mein sirf 2 cases ki wajah se dasve number par hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek case aur hota toh woh top five mein pahunch jaata; ek kam hota toh national rate se bhi neeche chala jaata. Doosre chhor par Ladakh ka 0.8 ka rate, jo India mein sabse kam hai, sirf ek case hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Chandigarh ke 96 cases thoda bada base hain, par itne chhote ki ladkiyon wale uske 47 cases hi tay kar dete hain ki woh kis number par aayega. Yahan do distortions ek ke upar ek chadh jaate hain: chhoti aabadi, aur cases file karne ki aisi aadat jo bahut kam jagahon par hai. NCRB khud chetavni deta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada crime darj hona "not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" hai, yaani is baat ka saboot nahi ki woh jagah kam safe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Jis chhote territory ki rape row mein bachche gine ja rahe hon, uspar yeh chetavni do baar laagu hoti hai.

## Rape aur POCSO ko saath padhiye

Iska matlab yeh bilkul nahi ki Chandigarh ya Goa safe hain. In mein se har case ke peechhe ek aurat ya ladki hai jiske rape ki report police tak pahunchi. Par sirf rape rate se jagahon ki ranking nahi ho sakti. Ise aise padhiye.

1. **Rape row aur uska count dhoondhiye.** *Crime in India 2024*, Volume I ki Table 3A.2(i) mein har state ke cases aur rate hain. Dekhiye ki rate ke peechhe kitne cases hain.
2. **Ladkiyon wali rows dhoondhiye.** Usi table mein woh rape cases bhi hain jinmein victim 18 saal se kam ki ladki thi. Agar yeh hissa bada hai, jaise Chandigarh, Goa aur Himachal Pradesh mein, toh rate mein woh cases bhi shamil hain jo zyadatar states kahin aur file karte hain.
3. **POCSO table dhoondhiye.** Table 4A.2(ii) mein har state ke POCSO cases hain. Ise rape row ke saath padhiye, uski jagah kabhi nahi.
4. **Iske baad hi compare kijiye**, yeh jaan kar ki kis state ne kaun se cases kis table mein rakhe.

Poore India ki imaandaar tasveer ke liye dono tables chahiye: 2024 mein rape ke 29,536 cases aur ladkiyon par penetrative assault ke POCSO ke 43,313 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo territory bachchon ke cases ek table mein daal kar usmein top par pahunchta hai, woh India ki sabse khatarnaak jagah nahi ban jaata. Woh bas yeh dikhata hai ki koi ranking is baat par kitna tiki hai ki paperwork kahan jaata hai.

conviction-lottery-crimes-against-women-.en:
Imagine two women whose cases finally reach a verdict in 2024, one in Uttar Pradesh and one in West Bengal. Each complained of a crime against women: cruelty by a husband or his family, stalking, sexual assault or rape. In Uttar Pradesh, 76.6% of the crime-against-women trials completed that year ended in a conviction. In West Bengal, 1.6% did [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Same country, same criminal law, almost opposite odds.

## One country, two conviction worlds

Nationally, courts convicted the accused in 25.7% of crime-against-women trials completed in 2024. By the end of the year, 24,32,527 cases, 92.1% of all those before the courts, were still waiting for a verdict [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For rape alone, the conviction rate was 24.4%, with 5,032 convictions, and 1,85,785 rape cases were pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The average hides a split. Seven large states, West Bengal among them, convicted in fewer than one trial in ten, while Uttar Pradesh convicted in more than three of every four [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| State | Conviction rate, crimes against women, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | 76.6% |
| India | 25.7% |
| Maharashtra | 8.7% |
| Odisha | 6.3% |
| Karnataka | 4.8% |
| West Bengal | 1.6% |

Gujarat (9.9%), Assam (8.1%) and Andhra Pradesh (5.4%) complete the bottom seven [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In each of them, more than nine of every ten trials ended without a conviction.

## Uttar Pradesh's half of all convictions

Uttar Pradesh is an outlier twice over. It registered more crimes against women than any other state, 66,398 in 2024, although its rate of 58.0 cases per lakh women was below the national 64.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And its courts delivered 21,169 convictions, nearly half of India's 45,832 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A state with about one in six of India's women produced close to one in two of its convictions.

A conviction rate counts only trials that finished during the year: convictions divided by trials completed. It ignores the cases still waiting, and nationally those were 92.1% of everything before the courts at year-end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A high rate on the trials that finish can sit on top of a large backlog of trials that have not. A rate this far above every other large state deserves close study, both by states that want to copy it and by anyone checking what it really measures.

## West Bengal's 1.6% and India's biggest backlog

At the other end, West Bengal's courts recorded 203 convictions and 12,301 acquittals in crime-against-women cases in 2024, roughly 60 acquittals for every conviction. The state also carried India's largest trial backlog: 3,84,388 cases pending at the end of the year, a pendency of 96.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of every 100 cases on its courts' books that year, about 97 were still there when the year closed.

This is not a state where women do not complain. West Bengal registered 34,360 crimes against women in 2024, the fourth-highest count in India, at 70.3 per lakh women, above the national rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Complaints reach the police. Very few reach a verdict, and almost none of those verdicts is a conviction.

Delay has a cost. The longer a case waits, the more room there is for memories to fade, witnesses to drift away and a complainant to be pushed into a "compromise".

## Why state rates are slippery

Before reading the table as a ranking of justice, know its limits.

**The denominator shifts.** A state's rate depends on which trials happen to finish that year, often cases filed years earlier, and on how cases were classified. A small state such as Mizoram posts an even higher rate than Uttar Pradesh, on very few trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**"Crimes against women" is a basket.** Cruelty by husband or relatives made up 27.2% of cases registered in 2024 and rape 6.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], and each crime fares differently in court. Nationally, the conviction rate was 20.1% for cruelty by husband or relatives, 24.4% for rape, 32.3% for POCSO cases and 46.2% for dowry deaths [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A state whose courts happened to finish more cruelty cases would score lower without doing anything worse.

**Police and courts are separate links.** Andhra Pradesh filed charge-sheets in 94.4% of the crime-against-women cases its police disposed of, the highest of any large state, yet its courts convicted in 5.4% of completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A case can survive the police station and still collapse in the courtroom.

**The data cannot say why a trial failed.** An acquittal can follow a weak investigation, a hostile witness, a compromise or a false complaint, and the tables do not separate them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB's own word of caution says that comparing states on its crime data alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

None of this turns 1.6% into a working system. It means the useful question is not "which state is best?" but "where, in each state, does the chain break?"

## What would even out the odds

The law already promises speed on paper. Police must finish a rape investigation within two months of recording the complaint, and a rape trial is meant to end within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. With 1,85,785 rape cases pending at the end of 2024, those deadlines read as wishes.

Evening out the odds means repairing the links where cases die, state by state: investigations that gather evidence properly the first time, prosecutors with time to prepare, protection that lets complainants and witnesses testify without fear, and courts that hear these cases continuously rather than on scattered dates. It also means publishing why trials end in acquittal, so that a 1.6% rate triggers an audit instead of a shrug.

Individual women have some tools. A victim is entitled to an update on the investigation within 90 days, to free copies of the police report, FIR and statements soon after the accused first appears in court if she has a lawyer, and to be heard before any prosecution is withdrawn [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. She can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority for compensation even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

A woman's chance of justice should not depend on which side of a state border she lives on. Until states can explain gaps this wide, the numbers suggest it does.
conviction-lottery-crimes-against-women-.hg:
Sochiye do auratein hain jinke cases ka faisla aakhirkar 2024 mein aata hai: ek Uttar Pradesh mein, ek West Bengal mein. Dono ne crime against women ki complaint ki thi: pati ya uske parivaar ki cruelty, stalking, sexual assault ya rape. Uttar Pradesh mein us saal jo crime-against-women trials poore hue, unme se 76.6% conviction par khatam hue. West Bengal mein sirf 1.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek hi desh, ek hi criminal law, aur chances lagbhag ulte.

## Ek desh, conviction ki do duniya

Poore desh mein 2024 mein jo crime-against-women trials poore hue, unme se 25.7% mein courts ne accused ko convict kiya. Saal ke end tak 24,32,527 cases, yaani courts ke saamne jitne cases the unka 92.1%, ab bhi faisle ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sirf rape ki baat karein toh conviction rate 24.4% tha, 5,032 convictions ke saath, aur 1,85,785 rape cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh average ek bada fark chhupa leta hai. Saat bade states, jinme West Bengal bhi hai, das mein se ek trial mein bhi conviction tak nahi pahunche, jabki Uttar Pradesh ne har chaar mein se teen se zyada trials mein saza di [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| State | Crimes against women mein conviction rate, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | 76.6% |
| India | 25.7% |
| Maharashtra | 8.7% |
| Odisha | 6.3% |
| Karnataka | 4.8% |
| West Bengal | 1.6% |

Gujarat (9.9%), Assam (8.1%) aur Andhra Pradesh (5.4%) milkar neeche ke yeh saat states poore karte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se har state mein das mein se nau se zyada trials bina conviction ke khatam hue.

## Uttar Pradesh: India ke lagbhag aadhe convictions

Uttar Pradesh do tarah se alag hai. 2024 mein usne kisi bhi state se zyada crimes against women register kiye, 66,398, halaanki uska rate, 58.0 cases per lakh women, national rate 64.6 se kam tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur uski courts ne 21,169 convictions diye, jo India ke kul 45,832 ka lagbhag aadha hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis state mein India ki lagbhag chhah mein se ek aurat rehti hai, wahan desh ke lagbhag aadhe convictions hue.

Conviction rate sirf un trials ko ginta hai jo saal ke andar khatam hue: convictions ko poore hue trials se divide kiya jaata hai. Jo cases abhi intezaar mein hain, unhe yeh rate dekhta hi nahi. Aur desh bhar mein saal ke end tak courts ke saamne ke 92.1% cases yahi intezaar wale cases the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo trials khatam hote hain unpar rate ooncha ho sakta hai, jabki unke neeche un trials ka bada backlog pada ho jo khatam hi nahi hue. Baaki har bade state se itna upar ka rate dhyan se study karne layak hai: un states ke liye jo ise copy karna chahte hain, aur har us insaan ke liye jo check karna chahta hai ki yeh rate asal mein naap kya raha hai.

## West Bengal ka 1.6% aur India ka sabse bada backlog

Doosre chhor par, 2024 mein West Bengal ki courts ne crime-against-women cases mein 203 convictions aur 12,301 acquittals record kiye: har ek conviction par lagbhag 60 acquittals. India ka sabse bada trial backlog bhi isi state mein tha: saal ke end mein 3,84,388 cases pending, yaani 96.6% pendency [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal courts ki list par jo har 100 cases the, unme se lagbhag 97 saal khatam hone par bhi wahin pade the.

Aisa nahi hai ki yahan auratein complaint nahi karti. 2024 mein West Bengal ne 34,360 crimes against women register kiye, jo India mein chautha sabse bada number tha, 70.3 per lakh women ke rate par, yaani national rate se zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Complaints police tak pahunchti hain. Faisle tak bahut kam pahunchti hain, aur un faislon mein conviction lagbhag na ke barabar hai.

Deri ki bhi keemat hoti hai. Case jitna lamba latakta hai, utna hi yaadein dhundhli hoti hain, gawah door chale jaate hain, aur complainant par "compromise" ka dabaav badhta jaata hai.

## State ke rates par aankh band karke bharosa kyun nahi

Is table ko insaaf ki ranking samajhne se pehle, iski seemaayein samajh lijiye.

**Denominator badalta rehta hai.** Kisi state ka rate is par depend karta hai ki us saal kaun se trials khatam hue, jo aksar saalon pehle file hue cases hote hain, aur cases ko kis category mein rakha gaya. Mizoram jaisa chhota state bahut kam trials par Uttar Pradesh se bhi zyada rate dikhata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**"Crimes against women" ek tokri hai.** 2024 mein register hue cases mein 27.2% pati ya rishtedaron ki cruelty ke the aur 6.7% rape ke [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]], aur court mein har crime ka anjaam alag hota hai. Desh bhar mein conviction rate pati ya rishtedaron ki cruelty mein 20.1%, rape mein 24.4%, POCSO cases mein 32.3% aur dowry deaths mein 46.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis state ki courts ne us saal cruelty ke zyada cases khatam kiye, uska score kuch bhi bura kiye bina neeche aa jaayega.

**Police aur courts alag kadiyaan hain.** Andhra Pradesh ki police ne jitne crime-against-women cases dispose kiye, unme se 94.4% mein charge-sheet file ki, jo bade states mein sabse zyada tha. Phir bhi uski courts ne poore hue trials mein sirf 5.4% mein saza di [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Case police station se toh bach nikalta hai, par courtroom mein toot sakta hai.

**Data yeh nahi bata sakta ki trial kyun fail hua.** Acquittal kamzor investigation, hostile witness, compromise ya jhoothi complaint, kisi ki bhi wajah se ho sakta hai, aur tables inhe alag nahi karti [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB ki apni "word of caution" kehti hai ki sirf uske crime data ke basis par states ko compare karna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Inme se koi bhi baat 1.6% ko ek chalta hua system nahi bana deti. Matlab bas itna hai ki kaam ka sawaal "kaunsa state sabse achha hai?" nahi, balki "har state mein chain kahan toot rahi hai?" hai.

## Chances barabar kaise ho sakte hain

Law kaagaz par pehle se speed ka vaada karta hai. Police ko complaint record hone ke do mahine ke andar rape investigation poori karni hai, aur rape trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases pending the; aise mein yeh deadlines sirf khwahishen lagti hain.

Chances barabar karne ka matlab hai har state mein un kadiyon ko theek karna jahan cases dam tod dete hain: aisi investigation jo pehli baar mein hi theek se saboot ikattha kare, aise prosecutors jinke paas taiyaari ka waqt ho, aisi protection jisse complainant aur gawah bina darr ke gawahi de sakein, aur aisi courts jo in cases ko bikhri hui tareekhon par nahi, lagataar sunein. Iska matlab yeh bhi hai ki acquittals ki wajah public ki jaaye, taaki 1.6% jaisa rate dekh kar log sirf kandhe na uchkaayein, balki audit ho.

Akeli aurat ke paas bhi kuch auzaar hain. Victim ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update paane ka haq hai; agar uska vakeel hai, toh accused ke court mein pehli baar pesh hone ke kuch hi din baad police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies paane ka haq hai; aur koi bhi prosecution wapas lene se pehle sunwaai ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Woh State ya District Legal Services Authority mein compensation ke liye apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda na jaye aur trial hi na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Kisi aurat ko insaaf milne ka chance is baat par nahi tikna chahiye ki woh state border ke kis taraf rehti hai. Jab tak states itne bade gap ki wajah nahi batate, numbers yahi kehte hain ki aaj aisa hi hai.

conviction-rates-crimes-against-women-ra.en:
Every year the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reports how often trials end in conviction, crime by crime. Read side by side, the 2024 rates show a pattern no single headline does. Trials for murder with rape ended in conviction 76.4% of the time. Rape trials: 24.4%. Human trafficking trials: 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Here is the full table, and what it hides.

## The league table

NCRB's conviction rate divides the cases that ended in conviction by the trials completed that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For the main crimes against women and children in 2024, ranked:

1. **Murder with rape or gang rape: 76.4%.** 42 convictions in 55 completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
2. **Dowry death: 46.2%.** 1,869 convictions in 4,043 completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
3. **POCSO (sexual offences against children): 32.3%.** 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
4. **Rape: 24.4%.** 5,032 convictions against 13,980 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
5. **Cyber stalking or bullying of women and children: 22.8%.** Just 33 convictions, with 95.3% of cases still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
6. **Cruelty by husband or his relatives: 20.1%.** 10,689 convictions in 53,137 completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
7. **Human trafficking: 7.3%.** 43 convictions in 586 completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Across all crimes against women the rate was 25.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so rape sits just below the average. The rape row can only ever count women and girls: Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so an adult man cannot legally be a victim of rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Boys appear in the POCSO row; an adult man who is sexually assaulted has no row of his own.

## Rape-murder trials convict three times as often as rape trials

The two rows at the top share one fact. In murder with rape, and in dowry death, the woman at the centre of the case is dead.

NCRB does not record why a trial ends the way it does, but one difference is plain: these cases do not hinge only on a living woman's testimony holding up in court. Medical and circumstantial evidence carry more of the weight. In dowry deaths the law does part of the work too. If a woman dies of burns, injuries or in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after dowry-related cruelty soon before her death, Section 80 of the BNS deems her husband or in-laws to have caused it [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

When she survives, the case usually rests on her. She may have to give her account more than once, and finally in court, often years after the event. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024 the accused was someone she knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so the pressure to stay quiet often comes from inside her own world. Even a law tilted towards the prosecution does not close the gap. In POCSO trials for penetrative or sexual assault, the court must presume the accused committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and still fewer than one in three completed POCSO trials ends in conviction.

Read together, the top rows say something hard. Indian trials convict most reliably when the woman is no longer alive to testify, and least reliably when everything depends on a living survivor's evidence holding up through years of delay and pressure. That points at how cases are built and how witnesses are protected, not at survivors.

One caution: the 76.4% rests on only 55 completed trials, while 1,574 such cases were still waiting for a verdict at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The bottom: trafficking's 43 convictions

At the foot of the table, 43 trafficking trials ended in conviction in 2024. The other 543 completed trials ended in acquittal or discharge [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The law on paper is severe. Trafficking a person for exploitation carries 7 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 143 of the BNS, at least 10 years if the victim is a child, and the victim's consent is irrelevant [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Of 5,839 trafficked people rescued in 2024, 2,347 (40%) had been trafficked for sexual exploitation for prostitution and 1,493 (26%) for forced labour [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of 6,018 people recorded as trafficked, 2,297 were children, and more of them were boys (1,384) than girls (913) [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The crime itself can scatter the witnesses. Consider a hypothetical: a person trafficked across state lines may be rescued in one district, sent home to another and summoned years later to testify in a third, Each of those distances makes it harder for a witness to reach the courtroom. And the 2,135 trafficking cases NCRB recorded in 2024 come only from states' Anti-Human Trafficking Units; trafficking booked as kidnapping or child labour is counted elsewhere, so the real number is larger [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What a conviction rate leaves out

Every rate in the table is a fraction that hides at least four things.

**Only finished trials count.** Courts completed 53,137 trials for cruelty by a husband or relatives in 2024, while 8,54,798 such cases, 92.2%, were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The 20.1% describes the small slice that reached a verdict.

**Settlements are invisible.** The same year, 16,396 cruelty cases ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A compromise can be a real reconciliation or a woman pushed into withdrawing; the data do not say which.

**Cases are counted, not people.** A case with several accused counts once, whatever happens to each of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Averages blur differences.** Within rape, the rate was 31.4% when the victim was a girl under 18 and 23.7% when she was an adult woman [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

So a 24.4% conviction rate does not mean that three in four complaints were false. It means three in four completed trials did not end in a conviction, for reasons the table does not record: weak investigation, a hostile witness, a compromise and a false complaint all look the same in it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The biggest number sits outside every row: 24,32,527 crime-against-women cases, 92.1% of those before the courts, were still waiting for trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A conviction rate measures outcomes only in the cases that got that far.
conviction-rates-crimes-against-women-ra.hg:
Har saal National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) batata hai ki trials kitni baar conviction par khatam hote hain, crime by crime. 2024 ke rates ko saath rakh ke padho, toh ek pattern dikhta hai jo koi akeli headline nahi dikhati. Murder with rape ke trials 76.4% baar conviction par khatam hue. Rape trials: 24.4%. Human trafficking trials: 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh rahi poori table, aur woh sab jo yeh chhupati hai.

## League table

NCRB ka conviction rate simple hai: jin cases mein conviction hua, unhe us saal poore hue trials se divide karo [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 mein women aur children ke khilaaf main crimes, rank karke:

1. **Murder with rape ya gang rape: 76.4%.** 55 poore hue trials mein 42 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
2. **Dowry death: 46.2%.** 4,043 poore hue trials mein 1,869 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
3. **POCSO (bachchon ke khilaaf sexual offences): 32.3%.** 25,476 acquittals ke saamne 12,672 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
4. **Rape: 24.4%.** 13,980 acquittals ke saamne 5,032 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
5. **Women aur children ki cyber stalking ya bullying: 22.8%.** Sirf 33 convictions, aur 95.3% cases ab bhi pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
6. **Pati ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty: 20.1%.** 53,137 poore hue trials mein 10,689 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
7. **Human trafficking: 7.3%.** 586 poore hue trials mein 43 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Saare crimes against women ko milaakar rate 25.7% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani rape average se thoda neeche hai. Rape wali row mein sirf women aur girls hi gine ja sakte hain: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko ek aadmi dwara ek aurat ke khilaaf kiya gaya act maanta hai, isliye law ki nazar mein ek adult aadmi rape ka victim ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ladke POCSO wali row mein aate hain; jis adult aadmi ka sexual assault hua ho, uski apni koi row hi nahi hai.

## Rape-murder trials mein rape trials se teen guna zyada conviction

Table ke top ki do rows mein ek baat common hai. Murder with rape mein bhi, aur dowry death mein bhi, case ke centre mein jo aurat hai, woh mar chuki hai.

NCRB yeh record nahi karta ki trial jis tarah khatam hua, kyun hua, lekin ek farq saaf hai: yeh cases sirf ek zinda aurat ki gawahi ke court mein tike rehne par nahi latakte. Medical aur circumstantial evidence zyada bojh uthate hain. Dowry death mein law bhi kuch kaam khud kar deta hai. Agar shaadi ke saat saal ke andar kisi aurat ki maut jalne se, chot se ya abnormal haalaat mein hoti hai, aur maut se kuch hi pehle dahej ke liye uske saath cruelty hui thi, toh BNS ka Section 80 yeh maan ke chalta hai ki uski maut pati ya sasuraal walon ne hi cause ki [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Jab woh zinda bach jaati hai, toh case aksar usi par tika hota hai. Use apni baat ek se zyada baar batani pad sakti hai, aur aakhir mein court mein, aksar ghatna ke saalon baad. 2024 mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein accused koi aisa tha jise woh jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye chup rehne ka pressure aksar uski apni duniya ke andar se hi aata hai. Prosecution ki taraf jhuka hua law bhi yeh gap band nahi kar paata. POCSO mein penetrative ya sexual assault ke trials mein court ko maan ke chalna padta hai ki offence accused ne hi kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur phir bhi poore hue POCSO trials mein teen mein se ek se bhi kam conviction par khatam hote hain.

Dono top rows ko saath padho toh ek kadwi baat saamne aati hai. Indian trials sabse bharose se conviction tab dete hain jab aurat gawahi dene ke liye zinda nahi hoti, aur sabse kam tab, jab sab kuch ek zinda survivor ki gawahi par tika ho, jise saalon ki deri aur pressure jhelna padta hai. Yeh survivors ki taraf nahi, is baat ki taraf ishaara karta hai ki cases kaise banaye jaate hain aur gawahon ko kaise protect kiya jaata hai.

Ek savdhaani: 76.4% sirf 55 poore hue trials par tika hai, jabki 2024 ke end mein aise 1,574 cases ab bhi verdict ka wait kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Sabse neeche: trafficking ke 43 convictions

Table ke sabse neeche, 2024 mein sirf 43 trafficking trials conviction par khatam hue. Baaki 543 poore hue trials acquittal ya discharge par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kaagaz par law sakht hai. BNS ke Section 143 ke tehat exploitation ke liye kisi ki trafficking par 7 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, victim bachcha ho toh kam se kam 10 saal, aur victim ki consent ka koi matlab nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein rescue kiye gaye 5,839 trafficked logon mein se 2,347 (40%) ki trafficking prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation ke maqsad se hui thi, aur 1,493 (26%) ki forced labour ke liye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Trafficked record kiye gaye 6,018 logon mein 2,297 bachche the, aur unme ladkiyon (913) se zyada ladke (1,384) the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh crime khud gawahon ko bikher sakta hai. Ek hypothetical socho: jis insaan ki trafficking ek state se doosre state mein hui ho, use ek district mein rescue kiya ja sakta hai, doosre mein ghar bheja ja sakta hai, aur saalon baad teesre district mein gawahi ke liye bulaya ja sakta hai. Har doori ke saath gawah ka courtroom tak pahunchna aur mushkil ho jaata hai. Aur NCRB ne 2024 mein jo 2,135 trafficking cases record kiye, woh sirf states ki Anti-Human Trafficking Units se aaye hain; jo trafficking kidnapping ya child labour ke naam se darj hoti hai, woh kahin aur gini jaati hai, isliye asli sankhya isse zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Conviction rate kya chhod deta hai

Table ka har rate ek fraction hai, jo kam se kam chaar cheezein chhupata hai.

**Sirf poore hue trials gine jaate hain.** 2024 mein courts ne pati ya rishtedaaron ki cruelty ke 53,137 trials poore kiye, jabki aise 8,54,798 cases, yaani 92.2%, ab bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 20.1% sirf us chhote hisse ki baat karta hai jo verdict tak pahuncha.

**Settlements dikhte hi nahi.** Usi saal cruelty ke 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding par khatam hue, jo conviction wale 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Compromise sach mein sulah bhi ho sakta hai, aur case wapas lene ke liye majboor ki gayi aurat bhi; data yeh nahi batata ki kaunsa.

**Cases gine jaate hain, log nahi.** Kai accused wala case ek hi baar gina jaata hai, chahe har accused ke saath kuch bhi ho [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Average farq ko dhundhla kar deta hai.** Rape ke andar hi, victim 18 se kam umar ki ladki thi toh rate 31.4% tha, aur adult aurat thi toh 23.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Toh 24.4% conviction rate ka matlab yeh nahi ki chaar mein se teen complaints jhoothi thi. Iska matlab hai ki chaar mein se teen poore hue trials conviction par khatam nahi hue, aur kyun, yeh table record nahi karti: kamzor investigation, hostile gawah, compromise aur jhoothi complaint, sab isme ek jaise dikhte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse badi sankhya kisi row mein hai hi nahi: 2024 ke end mein crimes against women ke 24,32,527 cases, yaani courts ke saamne wale cases ka 92.1%, ab bhi trial ka wait kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Conviction rate sirf un cases ke nateeje naapta hai jo wahan tak pahunch paaye.

country-rape-rankings-mislead.en:
Every time a rape case in India makes global news, the same post returns: India is "the rape capital of the world". Soon comes the reply, often a table in which India's figure is tiny and Sweden's is huge: India, it says, is safer than Sweden. Both posts treat a rape statistic like a thermometer that reads the same everywhere. It is not one. Each figure measures violence, but also how freely women can speak, what the law calls rape, and who writes it down.

## Two viral claims, both wrong

The "rape capital" label usually comes with no number, or with a raw count. Police in India registered 29,536 rape cases in 2024, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Totals grow with population, and India's is among the world's largest. The counter-claim uses rates and makes the opposite mistake: it reads a low figure as proof of safety.

Both treat the number that reached a survey or a police register as the number of rapes. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) warns that each country's crime statistics follow its own criminal law, so the same act can be a crime in one country and not in another, and that only a varying share of offences is ever reported and recorded. Any international comparison, it says, must be read in the light of these differences [[unodc-iccs-2015]].

India's own data shows the problem in miniature. Under one law and one crime bureau, the registered rape rate in 2024 was 16.6 per lakh women in Chandigarh, the highest of any state or union territory, and 1.1 in Tamil Nadu, among the lowest [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Part of that gap is paperwork: about half of Chandigarh's cases under the rape head involved girls under 18, while Tamil Nadu files child cases under the POCSO Act. NCRB warns that more crime registered "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. If states cannot be ranked this way, countries certainly cannot.

## 4.1% versus 39.8%

WHO's 2023 estimates put lifetime sexual violence by someone other than a partner, since age 15, at 4.1% for women aged 15-49 in India and 39.8% in Sweden [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Read literally, Swedish women face nearly ten times the danger.

WHO does not read it that way: such gaps, it cautions, reflect disclosure, stigma and survey methods as well as real differences in violence. Even India's figure is uncertain: WHO's range runs from 2.5% to 5.8% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

The regions show the same shape: 4.7% in Southern Asia, India's region, against 17.8% in Western Europe, 19.5% in Australia and New Zealand and 23.3% in Central America [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO's previous round, on data up to 2018, also put Southern Asia joint lowest, at 2% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. The methods changed, so this is not a trend [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]], but the pattern held.

## Why disclosure drives the numbers

A survey counts only what a woman will tell a stranger. WHO explains: women in more gender-equal societies are more likely to disclose sexual violence, which raises the measured figure, while where stigma is high, services are few and reporting carries serious repercussions, the real level is likely much higher than the estimates [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Dedicated violence surveys also draw more disclosure than short modules inside broader surveys [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India's main source of such data, the National Family Health Survey, is the second kind. Our explainer on why surveys and police records disagree looks at what it misses.

Consider two women, both 24, both assaulted by an acquaintance after a party. One lives where sexual violence is discussed in classrooms and survivors expect to be believed. The other lives in a small Indian town, and the surveyor asking about forced sex sits in her in-laws' front room. For her, a yes could bring blame she cannot afford. The same act can produce a yes in one survey and a no in the other.

Police figures are thinner still. In most countries with data, fewer than 40% of women who experienced violence sought any help, and in almost all of them fewer than 10% of those who did went to the police [[un-worlds-women-2015]]. A police ranking mostly measures that last step.

## Same word, different crimes

Even when two tables both say "rape", they rarely count the same acts. Of 131 countries with data, just 38% have consent-based rape laws that explicitly criminalise marital rape, the UN's SDG Report 2026 finds [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]]. Elsewhere the definition is narrower: not based on consent, or not explicit about husbands.

India's law leaves husbands out. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape; Section 67 punishes non-consensual sex only with a wife living separately [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A challenge to the exception is pending in the Supreme Court, which listed it for final hearing in September 2026 [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. The BNS also has no rape offence for adult men or transgender survivors [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. They are missing from India's count by design, not because they are safe.

And the same WHO report that gives India 4.1% estimates that 22.4% of ever-married or partnered Indian women aged 15-49 faced physical or sexual violence by a partner in the past 12 months. That places India among the 33 countries and territory with the highest past-year rates [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Anyone who quotes the first number to call India safe is skipping the second.

## How to answer the next 'rape capital' post

You do not need a better ranking. You need four questions. Survey or police record? Which year and which ages? What does the law there call rape? Does the source itself warn against comparison? For both viral claims, the answer to the last is yes.

Cross-country numbers still have honest uses. They show that sexual violence is found everywhere, and which countries still exempt husbands. And a country can be tracked against itself, with the same survey and method, to see whether things change.

What they cannot do is crown a capital. India has a serious problem that its own data undercounts. A country where women can safely speak up can look worse on paper than one where they cannot.
country-rape-rankings-mislead.hg:
Jab bhi India ka koi rape case international news mein aata hai, ek post wapas ghoomne lagti hai: India "duniya ka rape capital" hai. Phir reply aata hai, aksar ek table ke saath jisme India ka figure bahut chhota hai aur Sweden ka bahut bada. Verdict: India Sweden se zyada safe hai. Dono posts rape statistic ko ek thermometer ki tarah dekhti hain jo har desh mein same reading deta ho. Aisa nahi hai. Har figure violence naapta hai, par saath mein yeh bhi ki auratein kitna khul kar bol paati hain, kanoon rape kise maanta hai, aur use likhta kaun hai.

## Do viral claims, dono galat

"Rape capital" wale claim ke saath aksar koi number nahi hota, ya hota hai toh bas total count. 2024 mein India mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye, yaani har ek lakh auraton par 4.3 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Totals population ke saath badhte hain, aur India ki population duniya ki sabse badi populations mein hai. Counter-claim rates use karta hai, par ulti galti karta hai: woh kam figure ko safety ka saboot maan leta hai.

Dono ek hi galti karte hain. Jo number survey ya police register tak pahuncha, use hi rapes ki asli ginti maan lete hain. UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is par saaf warning deta hai. Har desh ke crime statistics uske apne criminal law se bante hain, isliye ek hi kaam ek desh mein crime ho sakta hai aur doosre mein nahi. Aur har jagah crimes ka alag-alag hissa hi report aur record hota hai. UNODC ke mutabik har international comparison ko inhi farqon ko dhyan mein rakh kar padhna chahiye [[unodc-iccs-2015]].

India ka apna data yahi problem chhote scale par dikha deta hai. Kanoon ek, crime bureau ek. Phir bhi 2024 mein registered rape rate Chandigarh mein har lakh auraton par 16.6 tha, jo kisi bhi state ya union territory mein sabse zyada tha, aur Tamil Nadu mein 1.1, jo sabse kam rates mein se ek tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is gap ka ek hissa bas paperwork hai: Chandigarh mein rape head ke lagbhag aadhe cases 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke the, jabki Tamil Nadu bachchon ke cases POCSO Act mein darj karta hai. NCRB khud kehta hai ki zyada crime register hona is baat ka "indicator" nahi ki woh jagah doosri se zyada unsafe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Jab states ko aise rank nahi kar sakte, toh countries ko toh bilkul nahi.

## 4.1% versus 39.8%

WHO ke 2023 estimates dekho. Sawaal: 15 saal ki umar ke baad, partner ke alawa kisi aur se, zindagi mein kabhi sexual violence hui? India mein 15-49 saal ki auraton mein jawab 4.1% hai, Sweden mein 39.8% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Seedha padho toh lagega ki Sweden ki auraton ko lagbhag das guna zyada khatra hai.

WHO ise aise nahi padhta. Uski warning hai ki aise gaps disclosure, stigma aur survey methods se bhi aate hain, sirf violence ke asli farq se nahi. India ka figure bhi pakka nahi hai: WHO ke hisaab se yeh 2.5% se 5.8% ke beech kahin bhi ho sakta hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Regions mein bhi yahi pattern hai. Southern Asia, jisme India aata hai, 4.7% par hai, jabki Western Europe 17.8%, Australia aur New Zealand 19.5% aur Central America 23.3% par [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO ke pichhle round mein, 2018 tak ke data par, bhi Southern Asia sabse neeche tha, ek aur region ke saath barabari par, 2% par [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. Methods badal gaye hain, isliye ise trend mat samjho [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]], par pattern wahi raha.

## Batane ka mahaul hi number decide karta hai

Survey sirf wahi gin sakta hai jo ek aurat kisi anjaan insaan ko batane ko taiyaar ho. WHO ise saaf samjhata hai: jin samaajon mein gender equality zyada hai, wahan auratein sexual violence ke baare mein zyada batati hain, aur measured figure badh jaata hai. Jahan stigma zyada hai, services kam hain aur report karne ki bhaari keemat chukani padti hai, wahan asli violence estimates se kahin zyada hone ki sambhavna hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Ek baat aur: sirf violence par kiye gaye dedicated surveys mein auratein zyada batati hain, kisi bade survey ke andar chhote module mein kam [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India mein aise data ka main source, National Family Health Survey (NFHS), doosri type ka hai. Survey aur police records alag-alag baatein kyun kehte hain, is par humara explainer batata hai ki yeh module kya-kya miss karta hai.

Socho, do auratein hain. Dono 24 saal ki. Dono par ek party ke baad kisi jaan-pehchaan wale ne sexual assault kiya. Pehli aisi jagah rehti hai jahan classroom mein sexual violence par baat hoti hai aur survivor ko bharosa hota hai ki uski baat maani jayegi. Doosri India ke ek chhote shehar mein rehti hai, aur forced sex ke baare mein poochhne wala surveyor uske sasural ki baithak mein baitha hai. Uske liye "haan" kehne ka matlab aisa blame ho sakta hai jo woh afford nahi kar sakti. Ek hi ghatna ek survey mein "haan" banti hai aur doosre mein "na".

Police figures toh aur bhi kam pakadte hain. Jin countries ka data hai, unme se zyada tar mein violence jhelne wali 40% se bhi kam auraton ne kisi tarah ki help maangi, aur lagbhag sabhi mein help maangne walon mein se 10% se bhi kam police ke paas gayi [[un-worlds-women-2015]]. Yaani police wali ranking zyada tar bas yahi aakhri step naapti hai.

## Shabd ek, crime alag

Do tables mein "rape" likha ho, tab bhi woh shayad hi same cheez ginti hain. UN ki SDG Report 2026 ke mutabik, jin 131 countries ka data hai, unme se sirf 38% mein aisa rape law hai jo consent par based hai aur marital rape ko bhi saaf taur par crime maanta hai [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]]. Baaki jagah definition chhoti hai: ya toh consent par based nahi, ya husbands ke baare mein saaf nahi.

India ka kanoon husbands ko bahar rakhta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke hisaab se, agar wife 18 saal se kam ki nahi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai; Section 67 bina consent ke sex par saza sirf tab deta hai jab wife alag reh rahi ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is exception ke khilaaf challenge Supreme Court mein pending hai, aur court ne September 2026 mein ise final hearing ke liye list kiya [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. BNS mein adult mardon aur transgender survivors ke liye bhi rape ka koi offence nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh sab India ki ginti se kanoon ke design ki wajah se bahar hain, isliye nahi ki woh safe hain.

Aur wahi WHO report jo India ko 4.1% deti hai, ek aur estimate bhi deti hai: India ki 15-49 saal ki married ya partnered 22.4% auraton ne pichhle 12 mahino mein partner ki physical ya sexual violence jheli. Isse India un 33 countries aur territory mein aa jaata hai jahan past-year rate sabse zyada hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Jo pehla number dikha kar India ko safe bolta hai, woh doosra number chhod raha hai.

## Agli "rape capital" post ka jawab kaise do

Tumhe behtar ranking nahi chahiye. Chaar sawaal chahiye. Survey hai ya police record? Kaunsa saal, kis umar ke log? Wahan ka kanoon rape kise maanta hai? Kya source khud comparison se mana karta hai? Dono viral claims mein aakhri sawaal ka jawab hai: haan.

Countries ke numbers ka imaandaar use bhi hai. Woh dikhate hain ki sexual violence har jagah hoti hai, aur kin countries mein aaj bhi husbands ko chhoot hai. Aur kisi desh ko uske apne purane data se naapa ja sakta hai, same survey aur same method se, yeh dekhne ke liye ki halaat badal rahe hain ya nahi.

Bas woh kisi desh ko "capital" ka taj nahi pehna sakte. India mein problem serious hai, aur uska apna data use kam ginta hai. Jis desh mein auratein bekhauf bol paati hain, woh kaagaz par us desh se bura dikh sakta hai jahan woh bol nahi paati.

crime-in-india-2024-sexual-violence-deco.en:
The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) released *Crime in India 2024* on 6 May 2026 [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]]. As of 20 November 2026 there is still no 2025 edition [[ncrb-website-cii-year-wise-2026]], so these are the newest official numbers on sexual violence in India, the ones every debate, speech and reel will lean on until the next report. This card pulls out ten of them. Keep it open the next time one is quoted at you.

## How to use this card

Each entry gives the number, what it counts, and the caveat that most often gets dropped. Three rules apply to all ten.

- **They are police records.** Each figure is an FIR or a court record from 2024, not a measure of how much violence happened. NCRB itself says "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **States supplied them.** NCRB compiles what state and union territory police send, and says it is not responsible for the authenticity of that information [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **2024 had two penal codes.** The rape cases split into 19,683 filed under the Indian Penal Code and 9,853 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced it on 1 July 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Five numbers about the crimes

**1. 4,41,534 crimes against women.** Registered in 2024, 1.5% fewer than the 4,48,211 of 2023, at a rate of 64.6 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* this is the broadest head, and it includes special-law cases such as POCSO cases with girl victims. A 1.5% dip in registrations is not proof of a dip in violence.

**2. 29,536 rape cases.** A rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* it counts only what the law defines as rape. Section 63 of the BNS covers a man assaulting a woman, and exempts a husband unless his wife is under 18 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Wives living with their husbands, adult men and transgender survivors are therefore absent.

**3. 29,742 victims.** Victims outnumber cases because one FIR can name more than one person. Of them, 792 were girls under 18 and 19,489 were women aged 18 to 30 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* 792 is not the number of child rape victims. Most child rape is filed under POCSO, which is the next number.

**4. 43,313 child-rape cases with girl victims.** Cases of penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault on girls under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, involving 43,675 girls, more than the whole rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* girls only. Boys are in the chapter on crimes against children, which recorded 892 boys as victims of penetrative assault [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**5. 266 rape-murders.** Cases of murder with rape or gang rape, with 274 victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* NCRB's "principal offence rule" counts each FIR once, under the offence with the heaviest punishment [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so these 266 are not inside the 29,536.

## Five numbers about the accused and the courts

**6. 96.8% known to the survivor.** In 28,597 of the 29,536 rape cases, the accused was someone the victim knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The largest group, 13,879 cases, was friends, online friends, live-in partners "on the pretext of marriage" or separated husbands; family members were accused in 2,134 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* NCRB puts relationships and promises of marriage in one column, so the data cannot say how many cases involved a broken promise.

**7. 5,032 convictions.** Rape cases in which courts convicted the accused in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* they are counted by case, not by person, and many of these trials began with FIRs filed years earlier. You cannot set them against 2024's 29,536 FIRs.

**8. 13,980 acquittals.** Rape cases in which courts acquitted in 2024, far more than they convicted [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* an acquittal means the court held that the charge was not proved. It is not a finding that the complaint was false.

**9. 24.4% conviction rate.** That is 5,032 convictions out of 20,587 rape trials completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], up from 22.7% in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. *The caveat:* the base is trials completed that year, not cases registered and not accused persons. The rest of the completed trials ended in acquittal or discharge.

**10. 1,85,785 cases pending trial.** Rape cases still waiting at the end of 2024, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 that were before the courts during the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *The caveat:* do not quote 2,06,777 as the backlog. That is the year's whole caseload, old and new; 1,85,785 is what was left undecided.

## The caveats in one place

Before you quote any of the ten, check which of these applies.

- **Registered, not committed (all ten).** A 2022 study in *BMC Public Health* cited estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence in India report it to the authorities [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].
- **One FIR, one offence (numbers 2, 3 and 5).** Rape-murders and POCSO cases sit outside the rape head.
- **Children are mostly elsewhere (numbers 3 and 4).** Add the POCSO figure whenever you talk about rape in India.
- **Some survivors are missing by law (numbers 2, 3 and 6).** Wives living with their husbands, adult men and transgender survivors.
- **Courts count cases, not people, and not this year's FIRs (numbers 7 to 10).**
- **Two years old (all ten).** Nothing official yet covers 2025 or 2026.

Read with these caveats, the ten numbers are a precise record of what police and courts did in 2024. Read without them, they become the next viral mistake.
crime-in-india-2024-sexual-violence-deco.hg:
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne *Crime in India 2024* 6 May 2026 ko release ki [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]]. 20 November 2026 tak bhi 2025 ka koi edition nahi aaya hai [[ncrb-website-cii-year-wise-2026]], isliye India mein sexual violence par yahi sabse naye official numbers hain. Agli report aane tak har debate, har speech aur har reel inhi par tiki rahegi. Yeh card unmein se das numbers nikaalta hai. Agli baar jab inmein se koi number aapke saamne quote ho, toh ise khula rakhiye.

## Is card ko kaise use karein

Har entry mein number hai, woh kya ginta hai, aur woh caveat jo aksar chhoot jaata hai. Teen rules dason numbers par laagu hote hain.

- **Yeh police records hain.** Har figure 2024 ki ek FIR ya court record hai, is baat ka naap nahi ki asal mein kitni violence hui. NCRB khud kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag cheezein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Inhe states ne bheja.** NCRB wahi compile karta hai jo states aur union territories ki police bhejti hai, aur kehta hai ki is jaankari ki authenticity ki zimmedari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **2024 mein do penal codes the.** Rape cases do hisson mein bante: 19,683 Indian Penal Code ke tehat aur 9,853 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke tehat, jisne 1 July 2024 ko IPC ki jagah li [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Crimes ke baare mein paanch numbers

**1. Auraton ke khilaaf 4,41,534 crimes.** 2024 mein register hue, 2023 ke 4,48,211 se 1.5% kam, har lakh auraton par 64.6 ke rate se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* yeh sabse bada head hai, aur ismein special laws ke cases bhi shaamil hain, jaise girl victims wale POCSO cases. Registrations mein 1.5% ki girawat violence mein girawat ka saboot nahi hai.

**2. 29,536 rape cases.** Har lakh auraton par 4.3 ka rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* yeh sirf woh ginta hai jise law rape maanta hai. BNS ka Section 63 ek aadmi dwara ek aurat par kiye gaye assault ko cover karta hai, aur pati ko chhoot deta hai jab tak patni 18 saal se kam na ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Isliye pati ke saath rehne wali patniyan, adult mard aur transgender survivors is figure se gayab hain.

**3. 29,742 victims.** Victims cases se zyada hain, kyunki ek FIR mein ek se zyada logon ke naam ho sakte hain. Inmein se 792 ladkiyan 18 saal se kam ki thi aur 19,489 auratein 18 se 30 saal ki thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* 792 child rape victims ki ginti nahi hai. Bachchon ke zyadatar rape POCSO ke tehat file hote hain, aur wahi agla number hai.

**4. Girl victims wale 43,313 child-rape cases.** POCSO Act ke Sections 4 aur 6 ke tehat ladkiyon par penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke cases, jinmein 43,675 ladkiyan thi. Yeh poore rape head se bhi zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* sirf ladkiyan. Ladke crimes against children wale chapter mein hain, jahan 892 ladke penetrative assault ke victims ke roop mein record hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**5. 266 rape-murders.** Murder with rape ya gang rape ke cases, 274 victims ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* NCRB ka "principal offence rule" har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, us offence ke naam par jiski saza sabse bhaari ho [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye yeh 266 cases 29,536 ke andar nahi hain.

## Accused aur courts ke baare mein paanch numbers

**6. 96.8% survivor ke jaan-pehchaan wale.** 29,536 rape cases mein se 28,597 mein accused koi aisa tha jise victim jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse bada group, 13,879 cases, dost, online dost, "on the pretext of marriage" wale live-in partners ya alag rehne wale pati the; family members 2,134 cases mein accused the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* NCRB relationships aur shaadi ke vaadon ko ek hi column mein rakhta hai, isliye data yeh nahi bata sakta ki kitne cases toote hue vaade se jude the.

**7. 5,032 convictions.** Woh rape cases jinmein 2024 mein courts ne accused ko convict kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* yeh case ke hisaab se gine jaate hain, vyakti ke hisaab se nahi, aur inmein se kai trials saalon pehle file hui FIRs se shuru hue the. Inhe 2024 ki 29,536 FIRs ke saamne rakh kar nahi dekha ja sakta.

**8. 13,980 acquittals.** Woh rape cases jinmein 2024 mein courts ne accused ko bari kiya, convictions se kahin zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* acquittal ka matlab hai ki court ne maana ki charge saabit nahi hua. Yeh is baat ka faisla nahi hai ki complaint jhoothi thi.

**9. 24.4% conviction rate.** Yaani 2024 mein poore hue 20,587 rape trials mein se 5,032 convictions [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jo 2023 ke 22.7% se zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. *Caveat:* iska base us saal poore hue trials hain, register hue cases nahi, aur accused log bhi nahi. Baaki poore hue trials acquittal ya discharge par khatam hue.

**10. Trial ka intezaar kar rahe 1,85,785 cases.** 2024 ke end mein bhi intezaar kar rahe rape cases, jo saal bhar courts ke saamne rahe 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. *Caveat:* 2,06,777 ko backlog bata kar quote mat kijiye. Woh saal ka poora caseload hai, purana aur naya milakar; 1,85,785 woh hai jiska faisla nahi hua.

## Saare caveats ek jagah

Dason mein se koi bhi number quote karne se pehle dekhiye ki inmein se kaunsa caveat laagu hota hai.

- **Registered cases, kul crimes nahi (dason par).** 2022 mein *BMC Public Health* mein chhapi ek study ne un estimates ka hawala diya jinke mutabik India mein sexual violence ke sirf lagbhag 1% victims authorities ko report karte hain [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].
- **Ek FIR, ek offence (numbers 2, 3 aur 5).** Rape-murders aur POCSO cases rape head se bahar hain.
- **Bachche zyadatar kahin aur hain (numbers 3 aur 4).** Jab bhi India mein rape ki baat karein, POCSO figure saath jodiye.
- **Kuch survivors law ki wajah se gayab hain (numbers 2, 3 aur 6).** Pati ke saath rehne wali patniyan, adult mard aur transgender survivors.
- **Courts cases ginte hain, log nahi, aur is saal ki FIRs bhi nahi (numbers 7 se 10).**
- **Do saal purane (dason par).** 2025 ya 2026 ka koi official data abhi nahi hai.

In caveats ke saath padhein, toh yeh das numbers is baat ka sateek record hain ki 2024 mein police aur courts ne kya kiya. Inke bina padhein, toh yahi agli viral galti ban jaate hain.

custodial-rape-abuse-of-authority.en:
India's 1983 rape-law reform began with a case from a police station. Today the law has a detailed vocabulary for sexual abuse by people with power over their victims: police, jail staff, wardens, doctors. What it still lacks is a reliable way for those victims to be heard, and a record that counts them all.

## 1978: where it started

In 1978 the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a Maharashtra police station in 1972. The judges noted that she had no injuries and called the intercourse "a peaceful affair" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Our separate case file tells that story.

The protests that followed changed the law. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence and introduced a presumption, in custodial rape trials, that the woman had not consented [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Inside a lock-up, "she did not fight back" proves nothing, because fighting back was never a real option. In 2013 Parliament extended the idea to every rape: not physically resisting is not, by itself, consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

## What the law now calls aggravated

Since 1 July 2024, rape has been punished under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], with at least 10 years in prison. Its aggravated forms carry 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, and the first five are about institutional power: rape by a police officer, a public servant, a member of the armed forces, jail or custody staff, or hospital staff. The list continues with relatives, guardians, teachers and anyone in "a position of trust or authority" towards the woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The rules of evidence shift too. In these aggravated cases, once intercourse is proved and the woman testifies that she did not consent, the court "shall presume that she did not consent" under Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. The man who held the keys has to disprove it.

## Section 68: when a 'yes' is extracted by power

Some abuse of power looks nothing like force. Section 68 of the BNS punishes a person in authority, a public servant, or jail, institution or hospital staff who abuses that position to get a woman in his custody or care to have sex with him, short of rape, with 5 to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Consider a 19-year-old in a state-run women's shelter. The superintendent signs her release papers, decides who may visit her and writes the reports a court will read. He hints that things could move faster. If she gives in, the law sees a crime by him, not a choice between equals: a "yes" given to the person who controls your freedom is not a free yes.

## What the record sees, and who it leaves out

Of the 29,536 rape cases registered in India in 2024, police recorded these under the clauses for people in uniform or in charge [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Accused | Rape cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Police personnel | 27 |
| Other public servants | 15 |
| Members of the armed forces | 2 |
| Staff of jails, remand homes or places of custody | 3 |
| Hospital staff | 8 |

A case enters these rows only if police invoke that clause, and the officers deciding may be the accused's colleagues. Most survivors never get that far: in NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone, and only 6% of those who sought help went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. When the abuser is a policeman, even that narrow route runs through his own force. These numbers are a floor.

Some survivors are missing by design. Section 63 of the BNS defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman", and Section 68 protects only women [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The BNS dropped Section 377 of the old penal code, which had covered non-consensual sex against men, and put nothing in its place [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. So an adult man sexually assaulted by a police officer in a lock-up has no rape offence to file. Parliament's Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned of this gap on 10 November 2023; the government did not accept its advice [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Sexual abuse of a transgender person carries only six months to two years in prison [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Why custodial abuse goes unreported

Reporting abuse by someone in authority means asking his own institution to act against him. Three cases show what that can mean.

- **Kathua, 2018.** On 10 June 2019 a Pathankot court convicted six of the seven people tried for the rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl. Three were policemen, jailed for five years for destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]].
- **Gujarat, 2002.** In the riots gang rape case, a Mumbai special court convicted a police officer in 2008 of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly; in 2017 the Bombay High Court also convicted five police personnel and two doctors whom the trial court had acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].
- **Muzaffarpur, 2018.** Abuse at a state-funded girls' shelter home came to light when the Tata Institute of Social Sciences audited Bihar's children's homes for the state government [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. The audit revealed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. In January 2020 a Delhi court convicted 19 of the 20 accused [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

In each case, the people or institutions meant to record the crime, protect the evidence or shelter the child were part of the problem. Custodial survivors face the same wall: the FIR and the investigation pass through the accused's colleagues.

There are ways around that wall. A survivor can report at any police station, whatever the place of the crime, or send the complaint electronically and sign it within three days, and must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A woman's rape complaint must be recorded by a woman officer, and her statement is to be taken at her home or at a place she chooses [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who fails to record a rape FIR faces six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The 1983 law exists because a court once read a girl's silence in a police station as consent. Its test today is whether someone abused by a person in uniform can walk into another station and be believed.
custodial-rape-abuse-of-authority.hg:
India mein 1983 ka rape law reform ek police station ke case se shuru hua tha. Aaj law ke paas un logon ke sexual abuse ke liye poori vocabulary hai jinke haath mein victim par power hoti hai: police, jail staff, warden, doctor. Jo ab bhi nahi hai, woh hai aise victims ki baat sune jaane ka ek bharosemand raasta, aur ek aisa record jo un sabko gine.

## 1978: yahin se shuru hua

1978 mein Supreme Court ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya, jin par 1972 mein Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek naabaalig ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Judges ne note kiya ki ladki ke shareer par koi chot nahi thi, aur intercourse ko "a peaceful affair", yaani ek shaant maamla, kaha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Yeh poori kahani hamari alag case file mein hai.

Uske baad hue protests ne law badal diya. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 ne custodial rape ko ek alag aggravated offence banaya, aur custodial rape ke trials mein yeh presumption joda ki aurat ne consent nahi diya tha [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Lock-up ke andar "usne ladaai nahi ki" se kuch saabit nahi hota, kyunki ladna wahan kabhi asli option tha hi nahi. 2013 mein Parliament ne yahi soch har rape par laagu kar di: physically resist na karna, apne aap mein, consent nahi hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

## Law ab kise aggravated maanta hai

1 July 2024 se rape ki saza Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64 ke tahat milti hai [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]: kam se kam 10 saal ki jail. Iske aggravated roopon mein 10 saal se lekar baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak ho sakti hai, aur list ke pehle paanch roop institutional power ke baare mein hain: police officer, public servant, armed forces ka member, jail ya custody ka staff, ya hospital staff ka kiya rape. List aage relatives, guardians, teachers aur har us insaan tak jaati hai jo aurat ke prati "a position of trust or authority", yaani bharose ya adhikaar ki position mein ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Saboot ke niyam bhi badal jaate hain. In aggravated cases mein, jab intercourse saabit ho jaaye aur aurat court mein kahe ki usne consent nahi diya, toh Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ke Section 120 ke tahat court "shall presume that she did not consent", yaani court maan kar chalega ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Jiske haath mein chaabiyaan thi, use hi yeh galat saabit karna hoga.

## Section 68: jab 'haan' power ke zor par nikalwaya jaaye

Power ka kuch abuse zabardasti jaisa dikhta hi nahi. BNS ka Section 68 us insaan ko saza deta hai jo authority mein hai, public servant hai, ya jail, institution ya hospital ka staff hai, aur apni position ka galat istemaal karke apni custody ya dekhrekh mein rehne wali aurat ko apne saath sex ke liye raazi karta hai, chahe woh rape ki had tak na pahunche. Saza hai 5 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Ek situation sochiye. Ek 19 saal ki ladki ek sarkari women's shelter mein rehti hai. Superintendent hi uske release ke papers sign karta hai, tay karta hai ki usse kaun mil sakta hai, aur woh reports likhta hai jo court padhega. Woh ishaara karta hai ki kaam jaldi ho sakta hai. Agar ladki maan jaati hai, toh law ise do baraabar logon ka faisla nahi, balki uska crime maanta hai: jo insaan aapki aazaadi control karta hai, use di gayi "haan" aazaad haan nahi hoti.

## Record kya dekhta hai, aur kise chhod deta hai

2024 mein India mein darj 29,536 rape cases mein se, uniform wale ya zimmedaari sambhaalne wale logon ke clauses ke tahat police ne yeh case darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Aaropi | Rape case, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Police personnel | 27 |
| Doosre public servants | 15 |
| Armed forces ke members | 2 |
| Jail, remand home ya custody ki jagah ka staff | 3 |
| Hospital staff | 8 |

Koi case in rows mein tabhi aata hai jab police woh clause lagaye, aur faisla lene wale officer aaropi ke saathi bhi ho sakte hain. Zyadatar survivors yahan tak pahunchte hi nahi: NFHS-5 mein, physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% aurton ne na kabhi madad maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha, aur jinhone madad maangi unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jab abuser khud policewala ho, toh yeh patla sa raasta bhi usi ki force se hokar guzarta hai. Yeh numbers sirf ek floor hain, yaani kam se kam itne.

Kuch survivors toh design se hi gaayab hain. BNS ka Section 63 rape ko "a man", yaani aadmi, ka "a woman", yaani aurat, ke khilaaf kiya gaya kaam batata hai, aur Section 68 bhi sirf aurton ko bachata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. BNS ne purane penal code ka Section 377 hata diya, jo aadmiyon ke khilaaf bina consent ke sex ko bhi cover karta tha, aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Matlab, lock-up mein police officer ke haathon sexual assault jhelne wale adult aadmi ke paas file karne ke liye koi rape offence hi nahi hai. Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne 10 November 2023 ko is gap ki warning di thi; sarkar ne uski salaah nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Kisi transgender insaan ke sexual abuse par sirf chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Custodial abuse report kyun nahi hota

Authority wale kisi insaan ke abuse ko report karne ka matlab hai usi ki institution se uske khilaaf action ki ummeed karna. Teen case dikhate hain ki iska kya matlab ho sakta hai.

- **Kathua, 2018.** 10 June 2019 ko Pathankot ki ek court ne aath saal ki ek bachchi ke rape aur murder ke trial mein saat mein se chhe logon ko convict kiya. Unmein teen policewale the, jinhe saboot mitaane ke liye paanch saal ki jail hui [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]].
- **Gujarat, 2002.** Dangon ke gang rape case mein, Mumbai ki ek special court ne 2008 mein ek police officer ko jaan-boojhkar FIR galat likhne ka doshi paaya; 2017 mein Bombay High Court ne un paanch police personnel aur do doctors ko bhi convict kiya jinhe trial court ne bari kar diya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].
- **Muzaffarpur, 2018.** Sarkari paise se chalne wale ek girls' shelter home ka abuse tab saamne aaya jab Tata Institute of Social Sciences ne state government ke liye Bihar ke children's homes ka audit kiya [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Audit ne 34 naabaalig ladkiyon ka sexual abuse ujagar kiya [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. January 2020 mein Delhi ki ek court ne 20 mein se 19 aaropiyon ko convict kiya [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Har case mein, jin logon ya institutions ka kaam crime ko record karna, saboot bachana ya bachchi ko panaah dena tha, wahi problem ka hissa nikle. Custodial survivors ke saamne yahi deewar hoti hai: FIR aur investigation, dono aaropi ke saathiyon ke haathon se guzarte hain.

Is deewar se bachne ke raaste hain. Survivor kisi bhi police station par report kar sakte hain, crime chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya complaint electronically bhejkar teen din ke andar sign kar sakte hain, aur unhe FIR ki free copy milni hi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
