Kisi aurat ki rape complaint woman officer hi record karegi, aur uska statement uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par liya jaana hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape ki FIR na likhne wale officer ko chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

1983 ka law isliye bana kyunki ek court ne kabhi police station mein ek ladki ki chuppi ko consent maan liya tha. Aaj us law ka asli test yeh hai ki jis insaan ka abuse kisi uniform wale ne kiya ho, woh doosre station mein jaaye, toh kya uski baat par yakeen kiya jaayega.

dalit-adivasi-rape-cases-ncrb-floor.en:
Every day in 2024, police in India registered about 12 rape cases in which the victim was Dalit: 4,262 in the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read that number as a floor, not a measure. A rape enters India's caste statistics only when police write one particular law into the FIR, and nobody counts the cases where they don't.

## 4,262 cases, about 12 a day

The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) uses the legal terms Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST); we also use Dalit and Adivasi. Police registered 55,698 crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2024, a rate of 27.7 per lakh SC population, and rape made up 7.6% of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A year earlier, the count was 4,214 rape cases with 4,261 victims [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

Four states registered the most such cases in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]:

| State | Rape cases with SC victims, 2023 |
|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | 645 |
| Rajasthan | 630 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 560 |
| Maharashtra | 504 |
| All India | 4,214 |

Rajasthan's rate, 5.2 cases per lakh SC population, was more than twice the national 2.1 [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. NCRB itself warns that more crime registered in a place does not make it more unsafe [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A high figure can mean more crime, or police who register more of it.

## Adivasi victims, Dalit children

For Scheduled Tribes, rape takes up an even bigger share of the record. Police registered 1,268 rape cases with Adivasi victims in 2024, 12.7% of the 9,966 crimes against Scheduled Tribes, against 7.6% for Scheduled Castes [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Many of the victims are children. In 2023, 1,379 of the 4,214 rape cases with Dalit victims involved children under 18, about one in three [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. NCRB counts them under POCSO, which covers children of every gender. These are POCSO cases in which police also invoked the Atrocities Act, which, by NCRB's definition, means the accused was not from a Scheduled Caste or Tribe. Each one is a child whose case names an accused from outside those communities.

## The counting rule that hides cases

NCRB counts a crime as an atrocity against a Scheduled Caste person only when police invoke the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Cases registered only under the general penal code are left out, on the assumption that they were committed by SC or ST persons [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

That rule hides two kinds of cases. A rape of a Dalit woman by a Dalit man is not counted there at all. And a rape by a dominant-caste man drops out of it whenever police leave the Act out of the FIR, whether by mistake, ignorance or choice.

Imagine a 16-year-old Dalit girl in a village in Madhya Pradesh, assaulted by the son of the family whose fields her parents work. At the police station, the officer registers rape under POCSO but not the Atrocities Act. She will appear in India's child-abuse count. She will not appear in its caste statistics, and her case loses protections written for atrocities: trial in an Exclusive Special Court, and the state's duty to protect victims and witnesses from intimidation and to tell the family about every hearing, including bail [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

The law anticipates this failure. Under Section 4 of the Act, as amended in 2015, a public servant who is not SC or ST and wilfully neglects his duties, including registering the FIR under the correct sections and filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Beneath the floor is a wider silence. In NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The caste tables begin only after a survivor has broken that silence, reached a police station and been written down correctly.

## From FIR to verdict

Registration is the first gate, not the last. In 2023 police filed charge sheets in 88.1% of the rape cases with Dalit victims that they disposed of [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Courts that year convicted in 508 such cases and acquitted in 1,073, a conviction rate of 30.5%, and 20,622 cases, 92.3% of those awaiting trial, were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

The 2015 amendment asks Exclusive Special Courts to hear atrocity trials day to day and, as far as possible, to finish them within two months of the charge sheet [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. With 92.3% pending, that deadline exists mostly on paper. An acquittal does not prove a complaint was false. Delay gives pressure time to work on survivors and witnesses, which is exactly what the Act's protection duty is meant to stop.

## Where caste and sexual violence meet

The Supreme Court has named the pattern. Its 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that dominant-caste men would not want sex with women from oppressed castes, so their complaints must be false. "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies," it says [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The handbook also recalls where that stereotype once led. In 1995 a Rajasthan trial court acquitted the dominant-caste men accused of the 1992 gang rape of a government social worker from an oppressed caste, reasoning partly that dominant-caste men would not rape an oppressed-caste woman [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Even a case the whole country followed can end far from a rape conviction. In the 2020 Hathras case, in which a 19-year-old Dalit woman died, a special SC/ST court in March 2023 acquitted three of the four accused and found none guilty of gang rape or murder; one was convicted of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and of offences under the Atrocities Act [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

So read 4,262 for what it is: the cases that got through a police station door with the right law attached. Every survivor who never reached the station, and every FIR written without the Act, sits beneath it. Survivors can also seek compensation from the District Legal Services Authority, even if the offender is never traced or tried [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice. If you are helping a survivor, read the FIR before you leave the station.
dalit-adivasi-rape-cases-ncrb-floor.hg:
2024 mein har din, India mein police ne qareeb 12 aise rape case darj kiye jinmein victim Dalit the: poore saal mein 4,262 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is number ko poora hisaab nahi, ek floor samajhiye. Koi rape India ke caste statistics mein tabhi aata hai jab police FIR mein ek khaas law likhe, aur jin cases mein woh nahi likhti, unhe koi nahi ginta.

## 4,262 case, yaani roz qareeb 12

National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) legal terms Scheduled Castes (SC) aur Scheduled Tribes (ST) ka istemaal karta hai; hum Dalit aur Adivasi bhi likhte hain. 2024 mein police ne Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf 55,698 crime darj kiye, yaani har lakh SC aabadi par 27.7, aur inmein 7.6% rape the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek saal pehle yeh ginti 4,214 rape case aur 4,261 victims ki thi [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

2023 mein sabse zyada aise case in chaar states mein darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]:

| State | SC victims wale rape case, 2023 |
|---|---|
| Uttar Pradesh | 645 |
| Rajasthan | 630 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 560 |
| Maharashtra | 504 |
| Poora India | 4,214 |

Rajasthan ka rate, har lakh SC aabadi par 5.2 case, national rate 2.1 ke dugne se bhi zyada tha [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. NCRB khud warn karta hai ki kisi jagah zyada crime darj hone se woh jagah zyada unsafe nahi ho jaati [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Bada number zyada crime ka sign bhi ho sakta hai, aur aisi police ka bhi jo zyada case darj karti hai.

## Adivasi victims, Dalit bachche

Scheduled Tribes ke record mein rape ka hissa aur bhi bada hai. 2024 mein police ne Adivasi victims wale 1,268 rape case darj kiye, jo Scheduled Tribes ke khilaaf darj 9,966 crimes ka 12.7% hai, jabki Scheduled Castes ke liye yeh hissa 7.6% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Victims mein bahut saare bachche hain. 2023 mein Dalit victims wale 4,214 rape cases mein se 1,379 mein victim 18 saal se kam umar ke bachche the, yaani qareeb har teesra case [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. NCRB inhe POCSO ke tahat ginta hai, jo har gender ke bachchon ko cover karta hai. Yeh POCSO ke woh case hain jinmein police ne Atrocities Act bhi lagaya, aur NCRB ki definition ke hisaab se iska matlab hai ki aaropi kisi Scheduled Caste ya Tribe se nahi tha. Har case mein ek bachcha hai, aur aaropi in communities ke bahar ka hai.

## Ginti ka woh niyam jo case chhupa deta hai

NCRB kisi Scheduled Caste insaan ke khilaaf crime ko atrocity tabhi ginta hai jab police SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act lagaye. Jo case sirf general penal code ke tahat darj hote hain, unhe yeh maan kar bahar rakha jaata hai ki woh SC ya ST logon ne kiye honge [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

Is niyam se do tarah ke case chhup jaate hain. Kisi Dalit aadmi ke haathon Dalit aurat ka rape wahan gina hi nahi jaata. Aur dominant caste ke kisi aadmi ka kiya rape bhi us table se bahar ho jaata hai jab police FIR mein Act chhod deti hai, chahe galti se, jaankari ki kami se, ya jaan-boojhkar.

Sochiye, Madhya Pradesh ke ek gaon mein ek 16 saal ki Dalit ladki hai, jis par us parivaar ke bete ne hamla kiya jiske kheton mein uske maa-baap kaam karte hain. Police station mein officer POCSO ke tahat rape darj karta hai, lekin Atrocities Act nahi lagata. Woh ladki India ke child-abuse count mein dikhegi. Caste statistics mein nahi dikhegi, aur uska case un protections se bhi haath dho baithega jo atrocities ke liye likhi gayi hain: Exclusive Special Court mein trial, aur state ki yeh zimmedaari ki woh victims aur gawaahon ko dhamkiyon se bachaye aur parivaar ko har hearing, bail ki hearing samet, ki jaankari de [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Law ko is failure ka andaaza pehle se tha. 2015 mein badle gaye Act ke Section 4 ke tahat, jo public servant SC ya ST nahi hai aur jaan-boojhkar apni duties mein laaparwaahi karta hai, jaise FIR sahi sections mein darj karna aur 60 din ke andar charge sheet file karna, use chhe mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Is floor ke neeche ek aur badi chuppi hai. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% aurton ne na kabhi madad maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Caste tables ki ginti tab shuru hoti hai jab koi survivor yeh chuppi tode, police station tak pahunche, aur uska case sahi tarah likha jaaye.

## FIR se faisle tak

Case darj hona pehla darwaaza hai, aakhri nahi. 2023 mein police ne Dalit victims wale jin rape cases ko nipataya, unmein se 88.1% mein charge sheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Usi saal courts ne aise 508 cases mein conviction diya aur 1,073 mein aaropiyon ko bari kiya, yaani conviction rate 30.5% raha, aur saal ke ant mein 20,622 case, yaani trial ka intezaar kar rahe 92.3% case, abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

2015 ka amendment Exclusive Special Courts se kehta hai ki atrocity trials roz sune jaayein aur jahan tak ho sake, charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hon [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Jab 92.3% case pending hon, toh yeh deadline zyadatar kaagaz par hi hai. Bari hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki complaint jhoothi thi. Deri survivors aur gawaahon par dabaav ko kaam karne ka waqt deti hai, aur Act ki protection wali zimmedaari theek isi ko rokne ke liye hai.

## Jahan caste aur sexual violence milte hain

Supreme Court ne is pattern ko naam diya hai. Gender stereotypes par uski 2023 ki handbook is soch ko khaarij karti hai ki dominant caste ke aadmi oppressed caste ki aurton ke saath sex chahenge hi nahi, isliye unki complaints jhoothi hongi. Handbook kehti hai: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne itihaas mein sexual violence ko caste hierarchy mazboot karne aur barkaraar rakhne ke hathiyaar ki tarah istemaal kiya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Handbook yeh bhi yaad dilaati hai ki yeh stereotype ek baar kahan tak le gaya tha. 1995 mein Rajasthan ki ek trial court ne 1992 mein oppressed caste ki ek sarkari social worker ke gang rape ke aaropi dominant caste ke aadmiyon ko bari kar diya, aur ek wajah yeh di ki dominant caste ke aadmi oppressed caste ki aurat ka rape nahi karenge [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Jis case par poora desh nazar rakhe hue tha, woh bhi rape conviction se door khatam ho sakta hai. 2020 ke Hathras case mein, jismein ek 19 saal ki Dalit aurat ki maut hui, March 2023 mein ek special SC/ST court ne chaar mein se teen aaropiyon ko bari kiya aur kisi ko bhi gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya; ek ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder aur Atrocities Act ke offences mein convict kiya gaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Toh 4,262 ko waisa hi padhiye jaisa woh hai: woh case jo sahi law ke saath police station ka darwaaza paar kar paaye. Har woh survivor jo station tak kabhi pahunch hi nahi paaya, aur har woh FIR jo Act ke bina likhi gayi, is number ke neeche hai. Survivors District Legal Services Authority se compensation bhi maang sakte hain, chahe offender kabhi na mile ya uska trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aap kisi survivor ki madad kar rahe hain, toh station se nikalne se pehle FIR padhiye.

dalit-survivors-rape-trials-courts.en:
In 2023, Indian courts convicted the accused in 508 rape cases in which the victim was a Scheduled Caste (Dalit) woman or girl, and acquitted in 1,073. Another 20,622 such cases, 92.3% of all those before the courts, were still waiting for a verdict when the year ended [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. In 2015, Parliament had amended the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act to promise these survivors something better: a charge sheet within 60 days, special courts sitting day after day, and trials finished, as far as possible, within two months [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## 508 convictions, 1,073 acquittals

Another 86 cases ended in discharge. Counting all three outcomes, the conviction rate was 30.5%: more than two acquittals for every conviction [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

The uncomfortable part: that rate is not worse than the national one. Across all rape trials completed in India in 2023, courts convicted in 22.7% [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. In these figures, Dalit survivors' cases that reach a verdict do not end in acquittal more often than rape cases overall. The failure shows when you measure against the law's own promise of faster, safer trials. By that measure, almost every case is behind schedule.

An acquittal means the prosecution did not prove its charge. It does not mean the complaint was false.

## Charge-sheeted, then stuck

On paper, the police stage mostly works. In 2023 police filed charge sheets in 88.1% of the rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims whose investigation they completed that year, against 81.2% for all crimes against Scheduled Castes [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

Then the cases stop moving. Police registered 4,214 new rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims in 2023, 1,379 of them involving children under 18 [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Courts completed fewer than half as many trials. At 2023's pace, even if no new case arrived, clearing the 20,622 pending cases would take more than a decade.

Imagine a 20-year-old Dalit woman in an Uttar Pradesh village who reports a rape in 2023. Odds are the police file a charge sheet. Then she waits for years. Each hearing costs her a day's wages and a bus fare to the district court, and the man she accused may be back in the village on bail.

Her case also competes for court time with every other atrocity case: at the end of 2023, 3,11,986 cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes were pending trial, 93.8% of all such cases before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

## What the 2015 amendment promised

The amendment wrote deadlines and duties into the law [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Police:** a non-SC/ST public servant who wilfully neglects duties under the Act, including registering the FIR under the correct sections and filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison.
- **Courts:** states must set up Exclusive Special Courts, and enough of them. Trials are to run day to day and finish, as far as possible, within two months of the charge sheet.
- **Survivors and witnesses:** under Section 15A, the state must protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement and violence. Victims have the right to timely notice of every court proceeding, including bail hearings.
- **Consent:** for the Act's offence of sexual touching, consent means "an unequivocal voluntary agreement"; not physically resisting is not, by itself, consent.

This is general information, not legal advice.

## Hathras: a verdict without a rape conviction

The best-known test of these promises is the Hathras case. A 19-year-old Dalit woman was assaulted on 14 September 2020 and died on 29 September; police cremated her in the middle of the night without her family's consent. In December 2020 the CBI charged four men with rape, gang rape, murder and SC/ST Act offences [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

The law's target: a trial within two months of the charge sheet. The verdict came on 2 March 2023. A special SC/ST court acquitted three of the four accused and convicted one of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and of SC/ST Act offences. None was found guilty of gang rape or murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

This case had what most never get: national attention, a CBI investigation, a special court. It still took more than two years from the charge sheet, and ended without a rape conviction. If the system moves this way while the whole country is watching, consider the 20,622 cases no camera follows.

## Where the promises break

Delay is the first break, and it feeds the others. Every year of waiting gives more time for the intimidation, coercion and inducement that Section 15A was written to stop [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. NCRB's tables do not say why the 1,073 acquittals happened, whether through weak investigation, hostile witnesses, faded evidence or charges simply not proved.

Prejudice is the second. In 2023 the Supreme Court's handbook for judges had to name, as a stereotype, the belief that dominant-caste men would not have sex with women from oppressed castes, so their complaints must be false. It recalled a 1995 Rajasthan trial court that acquitted dominant-caste men accused of the 1992 gang rape of a government social worker from an oppressed caste, reasoning partly in exactly that way. "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies," the handbook says [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The third break is invisibility. NCRB counts a case as a crime against a Scheduled Caste person only when police invoke the SC/ST Act; if they leave it out, the case vanishes from these tables [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Every count here is a floor.

One right does not wait for the courts. Under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a survivor can apply for compensation directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
dalit-survivors-rape-trials-courts.hg:
2023 mein Indian courts ne 508 aise rape cases mein accused ko sazaa di jinmein victim Scheduled Caste (Dalit) aurat ya ladki thi, aur 1,073 cases mein accused bari ho gaye. Aise 20,622 aur cases, yaani courts ke saamne maujood aise sabhi cases ka 92.3%, saal khatam hone tak faisle ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. 2015 mein Parliament ne SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act mein badlaav karke in survivors se behtar insaaf ka vaada kiya tha: 60 din ke andar charge sheet, roz sunwaai karne wali special courts, aur jahan tak mumkin ho, do mahine mein poora trial [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## 508 sazaayein, 1,073 bari

Iske alawa 86 cases discharge ke saath khatam hue. Teenon nateejon ko milakar conviction rate 30.5% raha: har ek sazaa ke mukaable do se zyada cases mein accused bari hue [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

Ab ek uncomfortable baat: yeh rate national rate se bura nahi hai. 2023 mein India mein poore hue sabhi rape trials mein courts ne 22.7% mein sazaa sunayi [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Yaani in aankdon mein, faisle tak pahunchne wale Dalit survivors ke cases baaki rape cases ke mukaable zyada baar acquittal par khatam nahi hote. Asli nakaami tab dikhti hai jab inhe kaanoon ke apne vaade se naapa jaaye, yaani tez aur surakshit trials ke vaade se. Us paimaane par lagbhag har case apne samay se peeche chal raha hai.

Acquittal ka matlab hai ki prosecution apna charge saabit nahi kar paaya. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki complaint jhoothi thi.

## Charge sheet file hui, phir case atak gaya

Kaagaz par police ka stage zyada tar kaam karta hai. 2023 mein Scheduled Caste victims wale jin rape cases ki jaanch police ne us saal poori ki, unmein se 88.1% mein charge sheet file hui, jabki Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf sabhi crimes mein yeh rate 81.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

Phir cases ruk jaate hain. 2023 mein police ne Scheduled Caste victims wale 4,214 naye rape cases darj kiye, jinmein se 1,379 mein victim 18 saal se kam umr ke bachche the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Courts ne isse aadhe se bhi kam trials poore kiye. 2023 ki raftaar se, agar ek bhi naya case na aaye tab bhi, 20,622 pending cases nipataane mein das saal se zyada lag jaayenge.

Sochiye, Uttar Pradesh ke ek gaon ki 20 saal ki ek Dalit aurat 2023 mein rape ki report karti hai. Zyada sambhavna yahi hai ki police charge sheet file kar degi. Phir woh saalon intezaar karti hai. Har hearing par uski ek din ki dihaadi aur district court tak ka bus ka kiraya jaata hai, aur jis aadmi par usne ilzaam lagaya, woh shayad bail par gaon mein wapas ghoom raha ho.

Uske case ko court ke samay ke liye baaki sabhi atrocity cases se bhi hod karni padti hai: 2023 ke aakhir mein Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf crimes ke 3,11,986 cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, yaani courts ke saamne aise sabhi cases ka 93.8% [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

## 2015 ke amendment ne kya vaada kiya tha

Amendment ne kaanoon mein deadlines aur zimmedaariyan likh deen [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Police:** jo non-SC/ST public servant is Act ke tahat apni duties mein jaanbujhkar laaparwahi kare, jaise sahi sections ke saath FIR darj na karna ya 60 din ke andar charge sheet file na karna, use chhah mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai.
- **Courts:** states ko Exclusive Special Courts banani hain, aur utni sankhya mein jitni zaroori ho. Trial roz chalna chahiye aur jahan tak mumkin ho, charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye.
- **Survivors aur gawaah:** Section 15A ke tahat state ko victims, unke dependants aur gawaahon ko dhamki, zabardasti, laalach aur hinsa se bachana hai. Victims ko bail hearings samet har court proceeding ki samay par jaankari paane ka haq hai.
- **Consent:** is Act ke sexual touching wale offence ke liye consent ka matlab hai "an unequivocal voluntary agreement", yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi sehmati; physically virodh na karna apne aap mein consent nahi hai.

Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Hathras: faisla aaya, par rape ki sazaa nahi

In vaadon ki sabse jaani-maani pareeksha Hathras case hai. Ek 19 saal ki Dalit ladki par 14 September 2020 ko hamla hua aur 29 September ko uski maut ho gayi; police ne uski family ki marzi ke bina aadhi raat ko uska antim sanskar kar diya. December 2020 mein CBI ne chaar aadmiyon par rape, gang rape, murder aur SC/ST Act ke offences ke charge lagaye [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Kaanoon ka target tha: charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar trial. Faisla 2 March 2023 ko aaya. Ek special SC/ST court ne chaar mein se teen accused ko bari kar diya, aur ek ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder, yaani gair-iraadatan hatya, aur SC/ST Act ke offences ka doshi maana. Kisi ko bhi gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya gaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Is case ke paas woh sab tha jo zyada tar cases ko kabhi nahi milta: poore desh ka dhyaan, CBI ki jaanch, ek special court. Phir bhi charge sheet ke baad do saal se zyada lage, aur ant mein rape ki koi sazaa nahi hui. Agar poora desh dekh raha ho tab bhi system aise chalta hai, toh un 20,622 cases ke baare mein sochiye jinke peeche koi camera nahi hai.

## Vaade kahan tootte hain

Pehli daraar deri hai, aur yahi baaki daraaron ko badhati hai. Intezaar ka har saal us dhamki, zabardasti aur laalach ko aur waqt deta hai jise rokne ke liye Section 15A likha gaya tha [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. NCRB ki tables yeh nahi batatin ki woh 1,073 acquittals kyun hue: kamzor jaanch ki wajah se, gawaahon ke mukar jaane se, mit chuke saboot se, ya isliye ki charge bas saabit nahi hua.

Doosri daraar prejudice hai, yaani pehle se bani soch. 2023 mein Supreme Court ki judges ke liye handbook ko saaf likhna pada ki yeh ek stereotype hai ki dominant-caste aadmi oppressed castes ki auraton ke saath sex nahi karenge, isliye unki complaints jhoothi hongi. Handbook ne 1995 ke Rajasthan ke us trial court ko yaad kiya jisne oppressed caste ki ek government social worker ke 1992 ke gang rape ke accused dominant-caste aadmiyon ko bari kar diya tha, aur jiski reasoning kuch hadd tak yahi thi. Handbook kehti hai: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne itihaas mein caste ki oonch-neech banaye rakhne ke liye sexual violence ko hathiyaar ki tarah istemaal kiya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Teesri daraar yeh hai ki kai cases dikhte hi nahi. NCRB kisi case ko Scheduled Caste vyakti ke khilaaf crime tabhi ginta hai jab police SC/ST Act lagaye; agar police Act chhod de, toh woh case in tables se gaayab ho jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Isliye yahan ki har ginti ek nichli seema hai: asli sankhya isse zyada hi hogi.

Ek haq court ka intezaar nahi karta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 396 ke tahat survivor seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein compensation ke liye apply kar sakti hai, tab bhi jab koi trial na ho, aur authority ko do mahine ke andar apni jaanch poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

delhi-mumbai-crimes-against-women-compar.en:
Police in Delhi registered 13,396 crimes against women in 2024. Police in Mumbai registered 6,358 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. On rape the gap is wider: 1,058 cases in Delhi, 411 in Mumbai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yet in the 2011 Census figures that NCRB uses for cities, Mumbai had more women than Delhi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So is Delhi the most dangerous city in India for women, or the city where crimes against women are most often written down? The honest answer is that the data cannot say, and this piece shows exactly where they run out.

## Two cities, two very different tables

Here are the two cities side by side, from NCRB's 2024 tables for India's 19 largest cities [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| 2024 | Delhi | Mumbai |
|---|---|---|
| Crimes against women | 13,396 | 6,358 |
| Rape cases | 1,058 | 411 |
| POCSO cases, girl victims | 1,489 | 1,331 |

Delhi alone accounted for 26.5% of all crimes against women and 27.2% of all rape cases registered in the 19 cities. Mumbai was second on crimes against women and third on rape, after Delhi and Jaipur [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Over three years the two cities moved in opposite directions on rape. Delhi's count fell from 1,204 in 2022 to 1,088 in 2023 and 1,058 in 2024; Mumbai's rose from 370 to 387 to 411 [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even so, Delhi's 2024 figure was more than two and a half times Mumbai's.

One row breaks the pattern. For POCSO cases with girl victims, the cities were close: 1,489 in Delhi and 1,331 in Mumbai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Under the POCSO Act, anyone who knows or suspects that a child has been sexually abused must report it to the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], so these cases depend less on one person's decision to walk into a station. That may be part of why the gap narrows here. It is a clue, not proof.

## Delhi on top, two years running

Delhi's lead is not only about size. Among all states and Union Territories, it had the highest rate of registered crime against women in 2024, 130.7 per lakh women, just ahead of Telangana at 128.6; Maharashtra, Mumbai's state, stood at 78.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Delhi was top in 2023 as well, at 133.6 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Its rape rate, 10.3 per lakh women, was the highest of any large-population state or UT except Rajasthan, and its rate of cruelty by husbands or relatives, 45.3, was second only to Telangana's [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The total has been steady rather than spiking: 14,247 cases in 2022, 13,439 in 2023 and 13,396 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This is not a one-year blip. For two years running, Delhi has registered crimes against women at a higher rate than any state or UT.

## One city, two rates

Here is the trap. In NCRB's 2024 tables Delhi appears twice. As a Union Territory, its 13,396 cases give a rate of 130.7 per lakh women. As a metropolitan city, the same 13,396 cases give 176.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB notes that Delhi UT covers both Delhi City and rural Delhi [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]; in 2024 the two totals were identical.

Nothing about the crimes differs. Only the denominator does. The UT rate divides by NCRB's projection of Delhi's female population in 2024. The city rate divides by the much smaller 2011 Census figure, because NCRB has no population projections for cities, and it states that city and state rates are therefore not comparable [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Two consequences follow. Every city rate in NCRB's tables is calculated as if the city's population had not changed since 2011, which overstates the rate wherever the population has grown [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And the claim that Mumbai has more women than Delhi rests on the same 2011 count: NCRB's 2024 projection puts Delhi UT's female population well above its 2011 count, and there is no comparable projection for Mumbai. The fair comparison is the one inside the same table, on the same 2011 base, where Delhi's rate is 176.8 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Delhi registered more than twice Mumbai's cases from a smaller 2011 female population, so even on that footing its rate is more than twice Mumbai's.

## Danger or documentation?

Three things are true at once.

Delhi registers crimes against women at a rate no state or UT matched in 2023 or 2024. Behind that are thousands of women each year who reached a police station and got a case registered.

Registration is not the same as crime. NCRB warns that more crime registered in a city is "not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", and that higher numbers can follow citizen-centric steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A city where it is easier for women to complain will look worse in these tables than one where it is harder.

Police data see only a sliver of violence in either city. Nationally, only 14% of women who had experienced physical or sexual violence had ever sought help, and of those who did, only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Those survey figures are national, not city-level, but they suggest that both 13,396 and 6,358 capture only a small part of the violence women face.

What the data cannot do is separate these effects. Delhi may be more dangerous, more willing to record, or both. Mumbai may be safer, or quieter. The near-equal POCSO counts suggest the gap is not the same for every crime, but a suggestion is not an answer.

The practical conclusion is narrower. A woman in either city has the same legal right to have her complaint registered at any police station, wherever the crime happened, or to send it electronically [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice. Both cities' numbers depend on how many women use that right, and on how many officers honour it.
delhi-mumbai-crimes-against-women-compar.hg:
2024 mein Delhi police ne 13,396 crimes against women register kiye. Mumbai police ne 6,358 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape mein yeh gap aur bhi bada hai: Delhi mein 1,058 cases, Mumbai mein 411 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi, NCRB shehron ke liye 2011 Census ke jo figures use karta hai, unme Mumbai mein Delhi se zyada auratein thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Toh kya Delhi India mein auraton ke liye sabse khatarnak shehar hai, ya woh shehar jahan auraton ke khilaaf crimes sabse zyada likhe jaate hain? Imaandaar jawab yeh hai ki data yeh nahi bata sakta, aur yeh piece dikhata hai ki data theek kahan jaakar khatam ho jaata hai.

## Do shehar, do bilkul alag tables

NCRB ki 2024 tables se, India ke 19 sabse bade shehron mein se in do shehron ka aamne-saamne hisaab [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| 2024 | Delhi | Mumbai |
|---|---|---|
| Crimes against women | 13,396 | 6,358 |
| Rape cases | 1,058 | 411 |
| POCSO cases, girl victims | 1,489 | 1,331 |

19 shehron mein register hue sabhi crimes against women ka 26.5% aur sabhi rape cases ka 27.2% akele Delhi mein tha. Crimes against women mein Mumbai doosre number par tha, aur rape mein Delhi aur Jaipur ke baad teesre par [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Teen saalon mein rape ke maamle mein dono shehar ulti dishaon mein chale. Delhi ki ginti 2022 mein 1,204 se ghatkar 2023 mein 1,088 aur 2024 mein 1,058 par aayi; Mumbai ki ginti 370 se 387 aur phir 411 tak badhi [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi, 2024 mein Delhi ka figure Mumbai ke dhaai guna se bhi zyada tha.

Ek row is pattern ko todti hai. Girl victims wale POCSO cases mein dono shehar kareeb the: Delhi mein 1,489 aur Mumbai mein 1,331 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO Act ke under jo bhi jaanta hai ya shaq karta hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse hua hai, use police ko report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Isliye yeh cases is baat par kam tikte hain ki koi ek insaan khud police station jaane ka faisla kare. Ho sakta hai yahan gap kam hone ki ek wajah yahi ho. Yeh ek clue hai, saboot nahi.

## Delhi sabse upar, lagaataar do saal

Delhi ki badhat sirf size ki wajah se nahi hai. 2024 mein sabhi states aur Union Territories mein registered crime against women ka sabse zyada rate Delhi ka tha, 130.7 per lakh women, Telangana ke 128.6 se thoda aage; Mumbai ka state Maharashtra 78.3 par tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 mein bhi Delhi top par tha, 133.6 ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Uska rape rate, 10.3 per lakh women, Rajasthan ko chhod kar kisi bhi badi aabaadi wale state ya UT se zyada tha, aur pati ya rishtedaron ki cruelty ka uska rate, 45.3, sirf Telangana se peechhe tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kul ginti mein uchhaal nahi, thahraav dikhta hai: 2022 mein 14,247 cases, 2023 mein 13,439 aur 2024 mein 13,396 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh koi ek saal ki baat nahi hai. Lagaataar do saal se Delhi kisi bhi state ya UT se zyada rate par crimes against women register kar raha hai.

## Ek shehar, do rates

Yahan ek jaal hai. NCRB ki 2024 tables mein Delhi do baar aata hai. Union Territory ke roop mein uske 13,396 cases 130.7 per lakh women ka rate dete hain. Metropolitan city ke roop mein wahi 13,396 cases 176.8 dete hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB batata hai ki Delhi UT mein Delhi City aur rural Delhi dono shaamil hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]; 2024 mein dono ke totals bilkul ek jaise the.

Crimes mein koi fark nahi hai. Fark sirf denominator ka hai. UT rate ko NCRB ki 2024 ki Delhi female population ki projection se divide kiya jaata hai. City rate ko 2011 Census ke kahin chhote figure se divide kiya jaata hai, kyunki NCRB ke paas shehron ki population projections nahi hain, aur NCRB khud kehta hai ki isliye city aur state rates comparable nahi hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iske do nateeje hain. NCRB ki tables mein har city rate aise nikaala jaata hai jaise 2011 ke baad shehar ki aabaadi badli hi na ho, isliye jahan bhi aabaadi badhi hai, wahan rate zyada dikhta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur yeh daawa ki Mumbai mein Delhi se zyada auratein hain, usi 2011 ki ginti par tika hai: NCRB ki 2024 projection Delhi UT ki female population ko uski 2011 ki ginti se kaafi upar rakhti hai, aur Mumbai ke liye aisi koi projection nahi hai. Sahi comparison wahi hai jo ek hi table ke andar, ek hi 2011 base par ho, jahan Delhi ka rate 176.8 per lakh women hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Delhi ne 2011 ki chhoti female population ke bawajood Mumbai se do guna se zyada cases register kiye, isliye is hisaab se bhi uska rate Mumbai ke rate se do guna se zyada hai.

## Khatra ya record-keeping?

Teen baatein ek saath sach hain.

Delhi jis rate par crimes against women register karta hai, 2023 ya 2024 mein koi bhi state ya UT us tak nahi pahuncha. Iske peechhe har saal hazaaron auratein hain jo police station tak pahunchi aur jinka case register hua.

Registration aur crime ek cheez nahi hain. NCRB warn karta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada registered crime "not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" hai, aur zyada numbers e-FIR facility ya women help desks jaise citizen-centric kadmon ke baad bhi aa sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Jis shehar mein auraton ke liye complaint karna aasaan hai, woh in tables mein us shehar se bura dikhega jahan complaint karna mushkil hai.

Police data dono shehron mein hinsa ka bas ek chhota sa hissa dekh paata hai. Poore desh mein, physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki auraton mein se sirf 14% ne kabhi madad maangi thi, aur jinhone maangi, unme se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh survey figures national hain, city-level nahi, lekin yeh ishaara karte hain ki 13,396 aur 6,358, dono hi auraton par hone wali hinsa ka sirf ek chhota hissa pakadte hain.

Data in asar ko alag-alag nahi kar sakta. Ho sakta hai Delhi zyada khatarnak ho, ya record karne ko zyada tayyar ho, ya dono. Ho sakta hai Mumbai zyada safe ho, ya bas zyada chup. POCSO ki lagbhag barabar ginti ishaara karti hai ki gap har crime mein ek jaisa nahi hai, lekin ishaara jawab nahi hota.

Kaam ka nateeja isse chhota hai. Dono shehron mein aurat ka ek hi legal haq hai: woh kisi bhi police station mein complaint register karwa sakti hai, crime chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya use electronically bhej sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Dono shehron ke numbers is par depend karte hain ki kitni auratein is haq ka istemaal karti hain, aur kitne officers ise nibhaate hain.

disabled-survivors-rape-data-gap.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old Deaf woman in a district town. She uses sign language, and nobody at the local police station does. Her family speaks for her, and some of what she says never reaches the FIR. On paper, Indian law planned for this moment. In practice, the plan is often ignored, and the national crime data barely registers her.

## What the law promises

Raping a woman with a mental or physical disability is aggravated rape under Section 64(2)(k) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). It carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The procedure law goes further. Under Section 173(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police must record a disabled survivor's complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, and the recording must be videographed [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under Section 179, police cannot make her come anywhere other than where she lives, unless she chooses to. A magistrate must record her statement with the same help, on audio-video, preferably by mobile phone. Under Section 183(6), that statement counts as her main evidence at trial, so she does not have to repeat it, though the defence can still cross-examine her [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Little of this is new. The BNSS, in force since 1 July 2024, carried over disability protections first added to the old Criminal Procedure Code in 2013, so they were already law in every case Human Rights Watch later examined.

## 15 of 17: promises ignored

Human Rights Watch's (HRW) April 2018 report, "Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence", examined 17 rape and gang-rape cases involving eight girls and nine women with disabilities in eight states: Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand and West Bengal [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

In 15 of the 17 cases, the provisions meant to accommodate the survivor's disability were "simply not followed" by police and court officials, HRW wrote, even where severe, visible disabilities and injuries had been reported to police from the start [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. In 16 of the 17, survivors and their families did not know these protections existed, and the laws were often not available in formats they could use.

This is a small sample, not a national survey. But it shows the shape of the failure: a right nobody explains is a right nobody can claim.

## 144 of 29,536: a column that barely fills

Some cases do reach the aggravated charge. NCRB's section-wise rape table for 2024 shows 144 cases registered under the disability clause, out of 29,536 rape cases in India: 0.5% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 2021, under the old IPC clause, the figure was 117 [[ncrb-cii-2021]].

Four states, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, accounted for 86 of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| State | Rape cases, 2024 | Under the disability clause |
|---|---|---|
| Maharashtra | 3,091 | 32 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 3,061 | 19 |
| Tamil Nadu | 419 | 18 |
| Kerala | 940 | 17 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 3,209 | 3 |
| Bihar | 1,165 | 0 |

Nothing suggests disabled women in Uttar Pradesh or Bihar are safer than those in Tamil Nadu. The likelier reading is that police there rarely invoke the clause. Each case sits in one category only, so a rape filed under another one vanishes from this column [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The 144 is a floor, not a count of disabled women raped.

That count does not exist. Beyond this one column, NCRB does not record whether a crime victim is disabled, and in 2018 HRW found no disability breakdown in the National Family Health Survey either. Even the base number is contested: the 2011 Census counted 26.8 million disabled people, 2.21% of the population, against a WHO-World Bank global estimate of 15% [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. With no national figure, HRW cited a 2004 survey of 729 respondents in 12 districts of Odisha. It found that 25% of women with intellectual disabilities had been raped, and that nearly all the disabled women and girls surveyed had been beaten at home [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

## 56 cases under the disability law

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 has its own offences. Under Section 92(d), anyone in a position to dominate the will of a disabled woman or child who uses it to exploit her sexually faces six months to five years in prison [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. That can mean a carer, a guardian, a hostel warden or a teacher.

In 2024, the first year NCRB counted this law, police across India registered 56 cases under it, for all offences, not only sexual ones [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape itself is charged under the BNS, so 56 does not measure sexual violence. It measures how rarely the disability law reaches a police station.

Disbelief does the rest. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that able-bodied men do not want sex with disabled women, so their complaints must be false. Disability does not lower the risk, it says, and women whose disabilities affect communication are particularly vulnerable [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. And the law itself leaves men out. The BNS defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so a disabled adult man cannot legally be a rape victim; boys are covered by POCSO [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What families, carers and schools can do

Learn these rights before anyone needs them. Teach body safety in a form your child, student or relative understands (sign language, pictures, simple words), so she has the words to tell.

If something happens, call 112 and insist on what the BNSS promises: a complaint recorded where she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, on video, and a video statement before the magistrate. Take the free copy of the FIR and check that it records her disability [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape faces six months to two years in prison under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Compensation can be claimed from the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], and legal aid is free [[nalsa]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

If she becomes pregnant, our explainer on abortion law and disability covers her rights. Every case registered under the right section adds a line to a column India badly needs to fill.
disabled-survivors-rape-data-gap.hg:
Sochiye, kisi district ke chhote shehar mein 19 saal ki ek ladki hai jo sun nahi sakti. Woh sign language mein baat karti hai, par local police station mein koi sign language nahi jaanta. Uski taraf se family bolti hai, aur uski kahi kai baatein FIR tak pahunchti hi nahi. Kaagaz par Indian law ne theek is moment ke liye plan banaya hai. Asal mein yeh plan aksar ignore hota hai, aur national crime data mein woh mushkil se dikhti hai.

## Law kya vaada karta hai

Mental ya physical disability wali aurat ka rape, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64(2)(k) ke tahat aggravated rape hai. Iski saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, aur yeh life imprisonment tak ja sakti hai, yaani convict ki baaki poori zindagi jail mein [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Procedure wala law isse bhi aage jaata hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173(1) ke hisaab se, police ko disabled survivor ki complaint uske ghar par ya uski chuni jagah par record karni hogi. Saath mein interpreter ya special educator hoga, aur recording ka video banega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Section 179 ke tahat police use uske ghar ke alawa kahin aur aane ko majboor nahi kar sakti, jab tak woh khud na chahe. Magistrate bhi uska statement isi madad ke saath, audio-video par, ho sake toh mobile phone se record karega. Section 183(6) ke hisaab se yahi statement trial mein uski main gawahi maana jaayega. Yaani use sab kuch dobara nahi batana padega, haalaanki defence use cross-examine kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ismein zyada kuch naya nahi hai. BNSS 1 July 2024 se lagu hai, aur usne disability wale yeh protections purane Criminal Procedure Code se liye hain, jahan yeh 2013 mein jode gaye the. Yaani Human Rights Watch ne baad mein jin cases ki padtaal ki, un sabke waqt yeh protections law mein pehle se maujood the.

## 17 mein se 15: vaade toote

April 2018 mein Human Rights Watch (HRW) ki report "Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence" aayi. Ismein rape aur gang rape ke 17 cases ki padtaal thi, jo aath ladkiyon aur nau aurton ke the, sabko koi na koi disability thi. Yeh cases aath states se the: Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand aur West Bengal [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

17 mein se 15 cases mein police aur court officials ne woh provisions follow hi nahi kiye jo survivor ki disability ko dhyan mein rakh kar bane the. HRW ne likha ki yeh provisions "simply not followed" the, un cases mein bhi jahan disability aur chotein gambhir thi, saaf dikh rahi thi, aur police ko shuru se batayi gayi thi [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. 17 mein se 16 cases mein survivors aur unki families ko pata hi nahi tha ki law mein aise protections hain. Law ki jaankari bhi aksar aise format mein nahi thi jise woh padh ya samajh sakein.

Yeh chhota sample hai, national survey nahi. Lekin isse failure ki shakal saaf dikhti hai: jo haq kisi ko bataya hi na jaaye, use koi maang bhi nahi sakta.

## 29,536 mein se 144: ek column jo mushkil se bharta hai

Kuch cases aggravated charge tak pahunchte bhi hain. NCRB ki 2024 ki section-wise rape table mein disability wali dhara ke tahat 144 cases register hain, jabki us saal India mein rape ke kul 29,536 cases darj hue. Yaani sirf 0.5% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2021 mein, purane IPC clause ke tahat, yeh number 117 tha [[ncrb-cii-2021]].

Inmein se 86 cases sirf chaar states se aaye: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu aur Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| State | Rape cases, 2024 | Disability wali dhara mein |
|---|---|---|
| Maharashtra | 3,091 | 32 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 3,061 | 19 |
| Tamil Nadu | 419 | 18 |
| Kerala | 940 | 17 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 3,209 | 3 |
| Bihar | 1,165 | 0 |

Aisa maanne ki koi wajah nahi ki Uttar Pradesh ya Bihar mein disabled aurtein Tamil Nadu se zyada safe hain. Zyada mumkin yeh hai ki Uttar Pradesh aur Bihar ki police yeh dhara bahut kam lagati hai. Har case sirf ek category mein gina jaata hai, isliye jo rape kisi aur category mein file hua, woh is column se gaayab ho jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 144 ko sabse neeche ki limit samjhiye. Yeh is baat ki ginti nahi ki kitni disabled aurton ka rape hua.

Woh ginti kahin hai hi nahi. Is ek column ke alawa NCRB yeh record nahi karta ki crime ka victim disabled hai ya nahi, aur 2018 mein HRW ko National Family Health Survey (NFHS) mein bhi disability ke hisaab se koi data nahi mila. Disabled logon ki kul ginti par bhi sawal hai. 2011 ke Census ne 26.8 million logon ko disabled gina, yaani aabadi ka 2.21%, jabki WHO aur World Bank ka global estimate 15% hai [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Koi national figure na hone par HRW ne Odisha ke 2004 ke ek survey ka hawala diya, jo 12 districts mein 729 logon par hua tha. Usmein paaya gaya ki intellectual disability wali 25% aurton ka rape hua tha, aur survey mein shaamil lagbhag saari disabled aurton aur ladkiyon ko ghar par peeta gaya tha [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

## Disability law ke tahat 56 cases

Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 mein apne alag offences hain. Section 92(d) ke tahat, jo insaan kisi disabled aurat ya bachche par haavi ho aur is position ka fayda utha kar uska sexual exploitation kare, use chhe mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Aisa insaan caregiver, guardian, hostel warden ya teacher ho sakta hai.

2024 pehla saal tha jab NCRB ne is law ke cases gine, aur poore India mein police ne iske tahat sirf 56 cases register kiye. Ismein har tarah ke offences hain, sirf sexual nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape ka case toh BNS mein darj hota hai, isliye 56 ka number sexual violence ko nahi naapta. Yeh dikhata hai ki disability law police station tak kitna kam pahunchta hai.

Baaki kasar shaq poori kar deta hai. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook us soch ko galat batati hai ki bina disability wale mard disabled aurton ke saath sex nahi chahte, isliye unki complaints jhoothi hongi. Handbook kehti hai ki disability se khatra kam nahi hota, aur jin aurton ki disability baat-cheet par asar daalti hai, unhe khaas taur par zyada khatra hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Aur law khud mardon ko bahar rakhta hai. BNS ke hisaab se rape woh hai jo ek mard kisi aurat ke saath kare, isliye koi disabled adult mard legally rape victim nahi ho sakta; ladke POCSO ke tahat cover hote hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Families, caregivers aur schools kya kar sakte hain

Yeh rights zaroorat padne se pehle jaan lijiye. Apne bachche, student ya relative ko body safety usi tareeke se sikhaiye jo woh samajhte hain (sign language, pictures, simple words), taaki kuch ho toh uske paas batane ke liye shabd hon.

Agar kuch ho jaaye, toh 112 par call kijiye aur wahi maangiye jiska vaada BNSS karta hai: complaint uski chuni jagah par record ho, saath mein interpreter ya special educator ho, video bane, aur magistrate ke saamne statement bhi video par ho. FIR ki free copy lijiye aur check kijiye ki usmein uski disability likhi hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo police officer rape ki FIR record nahi karta, use BNS ke Section 199 ke tahat chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. State ya District Legal Services Authority se compensation maanga ja sakta hai, chahe offender kabhi trace na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], aur legal aid free hai [[nalsa]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Agar woh pregnant ho jaaye, toh abortion law aur disability par hamara explainer uske rights batata hai. Sahi section mein register hua har case us column mein ek line jodta hai, jise bharne ki India ko sakht zaroorat hai.

find-state-rape-data-ncrb-tables.en:
Imagine two forwards in your family WhatsApp group in the same week. One says Bihar is the safest state for women. The other says Maharashtra has the most rapes in India. Both can be checked in ten minutes, for free. Most rape figures quoted in India come from one annual report by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB). Here is where it lives, which tables matter, and how to read your state's line.

## Where the report lives

As of 20 November 2026, the latest edition of *Crime in India* is the 2024 report [[ncrb-website-cii-year-wise-2026]], released on 6 May 2026 [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]]. Of its three volumes, Volume I is the one you need: Chapter 3A covers crimes against women by state, 3B the big cities, and 4A crimes against children, including POCSO cases. The direct link: https://www.ncrb.gov.in/uploads/files/11CrimeinIndia2024-VolumeI.pdf

Know what you are holding. NCRB compiles what state and union territory police send, and its own disclaimer says it is not responsible for the authenticity of that information [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Its case counts are FIRs that police registered, not a measure of how much violence happened.

## Table by table: cases, ages, accused, police, courts

Five tables in Chapter 3A carry most of what you need.

- **Table 3A.2, cases and rates.** India registered 29,536 rape cases with 29,742 victims in 2024, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Because the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024, the count is split: 19,683 IPC cases plus 9,853 BNS cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.3, victims' ages.** Of the 29,742 victims, 792 were girls under 18 and 19,489 were women aged 18 to 30 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.4, who the accused was.** The offender was known to the victim in 96.8% of cases, 28,597 of 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.5, what police did.** Police filed charge-sheets in 24,614 cases, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3%, and 8,905 were still under investigation at year's end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It also lists 3,776 cases closed as "false": a police closure label, not a court finding [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.7, what courts did.** Courts convicted in 5,032 cases and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% of the 20,587 trials completed. At year's end, 1,85,785 cases were still pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

One rule prevents most mistakes: the conviction rate divides convictions by trials completed that year, not by cases registered. Many of those trials began with FIRs filed years earlier.

## Finding your state's line

Scroll to Table 3A.2 and find your state's row. Read across: IPC cases, BNS cases, total cases, victims, rate. Rajasthan's row, for example, shows 4,871 cases, 4,888 victims and a rate of 12.2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Victims can outnumber cases because one FIR can name more than one victim.

Now test the two forwards. Bihar registered 1,165 rape cases in 2024, a rate of 1.9 per lakh women. Maharashtra registered 3,091, a rate of 5.0 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The Maharashtra forward is simply wrong: Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh (3,209) both registered more [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And a count is not a rate. Uttar Pradesh has the second-highest count, but its rate of 2.8 is below the national 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The Bihar forward fails differently. A police rate measures reporting as well as violence. In the National Family Health Survey 2019-21, 40.1% of ever-married women in Bihar reported physical or sexual violence by a husband, the second-highest share of any state [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The two measure different things, but together they show why a low FIR rate is no safety certificate.

Then check where the children went. Nationally, only 784 rape cases involved girls under 18, against 43,313 POCSO cases of penetrative sexual assault on girls, listed in Table 3A.2(ii) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chapter 4A has the full POCSO count, boys included: Maharashtra registered 9,432 POCSO cases, the most of any state [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A few places file many child cases under rape instead. In Chandigarh, 47 of 96 rape cases had victims under 18, and Goa and Himachal Pradesh show the same pattern, which pushes up their rape rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Cities and caste: the other chapters

Chapter 3B covers cities, with a catch. NCRB collects data for 53 cities that had 10 lakh or more people at the 2011 Census, but prints only the 19 above 20 lakh; the other 34 are only online [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Patna and Pune are both among the 19 in print, and Pune registered 244 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. City rates use 2011 Census populations, so NCRB says they cannot be compared with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Crimes against Scheduled Castes and Tribes have their own chapter, Chapter 7, which in the 2023 edition sat in Volume II [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. The snapshots at the front of the 2024 Volume I give its headline figures: 4,262 rape cases of Scheduled Caste women and girls, and 1,268 rape cases with Scheduled Tribe victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read the chapter's footnote first. A case counts there only if police invoked the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act; cases filed only under the general penal code are left out, on the assumption that the accused was also SC or ST [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. If police leave the Act out, the case vanishes from the caste table. Treat these figures as a floor.

## The caveats NCRB prints up front

NCRB prints its own warnings in the opening pages of the report. Read them before the numbers.

- **One FIR, one crime.** Under the "principal offence rule", an FIR with several offences is counted once, under the most serious one. A rape that ends in murder appears as murder with rape, not in the rape row [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Registration is not crime.** NCRB says "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things; e-FIR facilities and women's help desks can push numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].
- **Don't rank states on this alone.** NCRB calls such comparisons "too simplistic" and "best avoided". More registered crime in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

None of this makes the tables useless. Each row tells you exactly what police recorded, in which year, under which law. Quote it that way, and no forward can twist it.
find-state-rape-data-ncrb-tables.hg:
Socho, ek hi hafte mein tumhare family WhatsApp group mein do forwards aate hain. Pehla kehta hai ki Bihar auraton ke liye sabse safe state hai. Doosra kehta hai ki India mein sabse zyada rapes Maharashtra mein hote hain. Dono ko tum das minute mein, free mein check kar sakte ho. India mein quote hone wale zyada tar rape figures ek hi saalana report se aate hain, jo National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) chhapta hai. Chalo dekhte hain ki report kahan milti hai, kaun si tables kaam ki hain, aur apne state ki line kaise padhni hai.

## Report kahan milti hai

20 November 2026 tak Crime in India ka sabse naya edition 2024 wali report hai [[ncrb-website-cii-year-wise-2026]]. Yeh 6 May 2026 ko release hui thi [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]]. Iske teen volumes hain, aur tumhare kaam ka Volume I hai. Chapter 3A mein har state mein auraton ke khilaf crime hai, 3B mein bade shehar, aur 4A mein bachchon ke khilaf crime, jismein POCSO cases bhi aate hain. Direct link: https://www.ncrb.gov.in/uploads/files/11CrimeinIndia2024-VolumeI.pdf

Pehle samajh lo ki tumhare haath mein kya hai. States aur union territories ki police jo data bhejti hai, NCRB bas use jodkar chhapta hai. Uske apne disclaimer mein likha hai ki is information ke sahi hone ki zimmedari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani ismein gine gaye cases woh FIRs hain jo police ne register kin. Yeh is baat ka naap nahi hai ki asal mein kitni violence hui.

## Table by table: cases, umar, accused, police, courts

Chapter 3A ki paanch tables mein tumhare kaam ki zyada tar cheezein mil jaati hain.

- **Table 3A.2: cases aur rate.** 2024 mein India mein rape ke 29,536 cases register hue, jinmein 29,742 victims thin. Rate raha har lakh auraton par 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 1 July 2024 se IPC ki jagah Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) laagu hui, isliye is saal ki ginti do hisson mein hai: IPC ke 19,683 cases aur BNS ke 9,853 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.3: victims ki umar.** 29,742 victims mein se 792 ladkiyan 18 se kam umar ki thin, aur 19,489 auratein 18 se 30 saal ki thin [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.4: accused kaun tha.** 96.8% cases mein accused victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha, yaani 29,536 mein se 28,597 cases mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.5: police ne kya kiya.** Police ne 24,614 cases mein chargesheet file ki. Chargesheet rate 81.3% raha, aur saal ke end tak 8,905 cases ki investigation chal hi rahi thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi table mein 3,776 cases "false" bolkar band kiye gaye dikhte hain. Yeh police ka lagaya label hai, court ka faisla nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Table 3A.7: courts ne kya kiya.** Courts ne 5,032 cases mein saza sunayi aur 13,980 mein accused bari ho gaye. Jin 20,587 cases ka trial poora hua, unmein conviction rate 24.4% raha. Saal ke end mein 1,85,785 cases ka trial pending tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek rule yaad rakho, isse zyada tar galtiyan bach jaati hain. Conviction rate us saal poore hue trials se nikalta hai, us saal register hue cases se nahi. Inmein se kai trials aisi FIRs se shuru hue the jo saalon pehle darj hui thin.

## Apne state ki line dhoondho

Table 3A.2 tak scroll karo aur apne state ki row dhoondho. Phir left se right padho: IPC cases, BNS cases, total cases, victims, aur rate. Jaise Rajasthan ki row mein 4,871 cases, 4,888 victims aur 12.2 ka rate likha hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Victims ki ginti cases se zyada ho sakti hai, kyunki ek FIR mein ek se zyada victims ho sakti hain.

Ab un dono forwards ko test karo. 2024 mein Bihar mein rape ke 1,165 cases register hue, yaani har lakh auraton par 1.9. Maharashtra mein 3,091 cases register hue, rate 5.0 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Maharashtra wala forward seedha galat hai: Rajasthan aur Uttar Pradesh (3,209), dono mein usse zyada cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur count aur rate ek cheez nahi hain. Uttar Pradesh count mein doosre number par hai, lekin uska rate 2.8 hai, jo national rate 4.3 se kam hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bihar wala forward alag tarah se galat hai. Police ka rate sirf violence nahi naapta, yeh bhi naapta hai ki kitni complaints police tak pahunchin. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein Bihar ki jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi hui hai, unmein se 40.1% ne bataya ki pati ne unke saath physical ya sexual violence ki. Yeh kisi bhi state mein doosra sabse ooncha share hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Dono numbers alag cheezein naapte hain, lekin saath rakho toh saaf dikhta hai ki FIR ka kam rate safety ka certificate nahi hai.

Phir dekho ki bachchon ke cases kahan gaye. Poore India mein rape ke sirf 784 cases 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke the, jabki ladkiyon par POCSO ke penetrative sexual assault (yaani bachchiyon ke rape) ke 43,313 cases Table 3A.2(ii) mein darj hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO ki poori ginti, ladkon samet, Chapter 4A mein hai: Maharashtra mein POCSO ke 9,432 cases register hue, jo kisi bhi state se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kuch jagahen bachchon ke kai cases POCSO ki jagah rape mein darj karti hain. Chandigarh mein rape ke 96 mein se 47 cases mein victim 18 se kam umar ki thi, aur Goa aur Himachal Pradesh mein bhi yahi pattern hai, isliye wahan rape ka rate upar chala jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Cities aur caste: baaki chapters

Chapter 3B mein cities ka data hai, par ek pench hai. NCRB un 53 cities ka data jodta hai jinki population 2011 Census mein 10 lakh ya usse zyada thi, lekin print sirf un 19 cities ka karta hai jo 20 lakh se upar thin. Baaki 34 cities ka data sirf online milta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Patna aur Pune, dono print hone wali 19 cities mein hain, aur 2024 mein Pune mein rape ke 244 cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cities ka rate 2011 Census ki population se nikalta hai, isliye NCRB kehta hai ki city aur state ke rates compare nahi ho sakte [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Scheduled Castes aur Scheduled Tribes ke khilaf crime ka alag chapter hai, Chapter 7, jo 2023 ke edition mein Volume II mein tha [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. 2024 ke Volume I ki shuruaat mein chhape snapshots iske main figures dete hain: Scheduled Caste auraton aur ladkiyon ke rape ke 4,262 cases, aur Scheduled Tribe victims wale 1,268 rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin pehle chapter ka footnote padho. Koi case yahan tabhi gina jaata hai jab police ne SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act lagaya ho. Jo cases sirf general penal code mein darj hue, woh bahar reh jaate hain, is maanyata par ki unmein accused bhi SC ya ST tha [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Agar police ne Act nahi lagaya, toh case caste wali table se gayab ho jaata hai. Isliye in numbers ko minimum ginti samjho, poori ginti nahi.

## Report ki shuruaat mein chhapi warnings

NCRB report ke shuruaati pannon mein apni warnings khud chhapta hai. Numbers se pehle inhe padho.

- **Ek FIR, ek crime.** "Principal offence rule" ke tehat ek FIR mein kai offences hon, tab bhi use ek hi baar gina jaata hai, sabse serious offence ke naam par. Jis rape ke baad murder hua, woh "murder with rape" mein dikhta hai, rape wali row mein nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Register hona aur crime hona alag hai.** NCRB kehta hai ki "crime badhna" aur "police mein crime zyada register hona" do alag baatein hain. e-FIR facility aur women help desks jaisi cheezon se bhi numbers badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].
- **Sirf in numbers se states ki ranking mat karo.** NCRB aise comparison ko "too simplistic" kehta hai aur bolta hai ki isse "bachna hi behtar" hai. Uske hisaab se kisi city mein zyada crime register hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki woh city doosri cities se zyada unsafe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki yeh tables bekaar hain. Har row theek-theek batati hai ki police ne kis saal, kis law mein, kya darj kiya. Numbers isi tarah quote karo, phir koi forward unhe tod-marod nahi paayega.

first-crime-data-under-new-bns.en:
Look up rape in *Crime in India 2024* and you meet two numbers before you reach the total: 19,683 cases under the Indian Penal Code and 9,853 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 29,536 in all [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It is the first edition of the National Crime Records Bureau's annual report to cover one year under two penal codes, and the change goes deeper than the column headings. One offence has its own row for the first time, one has vanished, and one has been split into five. Read carelessly, the 2024 data shows crimes rising or falling when only the definitions moved. This is a field guide to reading it properly.

## 1 July 2024: the changeover

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code of 1860 across India on 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Crime is still counted by calendar year, so the 2024 tables for penal-code crimes carry an IPC column and a BNS column.

The split is not a clean half and half. The date of the offence decides the code, not the date of the complaint: offences committed before 1 July 2024 were registered under the IPC, later ones under the BNS [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. An assault committed in May but reported in October goes into the IPC column.

So the first rule is simple. Never quote one column as the year. The 2024 rape figure is 29,536, against 29,670 in 2023 and 31,516 in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## A new row: Section 69

The BNS created an offence the IPC never named. Section 69 punishes sex obtained by "deceitful means" or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it, including false promises of a job or promotion and marrying while hiding one's identity. The punishment is up to 10 years, and the law describes this sex as "not amounting to the offence of rape" [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Between July and December 2024, police registered 1,325 cases under it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That number has no past. It is not a rise or a fall, only a first reading.

It may also pull cases out of the rape column. The largest offender group in the 2024 rape table, 13,879 cases, lumps together friends, online friends, live-in partners on the pretext of marriage and separated husbands, and the table does not separate out the promise-of-marriage cases inside it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. If complaints that police once booked as rape now go to Section 69, the rape count can shrink a little while nothing changes in women's lives. The 2024 data cannot yet tell us whether that is happening.

A new row can also be an old crime newly counted. Revealing a rape survivor's identity has been an offence since 1983, under Section 228A of the IPC [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. NCRB began showing it as its own category only with BNS Section 72, which logged 11 cases in the second half of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## A deleted row: unnatural offences

Once the Supreme Court took consensual same-sex relations between adults out of it in 2018 [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]], Section 377 of the IPC was left covering non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" and sex with animals. It produced 987 cases in 2022 and 888 in 2023, with no split by the victim's sex or by type. In the 2024 columns the row is blank, with a note that the section was "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Nothing in the new code replaced it. The BNS defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under it, and the BNS has no other specific offence for it [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Boys under 18 are still protected by POCSO. In November 2023 a parliamentary committee had warned that dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it; the government did not accept this [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

The lesson for any reader is blunt. The 888 cases of 2023 did not become zero in 2024. The count simply stopped.

## A split row: assault on modesty

Until 2023, NCRB's category "assault on women with intent to outrage her modesty" bundled five offences: the assault itself plus sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking. On that broad basis it recorded 83,891 cases in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

The 2024 report lists the five separately. The narrow category, Section 74 BNS or Section 354 IPC, shows 48,303 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sexual harassment adds 15,609, stalking 9,865, disrobing 8,409 and voyeurism 1,722 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Same definition, three years | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Narrow category only | 44,867 | 45,086 | 48,303 |
| All five offences together | 83,344 | 83,891 | 83,908 |

Put 48,303 next to 83,891 and you invent a collapse in sexual assault. Compare like with like and the picture changes: the narrow offence rose, and the five together held almost exactly steady, at roughly 230 cases a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Rules for comparing 2024 with 2023

1. **Add the columns.** IPC plus BNS is the year. Neither column alone is a trend.
2. **Check the definition before the number.** NCRB marks new, deleted and split categories in its footnotes and glossary. Read them first.
3. **A new row has no trend.** The 1,325 Section 69 cases are a baseline, and the rape count may lose cases to them.
4. **A missing row is not a safe year.** The 888 "unnatural offences" cases of 2023 have no 2024 successor.
5. **Registration is not crime.** NCRB itself warns that more registered cases do not mean more crime, and it counts each FIR only once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most violence never reaches a station: in NFHS-5, 77% of women who faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The new code changed the labels, not the lives behind them. If you need to report a sexual offence, any police station must record it wherever the crime happened (a Zero FIR), it can also be given electronically, and you are entitled to a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
first-crime-data-under-new-bns.hg:
*Crime in India 2024* mein rape ka data kholo, toh total se pehle do alag numbers milte hain: Indian Penal Code (IPC) ke under 19,683 cases aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke under 9,853, total 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ki yeh pehli annual report hai jismein ek hi saal do penal codes mein bata hua hai, aur badlaav sirf column ke naam ka nahi hai. Ek offence ko pehli baar apni alag row mili hai, ek ki row gayab ho gayi hai, aur ek row paanch hisson mein toot gayi hai. Jaldi mein padhoge toh lagega crime badh gaya ya ghat gaya, jabki badli sirf definition hai. Yeh story isi data ko sahi se padhne ki field guide hai.

## 1 July 2024: jis din law badla

1 July 2024 se poore India mein Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne 1860 ke Indian Penal Code ki jagah le li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Lekin crime ab bhi calendar year ke hisaab se gina jaata hai, isliye penal code wale crimes ki 2024 ki tables mein ab ek IPC column hai aur ek BNS column.

Yeh split aadha-aadha nahi hai. Kaunsa code lagega, yeh offence ki date se decide hota hai, complaint ki date se nahi: 1 July 2024 se pehle hue offences IPC mein register hue, uske baad wale BNS mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Matlab agar assault May mein hua aur report October mein hui, toh bhi case IPC column mein hi jaayega.

Toh pehla rule simple hai. Kisi ek column ko poore saal ka figure mat batao. 2024 mein rape ke total cases 29,536 hain, 2023 mein 29,670 the aur 2022 mein 31,516 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Nayi row: Section 69

BNS ne ek aisa offence banaya jiska IPC mein alag se koi naam nahi tha. Section 69 un cases ke liye hai jahan sex "dhokhe se" kiya gaya ho, ya shaadi ka aisa waada karke jise nibhane ka irada hi na ho. Naukri ya promotion ka jhootha waada aur apni pehchaan chhupa kar shaadi karna bhi isi mein aata hai. Saza 10 saal tak hai, aur law khud likhta hai ki yeh sex "rape ka offence nahi" hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

July se December 2024 ke beech police ne is section mein 1,325 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is number ka koi pichhla record nahi hai. Yeh na badhna hai, na ghatna, bas pehli reading hai.

Yeh section rape column se kuch cases kheench bhi sakta hai. 2024 ki rape table mein accused ka sabse bada group, 13,879 cases, kai tarah ke logon ko ek saath jodta hai: friends, online friends, shaadi ke bahane saath rehne wale live-in partners aur alag reh rahe husbands. Table inmein se shaadi ke waade wale cases alag nahi dikhati [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo complaints police pehle rape mein register karti thi, agar woh ab Section 69 mein jaane lagein, toh rape ka count thoda ghat sakta hai, jabki auraton ki life mein kuch nahi badla. 2024 ka data abhi yeh nahi bata sakta ki aisa ho raha hai ya nahi.

Nayi row ka matlab hamesha naya crime nahi hota. Rape survivor ki identity reveal karna 1983 se offence hai, IPC ki Section 228A ke under [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Lekin NCRB ne ise alag category mein dikhana ab jaake shuru kiya, BNS Section 72 ke saath, jismein 2024 ke aakhri chhe mahino mein 11 cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Deleted row: "unnatural offences"

2018 mein Supreme Court ne adults ke beech consensual same-sex relations ko Section 377 se bahar kar diya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Uske baad IPC ka yeh section bina consent wale "unnatural" sexual intercourse aur jaanwaron ke saath sex ke cases ke liye bacha tha. Ismein 2022 mein 987 cases register hue aur 2023 mein 888, aur NCRB ne yeh alag nahi dikhaya ki victim aadmi tha, aurat thi ya case kis tarah ka tha. 2024 ke columns mein yeh row khaali hai, bas ek note hai ki section "deleted in BNS" hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Naye code mein iski jagah kuch nahi aaya. BNS mein rape ki definition hi yeh hai ki yeh ek aadmi kisi aurat ke saath karta hai. Isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender person ke saath bina consent penetrative sex naye code mein rape nahi hai, aur BNS mein iske liye koi doosra specific offence bhi nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 18 saal se kam umar ke ladkon ko POCSO ab bhi protect karta hai. November 2023 mein ek parliamentary committee ne warn kiya tha ki Section 377 hatane se aadmiyon aur transgender logon ke khilaaf bina consent wale sexual offences ki koi saza nahi bachegi, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation di thi; government ne yeh baat nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

Padhne waalon ke liye lesson seedha hai. 2023 ke 888 cases 2024 mein zero nahi ho gaye. Bas unki ginti band ho gayi.

## Toot gayi row: "outraging modesty"

2023 tak NCRB ki ek category thi "assault on women with intent to outrage her modesty", jismein paanch offences ek saath gine jaate the: khud yeh assault, sexual harassment, kapde utaarne ke irade se assault, voyeurism (chori-chhupe dekhna ya record karna) aur stalking. Is badi category mein 2023 mein 83,891 cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

2024 ki report in paanchon ko alag-alag dikhati hai. Ab chhoti category, yaani Section 74 BNS ya Section 354 IPC, mein 48,303 cases hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Uske alawa sexual harassment ke 15,609, stalking ke 9,865, kapde utaarne ke irade se assault ke 8,409 aur voyeurism ke 1,722 cases hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Same definition, teen saal | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sirf chhoti category | 44,867 | 45,086 | 48,303 |
| Paanchon offences milakar | 83,344 | 83,891 | 83,908 |

48,303 ko 83,891 ke saamne rakh do toh lagega sexual assault achanak collapse ho gaya, jo kabhi hua hi nahi. Same cheez ko same cheez se compare karo toh picture badal jaati hai: chhoti category ke cases badhe, aur paanchon milakar lagbhag utne hi rahe, roz kareeb 230 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 2024 ko 2023 se compare karne ke rules

1. **Dono columns jodo.** IPC plus BNS se poora saal banta hai. Akela koi column trend nahi batata.
