Or a handful of cases where police never identified the accused can pull a small state's percentage down. NCRB's column mixes both. What the table does not support is a "stranger danger" story: even at the bottom of the list, the accused was someone the survivor knew in roughly four cases out of five.

## Small numbers, big swings

Sikkim registered 7 rape cases in 2024, Nagaland 14, Manipur 19 and Mizoram 20 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At that scale, one family's decision to go to the police, or one officer who writes down every complaint, can move a rate more than any change in violence. Registrations can also fall fast: Assam's registered crimes against women dropped from 29,046 in 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] to 10,546 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], almost two-thirds in three years. NCRB does not explain such trends, and a fall like that can reflect changes in policing or reporting rather than in violence.

Underneath every table sits silence: 77% of Indian women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone, and only 6% of those who sought help went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. So read the Northeast as you would read any state: the rate, the count behind it, and a survey beside it.

Mizoram's police filed charge sheets in 95.9% of the crime-against-women cases they disposed of in 2024, the highest of any state, against 77.2% nationally [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That says something about what happens after a complaint, not about how many women are hurt. No single stereotype, that the region is uniquely safe or uniquely dangerous, survives the numbers. What survives is a question every state shares: how many women and children never reach the table at all?
northeast-sexual-violence-data-outliers.hg:
2024 ke India ke crime statistics ki lagbhag koi bhi table uthaiye, uske kisi ek sire par koi north-eastern state baitha milega. Arunachal Pradesh mein rape 9.9 cases per lakh women ki rate se register hua, jo national rate 4.3 ke double se bhi zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nagaland mein aurton ke khilaaf registered crime ka rate desh mein sabse kam tha, 5.1, aur Manipur doosre number par tha, 12.0 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sikkim, Mizoram aur Meghalaya un paanch states mein hain jahan POCSO rates sabse zyada hain. Aur jin chaar states mein rape accused sabse kam baar survivor ke jaan-pehchaan wale the, unmein se teen isi region mein hain. Yeh story poochti hai ki in outliers mein se kaun violence ke baare mein kuch batate hain, aur kaun zyada yeh batate hain ki violence ginti kaise hoti hai.

## Arunachal ka ooncha rate, Nagaland ka neecha

Arunachal ka 9.9 India ke 36 states aur union territories mein paanchvaan sabse ooncha rate hai, Chandigarh, Goa, Rajasthan aur Delhi ke baad [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf 76 registered cases se banta hai. Phir bhi Arunachal mein aurton ke khilaaf saare crimes ka rate, 41.8, national 64.6 se kaafi neeche hai. Uske 321 registered crimes against women mein se 76 rape the; poore India mein 4,41,534 mein se 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani Arunachal mein police tak jo pahunchta hai, usmein rape ka hissa poore desh ke muqable kahin bada hai.

Table iski wajah nahi bata sakti. Yeh zyada violence ho sakti hai, zyada complaints ka register hona ho sakta hai, ya case file karne ka tareeka. Zyada tar states 18 se kam umar ki ladki ka rape POCSO ke tahat record karte hain, par sab nahi: Chandigarh, jo rape table mein sabse upar hai, wahan ke 96 rape cases mein se 47 mein victim 18 se kam umar ki thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Doosre sire par, Nagaland ki police ne poore 2024 mein aurton ke khilaaf sirf 56 crimes register kiye, jinmein 14 rape the; Manipur ne 19 rape register kiye. Inke rape rates, 1.3 aur 1.2, India ke sabse kam chhe rates mein aate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek survey 'chup' aur 'safe' ke beech ka fark samajhne mein madad karta hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein Nagaland ki 6.5% ever-married women ne pati ki taraf se physical ya sexual violence report ki, jo kisi bhi state mein sabse kam hai. Manipur mein yeh 39.6% thi, Karnataka aur Bihar ke baad teesri sabse oonchi, jabki national figure 29.2% hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Shaadi ke andar ki violence rape count nahi hai, aur dono ke saal bhi alag hain. Par jahan dono kam hain, jaise Nagaland mein, wahan dono ek hi taraf ishaara karte hain. Jahan sirf police figure kam hai, jaise Manipur mein, wahan khamoshi zyada sambhav wajah hai. Agle survey round, NFHS-6, ne Manipur ko cover hi nahi kiya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## Bachchon ke cases: Sikkim, Mizoram, Meghalaya

2024 mein states mein sabse ooncha POCSO rate Kerala ka tha, 48.0 cases per lakh children. Uske baad aaye Sikkim (36.7), Mizoram (36.4), Tamil Nadu (33.7) aur Meghalaya (30.7), jabki national rate 15.6 tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi teenon north-eastern states ke registered rape rates national 4.3 se neeche the: Sikkim 2.1, Mizoram 3.2, Meghalaya 3.4. Meghalaya ki police ne POCSO ke tahat 424 cases register kiye, aur rape law ke tahat 57 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO harassment se le kar penetrative assault tak, bachchon ke khilaaf har tarah ke sexual offences ginta hai.

Ooncha POCSO rate is baat ka saboot nahi hai ki wahan zyada bachchon ke saath abuse hota hai. NCRB khud warn karta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag cheezein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. POCSO ke tahat jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho, use report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Sochiye, Shillong ki ek 13 saal ki ladki apni class teacher ko ek uncle ke baare mein batati hai. Agar teacher police ke paas jaati hai, toh woh Meghalaya ke 424 cases mein se ek ban jaati hai. Agar yahi baat kisi aisi jagah ho jahan teachers chup reh jaate hain, toh woh kisi ginti mein aati hi nahi, aur woh state kaagaz par zyada safe dikhta hai. POCSO ke 'quiet states' par hamari story yahi baat Bihar (5.2) aur Uttar Pradesh (9.5) ke liye kehti hai.

Do saavdhaniyan abhi baaki hain. Bachchon ke rates 2011 Census ki child population par nikaale jaate hain, jo aaj ki sankhya se kaafi alag ho sakti hai. Aur region ka sabse bada state phir ek alag kahani sunata hai: Assam ne 2,920 POCSO cases register kiye, jo kisi bhi state ka saatvaan sabse bada count hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Kam jaan-pehchaan wale accused?

National level par 2024 mein rape ke 96.8% cases mein accused survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha; 29,536 mein se 939 cases mein offender anjaan tha ya kabhi pehchana hi nahi gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lagbhag har jagah yeh share 90% se upar tha. Sabse neeche chaar the: Nagaland (78.6%), Meghalaya (78.9%), West Bengal (84.9%) aur Mizoram (85.0%) [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab inke peeche ke cases giniye. Nagaland ke 78.6% ka matlab hai ki uske 14 mein se 3 cases mein accused anjaan tha ya pehchana nahi gaya. Mizoram ke 85.0% ka matlab hai 20 mein se 3. Meghalaya ke 78.9% ka matlab hai 57 mein se 12. Teenon milakar 20 se bhi kam cases, jabki poore India mein 939.

Ise do tarah se padha ja sakta hai. Ho sakta hai ki yahan police tak pahunchne wale gine-chune cases mein anjaan logon ka hissa sach mein bada ho. Ya phir kuch aise cases, jinmein police accused ko kabhi pehchaan hi nahi paayi, ek chhote state ka percentage neeche kheench sakte hain. NCRB ka column dono ko mila deta hai. Yeh table jis kahani ko support nahi karti, woh hai 'stranger danger' wali kahani: list ke bilkul neeche bhi, lagbhag har paanch mein se chaar cases mein accused survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha.

## Chhote numbers, bade jhatke

2024 mein Sikkim ne 7 rape cases register kiye, Nagaland ne 14, Manipur ne 19 aur Mizoram ne 20 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is scale par ek parivaar ka police ke paas jaane ka faisla, ya ek aisa officer jo har complaint likh leta hai, rate ko violence mein kisi bhi badlav se zyada hila sakta hai. Registrations tezi se gir bhi sakte hain: Assam mein aurton ke khilaaf registered crimes 2021 ke 29,046 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] se gir kar 2024 mein 10,546 reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani teen saal mein lagbhag do-tihai ki girawat. NCRB aise trends ki wajah nahi batata, aur aisi girawat violence ki jagah policing ya reporting mein badlav ka nateeja bhi ho sakti hai.

Har table ke neeche khamoshi hai: 18-49 saal ki jin Indian aurton ne physical ya sexual violence jheli, unmein se 77% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya, aur madad maangne walon mein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isliye Northeast ko waise hi padhiye jaise kisi bhi state ko padhte hain: rate, uske peeche ka count, aur saath mein ek survey.

Mizoram ki police ne 2024 mein aurton ke khilaaf crime ke jin cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 95.9% mein charge sheet file ki. Yeh kisi bhi state mein sabse zyada hai, jabki national figure 77.2% hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh number batata hai ki complaint ke baad kya hota hai, yeh nahi ki kitni aurtein hurt hoti hain. Koi bhi ek stereotype, ki yeh region khaas taur par safe hai ya khaas taur par khatarnak, in numbers ke saamne nahi tikta. Jo tikta hai, woh ek sawaal hai jo har state ka hai: kitni aurtein aur bachche kabhi is table tak pahunchte hi nahi?

police-rape-count-is-not-rape-count.en:
Every year, when the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) publishes Crime in India, one number travels fastest. For 2024 it was 29,536: the rape cases police registered that year, involving 29,742 women and girls, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In a headline or a WhatsApp forward, "cases registered" easily turns into "29,536 rapes". That is wrong. The number counts something real, but not what people think.

## The number everyone quotes

29,536 is a count of FIRs: complaints that reached a police station and were written down under the rape head.

Even before anyone decides whether to report, the law shrinks the count. Forced sex by a husband on a wife aged 18 or older is not rape under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the BNS either, and no specific offence replaced IPC Section 377 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Most rape of girls is filed under the POCSO Act instead: 43,313 penetrative-assault cases with girl victims in 2024, more than the whole rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

So the "rape count" holds only what the law calls rape and what police agreed to register. Now look at who reaches the police at all.

## The NFHS-5 arithmetic

The National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) asked women aged 18 to 49 about violence. Among those who had faced physical or sexual violence, 77% had never sought help or told anyone. Only 14% had sought help from anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Where did those 14% go? Mostly home. 61% turned to their own family; only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Do the sum. Take 100 women who have faced violence. Fourteen ask for help. Six per cent of 14 is less than one woman. Fewer than 1 in 100 goes to the police. That is a calculation from NFHS figures, not a number NFHS publishes [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Three honest caveats. The 6% is a share of the women who sought help, so "6% of women go to the police" overstates it. The figures mix physical and sexual violence. Women who faced both sought help more often, about a quarter of them, while those who faced only one kind did so less often, 10 to 12% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Either way, most never asked anyone for help. And the survey is itself a floor: answers given face to face to a stranger.

The silence is deepest where the law is absent. Among ever-married women who had experienced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband. Women abused only by their current husband sought help far less often than women abused only by a former husband: 11.3% against 23.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Because of the marital exception, most of that violence could never enter the rape count, even if every one of those women walked into a station.

## Where the '1%' comes from

You may have read that only 1% of rapes in India are reported. A 2022 peer-reviewed study in BMC Public Health noted estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence report it to the authorities [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. The authors linked that silence to false beliefs that put the responsibility on the victim, and to stigma around rape and female sexuality.

This is an estimate the authors cite from earlier studies, not a new calculation and not an official statistic. It points the same way as the NFHS sum, which reaches "fewer than 1 in 100" by a different route and for a wider group of women.

Nor is it permission to multiply 29,536 by 100 and post the result as India's "real" rape count. Nobody knows that number, and swapping one false precision for another corrects nothing.

Children are no different. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of children who reported being sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had told the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The sample was not nationally representative and the study predates POCSO, but it points the same way.

## India against the global benchmark

In most countries with data, fewer than 40% of women who experience violence seek help of any sort, and in almost all of them fewer than 10% of those who seek help go to the police, according to UN Women, citing the UN's World's Women 2015 report [[unwomen-facts-figures-evaw-2025]].

India sits below both lines: 14% seeking help, 6% of them going to the police. Behind that gap sit fears no table records: what the family will say, what an accused who lives nearby might do, whether the police will ask why she waited. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that a woman who delays reporting rape is lying, and says a lack of family support or fear of repercussions can cause the delay [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Consider this situation. A 22-year-old in Patna is sexually assaulted by a family friend. She tells her mother, who begs her to stay quiet until her sister's wedding. In NFHS terms she turned to family. In the NCRB table she does not exist.

## A correction you can post

The next time "29,536 rapes" lands in your family group, paste this:

> 29,536 is the number of rape cases police registered in 2024, not the number of rapes. Figures from India's own health survey suggest that fewer than 1 in 100 women who face violence go to the police.

To bring the police number closer to the truth, make reporting easier. Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), any police station must record a complaint wherever the crime happened (Zero FIR), a complaint can be sent electronically and signed within three days, and a woman's rape complaint must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A public servant who fails to record it commits a crime under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Our guide to Zero FIR and e-FIR walks through each step. This is general information, not legal advice.
police-rape-count-is-not-rape-count.hg:
Har saal National Crime Records Bureau, yaani NCRB, apni 'Crime in India' report nikalta hai, aur usme se ek number sabse tez viral hota hai. 2024 ke liye woh number tha 29,536: utne rape cases police ne us saal register kiye, jinme 29,742 auratein aur ladkiyan thi. Yaani har ek lakh auraton par 4.3 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kisi headline ya WhatsApp forward mein "registered cases" aasaani se "29,536 rapes" ban jaate hain. Yeh galat hai. Yeh number kuch sach zaroor ginta hai, par woh nahi jo log samajhte hain.

## Woh number jo sab share karte hain

29,536 asal mein FIRs ki ginti hai: woh complaints jo police station tak pahunchi aur rape wale column mein likhi gayi.

Report karne ki baat toh baad mein aati hai. Usse pehle kanoon hi ginti chhoti kar deta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke hisaab se, agar wife 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka zabardasti sex karna rape nahi maana jaata [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath bina consent ka penetrative sex bhi BNS mein rape nahi hai, aur purane IPC Section 377 ki jagah koi naya offence nahi bana [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke saath rape ke zyada tar cases POCSO Act mein darj hote hain: 2024 mein aise 43,313 cases POCSO ke Section 4 aur 6 mein register hue, jo poore rape head se bhi zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Matlab "rape count" mein sirf wahi hai jise kanoon rape maanta hai aur jise police ne register kiya. Ab dekho, police tak pahunchta kaun hai.

## NFHS-5 ka hisaab

National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne 18 se 49 saal ki auraton se violence ke baare mein poocha. Jinhone physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, unme se 77% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Sirf 14% ne kisi se help maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh 14% auratein help ke liye kahan gayi? Zyada tar ghar mein hi. 61% ne apni family se baat ki; police ke paas sirf 6% gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ab khud hisaab lagao. Maan lo 100 auraton ne violence jheli. Unme se 14 help maangti hain. 14 ka 6% ek se bhi kam hota hai. Yaani 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam aurat police tak jaati hai. Yeh calculation humne NFHS ke figures se kiya hai; NFHS khud yeh number publish nahi karta [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Iske saath teen baatein imaandari se samajh lo. Pehli, 6% un auraton ka hissa hai jinhone help maangi, sab auraton ka nahi, isliye "6% auratein police ke paas jaati hain" bolna baat ko badha-chadha kar bolna hai. Doosri, in figures mein physical aur sexual violence saath gine gaye hain. Jinhone dono tarah ki violence jheli, unhone zyada help maangi, kareeb chaar mein se ek ne, jabki sirf ek tarah ki violence jhelne walon mein yeh 10 se 12% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Dono hi soorat mein zyada tar auraton ne kisi se help nahi maangi. Teesri, survey khud bhi poora sach nahi pakadta: yeh jawab ek anjaan insaan ke saamne baith kar diye gaye the.

Chuppi wahan sabse gehri hai jahan kanoon hi saath nahi deta. Jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi hui thi aur jinhone sexual violence jheli, unme se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya. Jinke saath sirf current husband ne violence ki, unme se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi help maangi; jinke saath sirf pehle pati ne ki thi, unme yeh 23.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Marital exception ki wajah se is violence ka zyada tar hissa rape count mein aa hi nahi sakta, chahe yeh saari auratein police station chali jaayein.

## '1%' kahan se aaya

Tumne shayad suna hoga ki India mein sirf 1% rapes hi report hote hain. 2022 mein BMC Public Health journal mein chhapi ek peer-reviewed study ne aise estimates ka zikr kiya, jinke hisaab se sexual violence jhelne walon mein se sirf kareeb 1% hi police ya authorities tak report karte hain [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Authors ke hisaab se is chuppi ki wajah hai woh galat soch jo saari zimmedari survivor par daal deti hai, aur rape aur female sexuality se juda stigma.

Yeh authors ka apna naya calculation nahi hai. Yeh pehle ki studies se liya gaya estimate hai, koi official statistic bhi nahi. Phir bhi yeh usi taraf ishaara karta hai jidhar NFHS ka hisaab, jo ek alag raaste se, aur auraton ke bade group ke liye, "100 mein se 1 se bhi kam" tak pahunchta hai.

Iska matlab yeh bhi nahi ki 29,536 ko 100 se multiply karke use India ka "asli" rape count bata kar post kar do. Asli number kisi ko nahi pata, aur ek galat pakke number ki jagah doosra galat pakka number rakhne se kuch theek nahi hota.

Bachchon ke saath bhi yahi hota hai. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein jin bachchon ne bataya ki un par sexual assault hua tha, unme se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh sample poore desh ki tasveer nahi tha aur study POCSO se pehle ki hai, par yeh bhi usi taraf ishaara karti hai.

## Duniya ke mukable India

UN Women, UN ki World's Women 2015 report ke hawale se batata hai ki jin deshon ka data hai, unme se zyada tar mein violence jhelne wali 40% se kam auratein kisi bhi tarah ki help maangti hain, aur lagbhag sabhi deshon mein help maangne wali auraton mein se 10% se kam police ke paas jaati hain [[unwomen-facts-figures-evaw-2025]].

India in dono lines se neeche hai: yahan 14% help maangti hain, aur unme se sirf 6% police ke paas jaati hain. Is gap ke peeche aise darr hain jo kisi table mein darj nahi hote: ghar wale kya kahenge, aas-paas rehne wala accused kya karega, aur kahin thane mein yeh toh nahi poochha jaayega ki itni der kyun ki. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook is soch ko galat bataati hai ki rape ki complaint mein der karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai. Handbook kehti hai ki family ka saath na milna, ya aage kya hoga iska darr, der ki wajah ho sakta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Ek situation socho. Patna ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ke saath family ka hi ek jaan-pehchaan wala sexual assault karta hai. Woh apni maa ko batati hai. Maa haath jod kar kehti hai ki chhoti behen ki shaadi tak chup raho. NFHS ki bhasha mein usne family se help maangi. NCRB ki table mein woh kahin nahi hai.

## Ek jawab jo tum post kar sakte ho

Agli baar jab family group mein "29,536 rapes" wala message aaye, toh jawab mein yeh bhejo:

> 29,536 un rape cases ki ginti hai jo police ne 2024 mein register kiye. Yeh rapes ki ginti nahi hai. Desh ke apne health survey ke figures ke hisaab se violence jhelne wali 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam aurat police ke paas jaati hai.

Police ke number ko sach ke kareeb laana hai, toh report karna aasaan banana hoga. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke hisaab se koi bhi police station complaint register karega, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR). Complaint online bhi bheji ja sakti hai, bas teen din ke andar us par sign karna hota hai. Aur kisi aurat ki rape complaint woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo public servant aisi complaint record nahi karta, woh BNS ke Section 199 ke tahat crime karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Zero FIR aur e-FIR par humari guide har step samjhati hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

principal-offence-rule-hides-worst-rapes.en:
Consider a hypothetical FIR. A woman is raped and murdered. The police register one FIR that lists both crimes, and a court may later convict on both. But when the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) counts that FIR for *Crime in India*, it gets one line in one table, and that line is not "rape".

## One FIR, one line in the table

NCRB calls this the principal offence rule. When many offences are registered in a single FIR, its methodology says, only "the one that attracts maximum punishment will be considered as counting unit" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB says it follows an international standard in doing this, and the rule applies to every crime head in the report [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Apply it to a dowry case, for instance, and an FIR that includes both dowry death and cruelty counts only as a dowry death.

Courts do not work this way. When a Sealdah court in Kolkata sentenced the man convicted in the RG Kar Medical College case in January 2025, it did so under three sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 64 for rape and Section 103(1) for murder [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Our case file on that verdict tells the full story. A court can hold several crimes at once. NCRB's table cannot.

> Whatever else an FIR contains, its heaviest charge decides the one table it is counted in.

So a rape that ends in murder leaves the rape count. NCRB records it under a separate head, murder with rape or gang rape [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 2024 that head held 266 cases with 274 victims, led by Madhya Pradesh with 50 and Rajasthan with 38 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. None of them is part of the 29,536 rape cases that made the headlines [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The 2012 case that became a murder statistic

The clearest example is the case that changed India's rape law. According to a 2022 peer-reviewed study in *BMC Public Health*, the 2012 Delhi gang rape case was recorded as murder, not rape, because of this rule [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].

Think about what that means. The case led to the Justice Verma Committee, set up in December 2012 [[thehindu-verma-2013]], and to a wider legal definition of rape from February 2013 [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. In May 2017 the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences of the four adult convicts [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. Yet by the study's account, the case that rewrote the rape law sits in India's murder statistics, not among the 24,923 rape cases registered in 2012 [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]].

The study's authors drew the obvious conclusion: "it is very likely that there are more rape-related cases in the police records which are hidden in the NCRB reports" [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].

## What else drops out of the rape column

Rape-murders are the most visible loss. They are not the largest.

**Child rape.** An FIR about the rape of a girl that invokes POCSO Sections 4 or 6 is counted in the POCSO table instead. In 2024 it recorded 43,313 such cases with girl victims, more than the entire rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our data story on the POCSO column adds the two together.

**Gang rape of children.** The rape table recorded 1,537 gang-rape cases in 2024, and only 30 of them involved girls under 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That 30 is not a count of gang rapes of girls. Such cases are often registered under POCSO, and gang rapes that end in death go to the murder-with-rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Rapes the law does not call rape.** These are lost to the definition rather than the counting rule. Section 63 of the BNS covers only a man's assault on a woman, and it excludes a husband's forced sex with his adult wife [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Our myth-buster on the police figure looks at who that leaves out.

## Reading the rape count as a floor

NCRB admits the effect. Its 2024 disclaimer warns that because of the principal offence rule, "the actual count of each crime head may be different from reported" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For rape, the error runs one way. The rule can move an FIR with a rape charge out of the rape head, but it never adds an FIR without one.

So read the published figure for what it is. The 29,536 cases of 2024 are the FIRs in which rape of a woman or girl was the heaviest charge and the rape sections, not POCSO, were applied, after someone reached a police station. It is the minimum, not the total. A fuller count would also publish every FIR that includes a rape charge, whatever else it includes.

Until NCRB does that, two habits help. When you quote the figure, say "at least". When you compare years or states, put the rape, POCSO and murder-with-rape lines side by side before you conclude anything.

And if you are the one filing a complaint, the statistics are not your problem, but the FIR is. You are entitled to a free copy of it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; check that it records everything you told the police. This is general information, not legal advice.
principal-offence-rule-hides-worst-rapes.hg:
Ek hypothetical FIR ke baare mein sochiye. Ek aurat ka rape hua aur phir uska murder kar diya gaya. Police ek hi FIR register karti hai jismein dono crimes likhe hain, aur aage chal kar court dono ke liye saza bhi de sakti hai. Lekin jab National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) *Crime in India* ke liye is FIR ko ginta hai, toh ise ek hi table mein ek hi line milti hai. Aur woh line "rape" ki nahi hoti.

## Ek FIR, table mein ek line

NCRB ise "principal offence rule" kehta hai. Uski methodology kehti hai ki agar ek hi FIR mein kai offences darj hon, toh sirf "the one that attracts maximum punishment" ko counting unit maana jaayega [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB kehta hai ki woh aisa ek international standard ke hisaab se karta hai, aur yeh rule report ke har crime head par lagta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Misaal ke taur par, ise dowry ke case par lagaiye: jis FIR mein dowry death aur cruelty dono hon, woh sirf dowry death mein gini jaayegi.

Courts is tarah kaam nahi karte. January 2025 mein Kolkata ki Sealdah court ne RG Kar Medical College case mein convict hue aadmi ko saza sunayi, aur yeh saza Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke teen sections mein di gayi, jinmein rape ka Section 64 aur murder ka Section 103(1) shamil hain [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Us verdict par hamari case file poori kahani batati hai. Court ek saath kai crimes maan sakti hai. NCRB ki table aisa nahi kar sakti.

> FIR mein aur chahe jo bhi likha ho, uska sabse bhaari charge hi tay karta hai ki woh kis ek table mein gini jaayegi.

Isliye jis rape ke baad murder hota hai, woh rape count se bahar ho jaata hai. NCRB use ek alag head mein record karta hai: murder with rape ya gang rape [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 mein is head mein 266 cases the, jinmein 274 victims darj hue. Sabse zyada cases Madhya Pradesh mein the, 50, aur uske baad Rajasthan mein, 38 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein se ek bhi case un 29,536 rape cases mein nahi hai jo headlines mein chhaaye rahe [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 2012 ka case jo murder statistic ban gaya

Sabse clear example wahi case hai jisne India ka rape law badal diya. *BMC Public Health* journal mein 2022 mein chhapi ek peer-reviewed study ke mutabik, isi rule ki wajah se 2012 ka Delhi gang rape case rape nahi, murder ke roop mein record hua [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].

Zara sochiye iska matlab kya hai. Isi case ke baad December 2012 mein Justice Verma Committee bani [[thehindu-verma-2013]], aur February 2013 se rape ki legal definition badi hui [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. May 2017 mein Supreme Court ne chaaron adult convicts ki death sentence barkarar rakhi [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]]. Phir bhi is study ke hisaab se, jis case ne rape law dobara likhwaya, woh India ke murder statistics mein baitha hai, 2012 mein register hue 24,923 rape cases mein nahi [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]].

Study ke authors ne isse seedha nateeja nikala: "it is very likely that there are more rape-related cases in the police records which are hidden in the NCRB reports" [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]].

## Rape column se aur kya bahar reh jaata hai

Rape-murder cases sabse zyada dikhte hain. Par sabse bada hissa woh nahi hain.

**Child rape.** Kisi ladki ke rape ki jis FIR mein POCSO Section 4 ya 6 lagta hai, woh POCSO table mein gini jaati hai. 2024 mein us table mein girl victims wale aise 43,313 cases darj hue, jo poore rape head se bhi zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO column par hamari data story dono ko jod kar dikhati hai.

**Bachchiyon ka gang rape.** 2024 mein rape table mein gang rape ke 1,537 cases darj hue, aur inmein se sirf 30 cases 18 saal se kam ki ladkiyon ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh 30 ladkiyon ke gang rape ki asli ginti nahi hai. Aise cases aksar POCSO mein register hote hain, aur jis gang rape ke baad maut ho jaati hai, woh murder with rape wale head mein chala jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Woh rapes jinhe law rape hi nahi maanta.** Yeh counting rule se nahi, definition ki wajah se bahar reh jaate hain. BNS ka Section 63 sirf us assault ko rape maanta hai jo ek aadmi kisi aurat par karta hai, aur ismein pati ka apni adult wife ke saath zabardasti sex shamil nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police figure wale myth par hamara article batata hai ki isse kaun-kaun chhoot jaata hai.

## Rape count ko 'kam se kam' ki tarah padhiye

NCRB khud yeh asar maanta hai. 2024 ke disclaimer mein woh warn karta hai ki principal offence rule ki wajah se "the actual count of each crime head may be different from reported" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape ke case mein yeh farq ek hi taraf jaata hai. Yeh rule rape charge wali FIR ko rape head se bahar toh kar sakta hai, par bina rape charge wali koi FIR usmein kabhi nahi jodta.

Isliye published figure ko waise hi padhiye jaisa woh hai. 2024 ke 29,536 cases woh FIRs hain jinmein kisi aurat ya ladki ka rape sabse bhaari charge tha, POCSO ki jagah rape sections lage, aur koi police station tak pahunch paaya. Yeh minimum ginti hai, poori ginti nahi. Ek behtar count mein har woh FIR bhi publish honi chahiye jismein rape ka charge ho, phir usmein chahe aur jo bhi offences hon.

Jab tak NCRB aisa nahi karta, do aadatein kaam aayengi. Figure quote karte waqt "kam se kam" boliye. Aur saalon ya states ko compare karte waqt, koi nateeja nikalne se pehle rape, POCSO aur murder with rape, teeno lines saath rakhiye.

Aur agar complaint aap khud file kar rahe hain, toh statistics aapki fikr nahi hain, par FIR zaroor hai. Aapko uski free copy paane ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; usmein check kijiye ki aapne police ko jo-jo bataya, woh sab likha hai ya nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

rajasthan-rape-count-false-closures.en:
For three years running, no state has registered more rape cases than Rajasthan: 5,399 in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2022]], 5,078 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] and 4,871 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The same 2024 report holds two other numbers. Rajasthan's police closed 12,217 crime-against-women cases as "false", a third of all such closures in India, and filed charge-sheets in 54.1% of the cases they finished investigating, the lowest rate of any state or union territory [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Together, the three numbers raise a question the published data cannot answer: does Rajasthan register more complaints and filter them later, or does it fail women after the FIR?

## Three years at the top

Rajasthan's rate was 13.8 rape cases per lakh women in 2022 and 12.8 in 2023, against national rates of 4.7 and 4.4 [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. In 2024 its rate was 12.2, nearly three times the national 4.3, and its 4,871 cases were 16.5% of India's total, though it has 5.9% of India's projected female population [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Only two small places, Chandigarh and Goa, had higher rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Its police also registered the most cases of assault to outrage a woman's modesty, 8,276, and the second-most attempts to rape, 778 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Its registered crimes against women of all kinds, meanwhile, fell from 45,450 in 2023 to 36,563 in 2024, a drop of 19.6%, though its rate of 91.3 per lakh women was still the fifth-highest in India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A one-year fall that steep could mean less violence or fewer complaints registered. The tables cannot say which.

## 12,217 'false' closures

Police end an investigation with either a charge-sheet, which sends the accused for trial, or a final report, which asks the court to close the case. A "final report false" is the police conclusion that the complaint was untrue. It is a police classification, not a court finding, and NCRB does not publish the reasons behind it [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In 2024 Rajasthan's police closed 12,217 crime-against-women cases this way, a third of India's 36,895 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two cautions apply. The figure covers every crime against women, from cruelty by a husband to kidnapping, not rape alone. And a year's closures can include cases registered in earlier years, so 12,217 cannot be divided by 2024's registrations to produce a "false" rate.

The categories are meant to be different. Nationally, of the 30,272 rape cases police disposed of in 2024, they closed 3,776 as false and 1,044 as true but with insufficient evidence or the accused untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A complaint police believe but cannot prove belongs in the last group, not under "false".

## 54.1%: India's lowest charge-sheeting rate

The charge-sheeting rate is the share of cases disposed of by police that end in a charge-sheet. For crimes against women in 2024 it was 77.2% nationally, ranging from 54.1% in Rajasthan to 95.9% in Mizoram; among large states, Andhra Pradesh reached 94.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In Rajasthan, nearly half the cases police finished investigating were not sent for trial.

The state capital mirrors the state. Of India's 19 largest cities, Jaipur had the lowest charge-sheeting rate, 55.7%, against 76.8% across all 19 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jaipur also had the highest registered rape rate among them, 34.2 per lakh women, though city rates rest on 2011 Census populations and NCRB warns against comparing them with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Two readings of the same data

**Reading one: an open door.** Indian law tells police to register first and test later. In Lalita Kumari (2013), a five-judge Supreme Court bench held that an FIR is mandatory when a complaint discloses a cognizable offence, with no preliminary inquiry [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Under the BNS, a public servant who fails to record a rape complaint faces six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and rape falls outside the 14-day preliminary enquiry that Section 173(3) BNSS allows for lesser offences [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A force that obeys these rules will register more complaints, and more will later fail investigation. NCRB itself warns that more registration can reflect better access to police rather than more crime [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

**Reading two: a door that shuts after the FIR.** Imagine a 24-year-old in a district town who reports a sexual assault by a neighbour. The FIR is written. Then the investigation stalls, both families push for a "compromise", and she stops answering the investigating officer's calls. Her file can close as "false", though nothing she said was shown to be untrue. Multiply that across thin investigations and pressured complainants, and 54.1% becomes the real headline; the high count is only where the failure begins.

Both readings fit the numbers, perhaps in different police stations, and the published tables cannot tell them apart. Yet "false" closures get quoted as proof that women lie, and the high count as proof that Rajasthan is uniquely dangerous. The data supports neither.

## What Rajasthan should publish

Rajasthan should publish the data that would settle it:

- closures by crime and by the year the FIR was registered, so rape can be separated from other offences;
- the grounds recorded in each "false" final report, grouped into categories;
- how many complainants were told of a closure, how many objected, and how many closure reports magistrates accepted or sent back for further investigation;
- figures by district and police station, to show whether closures cluster in a few places;
- how many rape investigations met the two-month deadline in Section 193(2) BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Until then, Rajasthan's numbers prove neither that it is India's most dangerous state nor that its women file false complaints. They do show that in 2024 a complaint of a crime against a woman was less likely to be sent for trial in Rajasthan than anywhere else in India. A victim is entitled to an investigation update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; in Rajasthan, ask for it in writing. This is general information, not legal advice.
rajasthan-rape-count-false-closures.hg:
Lagaatar teen saal se koi bhi state Rajasthan se zyada rape cases register nahi kar raha: 2022 mein 5,399 [[ncrb-cii-2022]], 2023 mein 5,078 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] aur 2024 mein 4,871 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi 2024 ki report mein do aur numbers hain. Rajasthan police ne auraton ke khilaf crime ke 12,217 cases "false" bolkar band kiye, jo India mein aise saare closures ka ek-tihaai hai. Aur jin cases ki investigation poori hui, unmein se sirf 54.1% mein chargesheet file hui, jo kisi bhi state ya union territory mein sabse kam rate hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Teeno numbers saath rakho toh ek sawaal khada hota hai jiska jawab published data nahi deta: kya Rajasthan zyada complaints darj karke baad mein unhe chhaant deta hai, ya FIR ke baad auraton ko fail kar deta hai?

## Teen saal sabse upar

Rajasthan ka rate 2022 mein har lakh auraton par 13.8 rape cases aur 2023 mein 12.8 tha, jabki national rate 4.7 aur 4.4 tha [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. 2024 mein uska rate 12.2 raha, yaani national 4.3 ka lagbhag teen guna, aur uske 4,871 cases India ke total ka 16.5% the, jabki India ki projected female population mein uska hissa sirf 5.9% hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sirf do chhoti jagahon, Chandigarh aur Goa, ka rate usse zyada tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Uski police ne aurat ki modesty bhang karne ke iraade se assault ke sabse zyada cases, 8,276, aur rape ki koshish ke doosre sabse zyada cases, 778, bhi register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Udhar, wahan auraton ke khilaf har tarah ke registered crimes 2023 ke 45,450 se gir kar 2024 mein 36,563 reh gaye, yaani 19.6% ki giravat. Phir bhi har lakh auraton par 91.3 ka uska rate India mein paanchve number par tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek saal mein itni tez giravat ka matlab kam violence bhi ho sakta hai aur kam complaints ka darj hona bhi. Tables yeh nahi bata saktin ki inmein se kaun sa sach hai.

## 12,217 'false' closures

Police investigation ya toh chargesheet ke saath khatam karti hai, jisse accused par trial chalta hai, ya final report ke saath, jismein court se case band karne ko kaha jaata hai. "Final report false" ka matlab hai police ka yeh nateeja ki complaint sach nahi thi. Yeh police ki classification hai, court ka faisla nahi, aur NCRB iske peeche ki wajahen publish nahi karta [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2024 mein Rajasthan police ne auraton ke khilaf crime ke 12,217 cases isi tarah band kiye, jo India ke 36,895 ka ek-tihaai hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Do baatein dhyaan mein rakhni hain. Yeh figure auraton ke khilaf har crime ka hai, pati ki cruelty se lekar kidnapping tak, sirf rape ka nahi. Aur kisi saal ke closures mein pichhle saalon mein darj cases bhi ho sakte hain, isliye 12,217 ko 2024 ke registrations se divide karke koi "false" rate nahi nikala ja sakta.

Yeh categories alag-alag hone ke liye hi bani hain. Poore India mein 2024 mein police ne rape ke jin 30,272 cases ka nipataara kiya, unmein se 3,776 "false" bolkar band kiye, aur 1,044 "true but insufficient evidence" ya accused ka pata na chalne ki wajah se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis complaint par police ko yakeen hai lekin woh use saabit nahi kar paati, uski jagah is aakhri group mein hai, "false" mein nahi.

## 54.1%: India ka sabse kam chargesheeting rate

Chargesheeting rate ka matlab hai ki police ne jin cases ka nipataara kiya, unmein se kitnon mein chargesheet file hui. 2024 mein auraton ke khilaf crimes mein yeh rate national level par 77.2% tha, Rajasthan ke 54.1% se lekar Mizoram ke 95.9% tak; bade states mein Andhra Pradesh 94.4% tak pahuncha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani Rajasthan mein police ne jin cases ki investigation poori ki, unmein se lagbhag aadhe trial ke liye bheje hi nahi gaye.

State ki capital bhi wahi kahani dikhati hai. India ke 19 sabse bade shehron mein Jaipur ka chargesheeting rate sabse kam tha, 55.7%, jabki in 19 shehron ka milakar rate 76.8% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In shehron mein Jaipur ka registered rape rate bhi sabse ooncha tha, har lakh auraton par 34.2, halaanki cities ke rates 2011 Census ki population par tike hain aur NCRB unhe state rates se compare karne se mana karta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Ek hi data, do tarah se padhna

**Pehli reading: khula darwaza.** Indian kanoon police se kehta hai ki pehle FIR darj karo, jaanch baad mein. Lalita Kumari (2013) mein Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki bench ne kaha ki agar complaint se cognizable offence banta hai toh FIR darj karna zaroori hai, aur usse pehle koi preliminary inquiry nahi ho sakti [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. BNS ke tahat jo public servant rape ki complaint darj nahi karta, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur rape us 14 din ki preliminary enquiry ke daayre se bahar hai jo Section 173(3) BNSS chhote offences ke liye allow karta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo police force in rules ko maanegi, woh zyada complaints darj karegi, aur unmein se zyada baad mein investigation mein tik nahi paayengi. NCRB khud warning deta hai ki zyada registration ka matlab zyada crime nahi, balki police tak behtar pahunch bhi ho sakta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

**Doosri reading: FIR ke baad band hota darwaza.** Socho, ek district town ki 24 saal ki aurat apne padosi ke khilaf sexual assault ki report karti hai. FIR likh li jaati hai. Phir investigation ruk jaati hai, dono parivaar "compromise" ke liye dabaav daalte hain, aur woh investigating officer ke calls uthana band kar deti hai. Uski file "false" bolkar band ho sakti hai, jabki uski kahi koi baat jhooth saabit nahi hui. Kamzor investigations aur dabaav jhelti complainants ke saath yahi kahani kai guna kar do, toh asli headline 54.1% ban jaati hai; bada count sirf woh jagah hai jahan se failure shuru hota hai.

Dono readings numbers mein fit baithti hain, shayad alag-alag police stations mein, aur published tables in dono mein fark nahi kar saktin. Phir bhi "false" closures ko is baat ka saboot bana kar quote kiya jaata hai ki auratein jhooth bolti hain, aur bade count ko is baat ka saboot ki Rajasthan sabse khatarnaak hai. Data in dono mein se kisi bhi daave ka saath nahi deta.

## Rajasthan ko kya publish karna chahiye

Rajasthan ko woh data publish karna chahiye jo yeh sawaal suljha de:

- closures, crime ke hisaab se aur FIR darj hone ke saal ke hisaab se, taaki rape ko baaki offences se alag dekha ja sake;
- har "false" final report mein likhi gayi wajah, categories mein baant kar;
- kitne complainants ko closure ke baare mein bataya gaya, kitnon ne objection kiya, aur magistrates ne kitni closure reports maanin ya aage investigation ke liye wapas bhejin;
- district aur police station ke hisaab se figures, taaki pata chale ki closures kuch hi jagahon par toh nahi simte;
- rape ki kitni investigations Section 193(2) BNSS ki do mahine wali deadline ke andar poori huin [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Tab tak Rajasthan ke numbers na yeh saabit karte hain ki woh India ka sabse khatarnaak state hai, na yeh ki wahan ki auratein jhoothi complaints karti hain. Haan, yeh zaroor dikhate hain ki 2024 mein auraton ke khilaf crime ki complaint ke trial tak bheje jaane ki sambhavna Rajasthan mein India ke kisi bhi aur hisse se kam thi. Victim ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update paane ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; Rajasthan mein ise likhit mein maango. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

rape-accused-known-to-survivor.en:
Of the 29,536 rape cases police registered in India in 2024, 28,597 named an accused the survivor already knew: 96.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 939 cases the accused was unknown or never identified [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Both numbers come from Table 3A.4 of the National Crime Records Bureau's annual report, which sorts every rape case by the accused's relationship to the survivor. Our myth-buster on the "dark lane" picture of rape asks what curfews cost. This story opens the table itself, group by group.

## 28,597 out of 29,536

The table counts cases, not people, and only cases that police registered. Each FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence, so a rape that ends in murder drops out of the rape count [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Fewer than 1 in 30 cases fell in the last column, accused "unknown or not identified", which mixes strangers with men police never traced.

Most survivors were young adults: of the 29,742 victims recorded under the rape head, 19,489 were aged 18 to 30 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most rape of girls under 18 is counted separately, under POCSO, and the pattern holds there too: in 96.6% of 2024 POCSO cases of penetrative sexual assault, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our story on child abusers opens that table.

## Inside NCRB's three categories

NCRB sorts the known accused into three groups [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Who the accused was (NCRB's wording) | Cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Friends, online friends, live-in partners "on pretext of marriage", separated husbands | 13,879 |
| Family friends, neighbours, employers, other known persons | 12,584 |
| Family members | 2,134 |
| Unknown or not identified | 939 |
| All rape cases | 29,536 |

**Friends and partners, 13,879 cases.** The largest group is also the most mixed. A boyfriend who used force, a man who lied about marriage and an estranged husband are counted together, and NCRB cannot separate the promise-of-marriage cases inside the group [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Since July 2024 deceit has its own offence, Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which logged 1,325 cases in its first six months, as our explainer on the first BNS crime data shows [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Neighbours, family friends and employers, 12,584 cases.** This is the group with access: men who come and go from the house, give a job or a lift, and have the family's trust. NCRB does not break down "other known persons".

**Family members, 2,134 cases.** The smallest group. Reporting here means accusing a relative, who may be the person the family depends on for money, shelter or standing.

**Who is missing.** A husband who forces sex on his wife aged 18 or older appears nowhere, because Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS says it is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Husbands living apart from their wives can be prosecuted under a separate offence, Section 67, with 2 to 7 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and NCRB folds them into the friends-and-partners group. Adult male survivors are missing too: Section 63 defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman", so in law an adult man cannot be raped [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Twelve years, the same pattern

The law shifted underneath these numbers. In 2013 Parliament widened the legal definition of rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]], and in 2024 the BNS replaced the IPC. Yet NCRB's figures for 2012 [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]], 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] and 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]] barely move:

| Year | Accused known to the survivor |
|---|---|
| 2012 | 98.2% (24,470 of 24,915) |
| 2023 | 97.5% (28,915 of 29,670) |
| 2024 | 96.8% (28,597 of 29,536) |

State figures tell the same story. The known share was above 90% in almost every state and union territory in 2024. The lowest were Nagaland (78.6%), Meghalaya (78.9%), West Bengal (84.9%) and Mizoram (85.0%) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Small numbers swing these shares: Nagaland's figure rests on 14 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even at the bottom of the list, roughly four in five cases named a known man.

## What survivors told surveyors

Police tables see only what reaches a station, and most violence never does. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The survey asked women at home who did it, and the answer matches the police table. Among never-married women who reported sexual violence, only 5% named a stranger. The most common answers were relatives other than a father or brother (39%), a current or former boyfriend (16%) and a family friend (12%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The group was small, so read the exact shares loosely. Among ever-married women who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]], the one man the police table almost never counts.

Two methods, different years, different definitions, one answer. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook for judges lists the belief that rapists are usually strangers as a false stereotype, and says it plainly [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> "Very often men sexually assault or rape a woman known to them in some capacity."

## Safety advice that fits the data

Consider three situations. A 23-year-old in Nagpur is being pushed to visit the flat of a man she has chatted with online for months. A 20-year-old in Patna is cornered by the owner of the shop where she works. A 26-year-old in Kochi has stopped visiting her uncle's house and cannot say why. "Don't talk to strangers" helps none of them. Each sits in a different column and needs something different.

- **With partners and online friends:** under Section 63, consent is an "unequivocal voluntary agreement", and a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Silence is not a yes, and a gift or a date does not buy one. Meet new online contacts in public first, and tell someone where you are.
- **With employers, neighbours and family friends:** watch for access and power, such as being alone with someone who controls your pay, housing or family's trust. Telling someone early, before "anything has happened", is not an overreaction.
- **In families:** abuse by a relative stays hidden when the first response is disbelief. Believe first, ask what she needs, and do not force a confrontation.
- **At the police station:** any station must register a rape complaint wherever the crime happened, a woman officer must record a woman's complaint, and her statement must be recorded at her home or a place she chooses [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who fails to record a rape FIR commits an offence, punishable with 6 months to 2 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The danger in this table does not wait in a dark lane. It has a name, a phone number and, sometimes, a place at the family table. Safety advice has to start there.
rape-accused-known-to-survivor.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye. Inmein se 28,597 cases mein accused koi aisa aadmi tha jise survivor pehle se jaanti thi: 96.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sirf 939 cases mein accused unknown tha ya kabhi identify hi nahi hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh dono numbers National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ki annual report ki Table 3A.4 se hain, jo har rape case ko is hisaab se baantti hai ki accused ka survivor se kya rishta tha. "Dark lane" wale myth par hamari story poochhti hai ki curfews ki kya keemat hai. Yeh story khud us table ko kholti hai, ek-ek group karke.

## 29,536 mein se 28,597

Yeh table cases ginti hai, log nahi, aur sirf woh cases jo police ne register kiye. Har FIR ek hi baar gini jaati hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam par, isliye agar rape ke baad murder hua toh woh case rape count se bahar chala jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har 30 mein se ek se bhi kam case aakhri column mein gaya, jahan accused "unknown ya identify nahi hua" likha hai. Is column mein strangers aur woh aadmi saath gine jaate hain jinhe police kabhi trace hi nahi kar paayi.

Zyada tar survivors young adults thin: rape head mein record hue 29,742 victims mein se 19,489 ki umar 18 se 30 saal thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke saath hue zyada tar rape alag se, POCSO mein gine jaate hain, aur wahan bhi yahi pattern hai: 2024 mein POCSO ke penetrative sexual assault wale 96.6% cases mein accused bachche ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Child abusers par hamari story us table ko kholti hai.

## NCRB ki teen categories, andar se

NCRB jaan-pehchaan wale accused ko teen groups mein baantta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Accused kaun tha (NCRB ke words mein) | Cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Friends, online friends, "shaadi ke bahane" wale live-in partners, alag reh rahe husbands | 13,879 |
| Family friends, neighbours, employers, baaki jaan-pehchaan wale | 12,584 |
| Family members | 2,134 |
| Unknown ya identify nahi hua | 939 |
| Total rape cases | 29,536 |

**Friends aur partners, 13,879 cases.** Sabse bada group sabse zyada mixed bhi hai. Zabardasti karne wala boyfriend, shaadi ke baare mein jhooth bolne wala aadmi aur alag reh raha husband, sab ek saath gine jaate hain, aur NCRB is group mein se shaadi ke waade wale cases alag nahi kar sakta [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. July 2024 se dhokhe ke liye ek alag offence hai, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 69, jismein pehle chhe mahino mein 1,325 cases register hue, jaisa BNS ke pehle crime data par hamari explainer batati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Neighbours, family friends aur employers, 12,584 cases.** Yeh woh group hai jiski ghar tak access hai: aadmi jo ghar mein aate-jaate hain, naukri ya lift dete hain, aur jin par family bharosa karti hai. "Baaki jaan-pehchaan wale" mein kaun-kaun hai, NCRB yeh break down nahi karta.

**Family members, 2,134 cases.** Sabse chhota group. Yahan complaint ka matlab hai kisi relative par ungli uthana, jo shayad wahi aadmi ho jis par family paise, ghar ya samaaj mein naam ke liye tiki hai.

**Kaun missing hai.** Agar husband apni 18 saal ya usse badi wife ke saath zabardasti sex kare, toh woh is table mein kahin nahi hai, kyunki BNS ki Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki yeh rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Alag reh rahe husbands par ek alag offence, Section 67, mein case chal sakta hai, jismein 2 se 7 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur NCRB unhe friends-aur-partners wale group mein hi mila deta hai. Adult male survivors bhi gayab hain: Section 63 ke hisaab se rape sirf "a man" hi "a woman" ke saath kar sakta hai, isliye law ki nazar mein kisi adult aadmi ka rape ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Baarah saal, wahi pattern

In saalon mein in numbers ke neeche law badalta raha. 2013 mein Parliament ne rape ki legal definition wide ki [[indiacode-cla-2013]], aur 2024 mein IPC ki jagah BNS aa gaya. Phir bhi 2012 [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]], 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] aur 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]] ke NCRB figures lagbhag wahin ke wahin hain:

| Saal | Accused survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala |
|---|---|
| 2012 | 98.2% (24,915 mein se 24,470) |
| 2023 | 97.5% (29,670 mein se 28,915) |
| 2024 | 96.8% (29,536 mein se 28,597) |

States ke figures bhi yahi kehte hain. 2024 mein lagbhag har state aur union territory mein known share 90% se upar tha. Sabse kam Nagaland (78.6%), Meghalaya (78.9%), West Bengal (84.9%) aur Mizoram (85.0%) mein tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chhote numbers mein percentage bahut upar-neeche hota hai: Nagaland ka figure sirf 14 cases par tika hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. List mein sabse neeche bhi, lagbhag paanch mein se chaar cases mein accused jaan-pehchaan wala tha.

## Survey mein auraton ne kya bataya

Police tables sirf wahi dekhti hain jo police station tak pahunchta hai, aur zyada tar violence wahan tak pahunchti hi nahi. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77% auraton ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Survey ne auraton se ghar par poochha ki yeh kisne kiya, aur jawab police table se match karta hai. Jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi nahi hui thi aur jinhone sexual violence report kiya, unmein se sirf 5% ne stranger ka naam liya. Sabse common jawab the: father ya brother ke alawa doosre relatives (39%), current ya ex-boyfriend (16%) aur family friend (12%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh group chhota tha, isliye exact shares ko rough andaaza hi samjho. Jin ever-married auraton ne sexual violence jhela tha, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]], woh ek aadmi jise police table lagbhag kabhi nahi ginti.

Do alag tareeke, alag saal, alag definitions, ek hi jawab. Supreme Court ki judges ke liye bani 2023 ki handbook is soch ko galat stereotype batati hai ki rapists zyada tar strangers hote hain, aur saaf kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> "Very often men sexually assault or rape a woman known to them in some capacity."

## Data se match karti safety advice

Teen situations socho. Nagpur mein ek 23 saal ki ladki par ek aadmi dabaav daal raha hai ki woh uske flat par aaye; dono mahino se online baat kar rahe hain. Patna mein ek 20 saal ki ladki ko us dukaan ka maalik gher leta hai jahan woh kaam karti hai. Kochi mein ek 26 saal ki aurat ne apne chacha ke ghar jaana band kar diya hai aur wajah nahi bata paati. "Strangers se baat mat karo" in mein se kisi ke kaam ka nahi. Har koi table ke alag column mein hai aur har kisi ko alag cheez chahiye.

- **Partners aur online friends ke saath:** Section 63 ke hisaab se consent ek "unequivocal voluntary agreement" hai, aur agar aurat ne physically resist nahi kiya, toh sirf is wajah se use consent nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Chup rehna "haan" nahi hai, aur koi gift ya date "haan" nahi khareed sakti. Naye online contacts se pehli baar public jagah par milo, aur kisi ko batake jao.
- **Employers, neighbours aur family friends ke saath:** power aur access par nazar rakho, jaise kisi aise aadmi ke saath akele hona jiske haath mein tumhari salary, ghar ya family ka bharosa ho. Kuch "hone" se pehle hi kisi bharose wale ko bata dena overreaction nahi hai.
- **Family mein:** agar pehla reaction yakeen na karna ho, toh relative ka kiya abuse chhupa hi reh jaata hai. Pehle yakeen karo, poochho use kya chahiye, aur zabardasti aamna-saamna mat karwao.
- **Police station par:** har station ko rape complaint register karni hogi, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho; aurat ki complaint woman officer record karegi; aur uska statement uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par hi record hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo officer rape ki FIR darj nahi karta, woh khud offence karta hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Is table ka khatra kisi dark lane mein wait nahi karta. Uska ek naam hai, ek phone number hai, aur kabhi-kabhi ghar mein uski bhi thaali lagti hai. Safety advice wahin se shuru honi chahiye.

rape-capital-label-counts-versus-rates.en:
Every year, after the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) publishes *Crime in India*, headlines and forwards go looking for India's "rape capital". The title usually goes to the state with the biggest number. In 2024 that was Rajasthan, with 4,871 registered rape cases, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 3,209 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The label sounds like a finding. It rests on two mistakes: reading a count as a measure of danger, and reading police registration as a measure of crime.

## Where the 'rape capital' label comes from

NCRB publishes two numbers for every state. The count is the number of rape FIRs police registered. The rate divides that count by the state's female population and expresses it per lakh women. For India in 2024 the count was 29,536 and the rate 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The label almost always comes from the count, the bigger and starker number. But a count answers only one question: in which state did police write the most rape FIRs? It does not tell you where a woman is most at risk.

## Counts: the biggest states top the list

Rank states by count and the large states fill the top: Rajasthan (4,871), Uttar Pradesh (3,209), Maharashtra (3,091) and Madhya Pradesh (3,061) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A count grows with population. Uttar Pradesh has India's largest female population, so even a modest rate produces a big number: its rate was 2.8 per lakh women, below the national 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The same flip shows up across all crimes against women. Uttar Pradesh registered the most, 66,398 cases, yet its rate of 58.0 was below the national 64.6, while Delhi's 130.7 was the highest [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Rajasthan is the case that makes the label stick. Its 4,871 cases were 16.5% of India's total, at 12.2 per lakh women, nearly three times the national rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A high count and a high rate together look damning. They still describe complaints that reached the police, not all the rapes that happened.

Put counts and rates side by side and the order scrambles [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| | Rape cases, 2024 | Per lakh women |
|---|---|---|
| Rajasthan | 4,871 | 12.2 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 3,209 | 2.8 |
| Delhi | 1,058 | 10.3 |
| Chandigarh | 96 | 16.6 |
| Ladakh | 1 | 0.8 |
| All India | 29,536 | 4.3 |

## Rates: small territories jump up

Switch to rates and the top of the table changes: Chandigarh (16.6), Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2) and Delhi (10.3) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rates fix the population problem but bring two problems of their own.

First, small numbers swing. Chandigarh's top rate comes from 96 cases. Lakshadweep entered the top ten, at 6.7 per lakh women, on 2 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ladakh's single case made it the lowest, at 0.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In Lakshadweep, a single case moves the rate by more than three points, enough to jump several places in the table.

Second, states do not file the same crimes in the same row. Most child rape is recorded under the POCSO Act, not the rape head: only 784 of India's 29,536 rape cases involved girls under 18, against 43,313 POCSO cases of penetrative sexual assault on girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chandigarh, Goa and Himachal Pradesh file many child cases under rape instead; in Chandigarh, 47 of the 96 rape cases had victims under 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Their rape rates partly reflect a filing practice. At the other end, Tamil Nadu's rape rate of 1.1 is among India's lowest, yet its POCSO rate, 33.7 cases per lakh children from 6,969 cases, is among the highest of any state [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Cities add a third trap. Of the 19 big cities, Delhi registered the most rape cases, 1,058, and Jaipur had the highest rate, 34.2 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But city rates are still calculated on 2011 Census populations, and NCRB says they cannot be compared with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What NCRB says about rankings

NCRB prints its own warning with the data. Comparing states or districts on its figures alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided". More crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" than a city with less. And "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are "clearly two different things": numbers can rise because police open e-FIR facilities or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. NCRB also says it only compiles what state police send and is not responsible for the authenticity of that information [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

This is the trap inside the label. Picture two police stations. In one, a woman who reports rape finds a women's help desk and an officer who writes the FIR that day. In the other, she is told to settle it at home. Only the first station adds to its state's count and pushes it towards the "rape capital" headline. A label that rewards under-registration punishes exactly what survivors need from the police.

## A better question to ask

The useful question is not which state is worst, but what happens to a woman who reports there. Most women never reach a police station at all. In the National Family Health Survey 2019-21, 77% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone, and among those who did seek help, only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Every state's rape count is built on that thin slice.

So before trusting any ranking, check four things:

- whether it compares counts or rates per lakh women;
- how many cases sit behind a rate;
- whether the state files child rape under the rape head or under POCSO;
- what happened after the FIR: charge-sheets, completed trials, convictions.

A state that registers many complaints and takes them to court may be failing women less than one with a small, quiet number. The words "rape capital" answer none of these questions.
rape-capital-label-counts-versus-rates.hg:
Har saal jab National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) *Crime in India* chhapta hai, headlines aur forwards India ki "rape capital" dhoondhne lagte hain. Yeh title aksar us state ko milta hai jiska number sabse bada ho. 2024 mein woh Rajasthan tha, 4,871 registered rape cases ke saath, aur uske baad Uttar Pradesh, 3,209 cases ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Label sunne mein kisi research ka nateeja lagta hai. Asal mein yeh do galtiyon par khada hai: count ko khatre ka naap samajhna, aur police registration ko crime ka naap samajhna.

## 'Rape capital' label aata kahan se hai

NCRB har state ke liye do numbers chhapta hai. Count ka matlab hai ki police ne rape ki kitni FIRs register kin. Rate us count ko state ki female population se divide karta hai aur use har lakh auraton par dikhata hai. 2024 mein poore India ka count 29,536 tha aur rate 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Label lagbhag hamesha count se aata hai, kyunki woh bada aur zyada chaunkane wala number hai. Lekin count sirf ek sawaal ka jawab deta hai: kis state mein police ne rape ki sabse zyada FIRs likhin? Woh yeh nahi batata ki aurat ko sabse zyada khatra kahan hai.

## Count: bade states list mein upar

States ko count se rank karo toh upar bade states hi dikhte hain: Rajasthan (4,871), Uttar Pradesh (3,209), Maharashtra (3,091) aur Madhya Pradesh (3,061) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Count population ke saath badhta hai. Uttar Pradesh mein India ki sabse badi female population hai, isliye wahan chhota rate bhi bada number bana deta hai: uska rate har lakh auraton par 2.8 tha, jo national 4.3 se kam hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Auraton ke khilaf saare crimes mein bhi yahi ulat-pher dikhta hai. Uttar Pradesh mein sabse zyada, 66,398 cases register hue, phir bhi uska rate 58.0 national 64.6 se kam tha, jabki Delhi ka 130.7 sabse ooncha tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Rajasthan woh case hai jiski wajah se yeh label chipak jaata hai. Uske 4,871 cases India ke total ka 16.5% the, aur rate tha har lakh auraton par 12.2, yaani national rate ka lagbhag teen guna [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bada count aur ooncha rate saath mein bahut bura dikhte hain. Phir bhi yeh un complaints ki baat karte hain jo police tak pahunchin, un sab rapes ki nahi jo hue.

Count aur rate ko saath rakho toh order bikhar jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| | Rape cases, 2024 | Har lakh auraton par |
|---|---|---|
| Rajasthan | 4,871 | 12.2 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 3,209 | 2.8 |
| Delhi | 1,058 | 10.3 |
| Chandigarh | 96 | 16.6 |
| Ladakh | 1 | 0.8 |
| Poora India | 29,536 | 4.3 |

## Rate: chhote territories upar uchhal jaate hain

Rate par jao toh table ka top badal jaata hai: Chandigarh (16.6), Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2) aur Delhi (10.3) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rate population wali problem toh theek kar deta hai, lekin apni do problems saath le aata hai.

Pehli, chhote numbers bahut hilte hain. Chandigarh ka top rate sirf 96 cases se bana hai. Lakshadweep sirf 2 cases par top ten mein aa gaya, har lakh auraton par 6.7 ke rate ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ladakh ka ek akela case use sabse neeche le aaya, 0.8 par [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lakshadweep mein ek case rate ko teen points se zyada hila deta hai, jo table mein kai jagah upar-neeche hone ke liye kaafi hai.

Doosri, states ek hi crime ko ek hi row mein darj nahi karte. Bachchon ke rape ke zyada tar cases POCSO Act mein darj hote hain, rape head mein nahi: India ke 29,536 rape cases mein se sirf 784 mein 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyan thin, jabki ladkiyon par penetrative sexual assault ke POCSO cases 43,313 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chandigarh, Goa aur Himachal Pradesh bachchon ke kai cases POCSO ki jagah rape mein darj karte hain; Chandigarh ke 96 rape cases mein se 47 mein victims 18 se kam umar ki thin [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unke rape rates kuch had tak isi filing ke tareeke ka nateeja hain. Doosri taraf, Tamil Nadu ka rape rate 1.1 India ke sabse kam rates mein hai, lekin uska POCSO rate, 6,969 cases se har lakh bachchon par 33.7, kisi bhi state ke sabse oonche rates mein hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Cities ek teesra jaal bichhati hain. 19 bade shehron mein sabse zyada rape cases Delhi mein register hue, 1,058, aur sabse ooncha rate Jaipur ka tha, har lakh auraton par 34.2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin cities ke rates abhi bhi 2011 Census ki population se nikalte hain, aur NCRB kehta hai ki inhe state rates se compare nahi kiya ja sakta [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Rankings par NCRB khud kya kehta hai

NCRB data ke saath apni warning khud chhapta hai. Uske figures par states ya districts ko compare karna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided", yaani bahut simplistic hoga aur isse bachna chahiye. Kisi shehar mein zyada crime register hona "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", yaani is baat ka saboot nahi ki woh kam crime wale shehar se zyada unsafe hai. Aur "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" "clearly two different things" hain: e-FIR facility ya women help desks khulne se bhi numbers badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. NCRB yeh bhi kehta hai ki woh sirf state police ka bheja data jodta hai, aur us information ke sahi hone ki zimmedari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Label ke andar ka jaal yahi hai. Do police stations socho. Ek mein rape report karne aayi aurat ko women help desk milta hai, aur ek officer jo usi din FIR likh deta hai. Doosre mein use kaha jaata hai ki maamla ghar par hi suljha lo. State ke count mein sirf pehle station ka case judta hai, aur wahi state ko "rape capital" wali headline ki taraf dhakelta hai. Jo label kam registration ko inaam deta hai, woh theek usi cheez ko saza deta hai jiski survivors ko police se zaroorat hai.

## Ek behtar sawaal

Kaam ka sawaal yeh nahi ki sabse bura state kaun sa hai, balki yeh ki wahan report karne wali aurat ke saath kya hota hai. Zyada tar auratein police station tak pahunchti hi nahi. National Family Health Survey 2019-21 mein 18-49 saal ki jin auraton ne physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, unmein se 77% ne kabhi madad nahi maangi ya kisi ko bataya tak nahi, aur jinhone madad maangi unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Har state ka rape count isi patli si parat par khada hai.

Isliye kisi bhi ranking par bharosa karne se pehle chaar cheezein check karo:

- woh count compare kar rahi hai ya har lakh auraton ka rate;
- rate ke peeche kitne cases hain;
- state bachchon ke rape ko rape head mein darj karta hai ya POCSO mein;
- FIR ke baad kya hua: chargesheets, poore hue trials, convictions.

Jo state zyada complaints darj karta hai aur unhe court tak le jaata hai, woh shayad auraton ko us state se kam fail kar raha ho jiska number chhota aur khamosh hai. "Rape capital" ke do shabd in mein se kisi bhi sawaal ka jawab nahi dete.

rape-case-justice-funnel.en:
Every rape case in India has to pass four gates: a police station that registers it, an investigation that ends in a charge-sheet, a court queue, and a verdict. In 2024, police registered 29,536 rape cases and courts convicted in 5,032 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It is tempting to divide one by the other. Don't: they are not the same cases. What the figures do show is where cases stall and leak, gate by gate.

| Rape cases in India, 2024 | Number |
|---|---|
| FIRs registered by police | 29,536 |
| Charge-sheeted by police | 24,614 |
| Before the courts, new and old | 2,06,777 |
| Trials completed | 20,587 |
| Ended in conviction | 5,032 |
| Still pending trial at year-end | 1,85,785 |

Each row is a separate flow of cases in 2024, not one group followed through [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Stage one: the FIR

Police registered 29,536 rape cases in 2024, involving 29,742 women and girls, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yet a 2022 peer-reviewed study cited estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence in India report it to the authorities [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone, and of those who did seek help, only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

This funnel follows the rape head only. Most rape of girls under 18 is filed under the POCSO Act, and because NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, a rape that ends in murder may be counted only as murder [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Reaching this gate is a right. A complaint can be made at any police station, wherever the crime happened (a Zero FIR), or electronically, and the victim must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A police officer who refuses to record a rape FIR faces six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Stage two: investigation

In 2024, police disposed of 30,272 rape cases, including some from earlier years. They filed charge-sheets in 24,614, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. They closed 3,776 with a final report calling the case false, 714 as a mistake of fact or law or a civil dispute, and 1,044 as true but with insufficient evidence or the accused untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At the end of the year, 8,905 cases were still under investigation.

"False" is a police label, not a court finding. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) gives police two months to finish a rape investigation, sets no consequence for missing that deadline, and entitles the victim to an update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Stage three: the courtroom queue

Every charge-sheet sends a case to court, where it joins a queue. In 2024 Indian courts had 2,06,777 rape cases before them, new and old. By the end of the year, 1,85,785 were still pending: a pendency of 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The queue keeps growing. At the end of 2018, 1,38,642 rape cases were pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. In 2024, police charge-sheeted 24,614 cases while courts completed 20,587 trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Arrivals outpace verdicts, so everyone in line waits longer.

The law promises otherwise: a rape trial is meant to finish within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. With nearly nine in ten cases still waiting at the end of the year, that deadline describes almost nobody's trial.

Consider a hypothetical. A 23-year-old in Indore files a complaint against a colleague, and police charge-sheet him on time. Her case joins a national list of more than two lakh, and when it is heard depends less on her evidence than on how many cases sit ahead of hers. Each year of waiting, witnesses move away, memories blur and pressure to "settle" builds.

## Stage four: the verdict

Courts completed 20,587 rape trials in 2024. They convicted in 5,032 cases and acquitted in 13,980; the rest were discharged. The conviction rate was 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It was higher when the victim was a girl under 18, at 31.4%, than when she was an adult woman, at 23.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

An acquittal means guilt was not proved beyond reasonable doubt, not that a complaint was false. And the 5,032 count cases, not convicted people.

Now the cohort problem. Trials that ended in 2024 include cases charge-sheeted years earlier, so the 5,032 convictions are not a slice of 2024's 29,536 FIRs. The honest single-year figure is the one NCRB publishes: convictions as a share of trials completed.

## Where the funnel leaks most

Put the stages together and three leaks stand out. The first and largest comes before the FIR: most survivors never reach a police station at all. The second is time: at the end of 2024, 1,85,785 cases were waiting, against 20,587 trials completed in the whole year. The third is the verdict, where fewer than one in four completed trials ended in conviction.

For a survivor, no single rate captures this. What matters is how few cases reach the end at all, and how long the ones that do take. Some help does not have to wait for the end. A survivor can apply for compensation to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the accused is never traced and no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under NALSA's 2018 model scheme, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
rape-case-justice-funnel.hg:
India mein har rape case ko chaar gates se guzarna padta hai: police station jo use register kare, investigation jo charge-sheet par khatam ho, court ki line, aur verdict. 2024 mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye aur courts ne 5,032 cases mein saza di [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek number ko doosre se divide karne ka mann karta hai. Mat kijiye: yeh same cases nahi hain.
