Yeh figures jo dikhati hain, woh yeh hai ki cases kahan atakte hain aur kahan se nikal jaate hain, gate by gate.

| India mein rape cases, 2024 | Number |
|---|---|
| Police ne FIR register ki | 29,536 |
| Police ne charge-sheet file ki | 24,614 |
| Courts ke saamne, naye aur purane | 2,06,777 |
| Trials poore hue | 20,587 |
| Saza hui | 5,032 |
| Saal ke end mein trial ke intezaar mein | 1,85,785 |

Har row 2024 mein cases ka ek alag flow hai, shuru se ant tak follow kiya gaya ek hi group nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Stage one: FIR

2024 mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye, jinmein 29,742 auratein aur ladkiyan thi, yaani har ek lakh auraton par 4.3 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi 2022 ki ek peer-reviewed study ne un estimates ka hawala diya jinke mutabik India mein sexual violence ke sirf lagbhag 1% victims authorities ko report karte hain [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya; aur jinhone madad maangi, unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh funnel sirf rape head ko follow karta hai. 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke zyadatar rape cases POCSO Act ke tahat darj hote hain, aur kyunki NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar, uske sabse serious offence ke naam par ginta hai, murder par khatam hua rape sirf murder ke roop mein gina ja sakta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Is gate tak pahunchna aapka haq hai. Complaint kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR), ya electronically, aur victim ko FIR ki copy free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo police officer rape ki FIR darj karne se mana kare, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Stage two: investigation

2024 mein police ne rape ke 30,272 cases dispose kiye, jinmein kuch pichhle saalon ke bhi the. Inmein se 24,614 mein charge-sheet file hui, yaani charge-sheeting rate 81.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 3,776 cases ko final report mein "false" bata kar band kiya gaya, 714 ko mistake of fact ya law ya civil dispute bata kar, aur 1,044 ko "true" maante hue bhi saboot kam hone ya accused ka pata na chalne ki wajah se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Saal ke end mein 8,905 cases ki investigation ab bhi chal rahi thi.

"False" police ka label hai, court ka faisla nahi. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) police ko rape investigation poori karne ke liye do mahine deti hai, deadline miss hone par koi consequence tay nahi karti, aur victim ko 90 din ke andar update paane ka haq deti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Stage three: court ki line

Har charge-sheet ek case ko court bhejti hai, jahan woh line mein lag jaata hai. 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne rape ke 2,06,777 cases the, naye aur purane milakar. Saal ke end tak 1,85,785 ab bhi pending the: yaani pendency 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Line lambi hoti ja rahi hai. 2018 ke end mein rape ke 1,38,642 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. 2024 mein police ne 24,614 cases charge-sheet kiye, jabki courts ne 20,587 trials poore kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jitne cases aate hain, utne faisle nahi hote, isliye line mein khade har insaan ka intezaar lamba hota jaata hai.

Kanoon ka waada kuch aur hai: rape trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jab saal ke end mein lagbhag das mein se nau cases ab bhi intezaar mein hon, to yeh deadline lagbhag kisi ke trial par laagu nahi hoti.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Indore ki ek 23 saal ki ladki apne colleague ke khilaaf complaint karti hai, aur police time par charge-sheet file kar deti hai. Uska case do lakh se zyada cases ki national list mein jud jaata hai, aur uski sunwai kab hogi, yeh uske saboot se kam aur is baat se zyada tay hota hai ki uske aage kitne cases hain. Intezaar ke har saal mein gawah door chale jaate hain, yaadein dhundhli hoti hain aur "settle" karne ka dabav badhta hai.

## Stage four: verdict

2024 mein courts ne rape ke 20,587 trials poore kiye. 5,032 cases mein saza hui aur 13,980 mein acquittal; baaki discharge hue. Conviction rate 24.4% raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab victim 18 se kam umar ki ladki thi, tab yeh 31.4% tha, aur jab adult aurat thi, tab 23.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Acquittal ka matlab hai ki guilt "beyond reasonable doubt" saabit nahi hua, yeh nahi ki complaint jhoothi thi. Aur 5,032 cases ki ginti hai, saza paane wale logon ki nahi.

Ab cohort wali problem. 2024 mein khatam hue trials mein woh cases bhi hain jinki charge-sheet saalon pehle file hui thi, isliye 5,032 convictions 2024 ki 29,536 FIRs ka hissa nahi hain. Imaandaar single-year figure wahi hai jo NCRB publish karta hai: poore hue trials mein se kitno mein saza hui.

## Funnel sabse zyada kahan leak hota hai

Saare stages ko saath rakhiye, to teen leaks saaf dikhte hain. Pehla aur sabse bada FIR se pehle hai: zyadatar survivors kabhi police station tak pahunchte hi nahi. Doosra hai waqt: 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 cases intezaar mein the, jabki poore saal mein 20,587 trials poore hue. Teesra hai verdict, jahan poore hue trials mein se chaar mein ek se bhi kam mein saza hui.

Survivor ke liye koi ek rate yeh sab nahi dikhata. Asli baat yeh hai ki kitne kam cases ant tak pahunchte hain, aur jo pahunchte hain unhe kitna waqt lagta hai. Kuch madad ke liye ant tak rukna zaroori nahi. Survivor State ya District Legal Services Authority ko compensation ke liye apply kar sakti hai, chahe accused kabhi na mile aur trial kabhi na ho, aur authority ko do mahine mein apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 ki model scheme mein rape survivor Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh tak ki hakdaar hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

rape-investigations-past-two-month-deadl.en:
Consider a 24-year-old in Lucknow who reports a rape at her local police station on 1 March. The moment the officer records her information, a legal clock starts. Under Section 193(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the investigation must be completed within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]: by 1 May. Nothing in the law says what happens if it is not. At the end of 2024, police across India still had 8,905 rape cases under investigation [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This is what happens between the FIR and the charge-sheet, and where cases stall before any court sees them.

## From FIR to charge-sheet

The first steps carry short deadlines of their own. Information from a woman about rape must be recorded by a woman officer, and she must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. With her consent, she must be sent for a medical examination within 24 hours, and the doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within seven days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A magistrate, a woman wherever practicable, must record her statement as soon as police learn of the offence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. And police cannot summon her: an investigating officer cannot require a woman to come anywhere other than the place where she lives [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Then comes the slower work: forensic results, tracing and questioning the accused, witness statements, phone records. It ends in one of two documents. A charge-sheet sends the case to court. A closure report, which NCRB calls a "final report", ends it at the police stage.

## 81.3%: what the charge-sheeting rate measures

In 2024 police disposed of 30,272 rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. They filed charge-sheets in 24,614, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. They closed 3,776 with a final report calling the case false, 714 as a mistake of fact or law or a civil dispute, and 1,044 as true but with insufficient evidence or the accused untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Three cautions. First, "false" is a closure label given by police at the investigation stage. It is not a court's finding, and it cannot be read as the share of complaints proven false [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Second, the rate says nothing about how strong a charge-sheet is. A thin one filed on time can still collapse at trial, where only 24.4% of completed rape trials ended in conviction in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Third, and least understood: the rate is calculated only on the cases police have finished with [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Files still open are left out entirely. A police force that leaves its hardest cases open can still report a high charge-sheeting rate.

## 8,905 cases still under investigation

Those open files are the 8,905 rape cases still under investigation at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], more than one in five of all the rape cases police had to investigate that year.

Not every open file is late. A case registered in mid-December was only days old on 31 December. But any case registered before November and still open at the end of the year had already run past the legal deadline. The NCRB year-end figure counts how many files are open, not how long each has been open, so it cannot show how many investigations meet the two-month rule.

The same deadline covers penetrative and other sexual assault on children of any sex under POCSO [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. At the end of 2024, 21,256 POCSO cases were still under investigation, 23.7% of those police had to investigate [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## A deadline with no penalty

Before 2018 only investigations into the rape of a child had a target, of three months, and the law said only that they "may" be completed in that time [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 made it two months for every rape investigation, and changed the word to "shall" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. The BNSS carried the rule into Section 193(2) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], in force from 1 July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

"Shall" sounds absolute. But the law attaches no consequence to missing the deadline [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Compare that with the step before. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape faces six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment under Section 199 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The law punishes the officer who refuses to open the file. It does nothing to the one who leaves it open.

One state has answered with a shorter deadline. West Bengal's Aparajita Bill, reserved for the President in September 2024, proposed cutting the investigation deadline from two months to 21 days, extendable by 15 [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. A shorter deadline with no consequence is still a deadline with no consequence.

## What a survivor can demand

While the investigation runs, the law gives a survivor specific rights.

- **A progress report within 90 days.** Police must tell the informant or the victim how the investigation is going within 90 days, by any means including electronic communication [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ask in writing, and keep a copy.
- **Questioning where she lives.** She may choose to go to the police station, but she cannot be required to [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Her documents.** A free copy of the FIR at the start [[indiacode-bnss-2023]] and, if she has a lawyer, free copies of the police report and statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance in court [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A hearing before the case is dropped.** No court may allow the prosecution to be withdrawn without hearing the victim [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Compensation that does not wait for a charge-sheet.** She can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

This is general information, not legal advice; a lawyer from the District Legal Services Authority can help a survivor use these rights. Two months is the law's own measure of a reasonable rape investigation. Holding police to it starts with knowing the date it runs out.
rape-investigations-past-two-month-deadl.hg:
Socho, Lucknow ki ek 24 saal ki ladki 1 March ko apne local police station mein rape report karti hai. Jis pal officer uski information record karta hai, ek legal ghadi chalne lagti hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 193(2) ke tehat investigation do mahine ke andar poori honi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]: yaani 1 May tak. Agar nahi hui toh kya hoga, is par law kuch nahi kehta. 2024 ke end mein poore India mein police ke paas 8,905 rape cases ab bhi investigation mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. FIR aur charge-sheet ke beech kya hota hai, aur court tak pahunchne se pehle cases kahan atakte hain, yeh uski kahani hai.

## FIR se charge-sheet tak

Shuru ke steps ki apni chhoti deadlines hain. Rape ke baare mein kisi aurat ki di hui information ek woman officer record karegi, aur use FIR ki free copy milegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Uski consent se, use 24 ghante ke andar medical examination ke liye bhejna hoga, aur doctor ko saat din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ek magistrate, jahan tak ho sake woman magistrate, police ko offence ka pata chalte hi uska bayaan record karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur police use bula nahi sakti: investigating officer kisi aurat ko uske rehne ki jagah ke alawa kahin aur aane ke liye majboor nahi kar sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Phir aata hai dheema kaam: forensic results, accused ko dhoondhna aur usse poochhtaachh, gawahon ke bayaan, phone records. Iska ant do mein se ek document se hota hai. Charge-sheet case ko court bhejti hai. Closure report, jise NCRB "final report" kehta hai, case ko police ke level par hi khatam kar deti hai.

## 81.3%: charge-sheeting rate kya naapta hai

2024 mein police ne 30,272 rape cases dispose kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unme se 24,614 mein charge-sheet file hui, yaani charge-sheeting rate 81.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 3,776 cases ko final report mein "false" bata ke band kiya gaya, 714 ko mistake of fact ya law ya civil dispute bata ke, aur 1,044 ko yeh keh ke ki case sach hai lekin saboot kam hain ya accused ka pata nahi chala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Teen savdhaaniyaan. Pehli, "false" police ka closure label hai jo investigation ke stage par diya jaata hai. Yeh court ka faisla nahi hai, aur ise is baat ka hissa nahi maana ja sakta ki kitni complaints jhoothi saabit hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosri, yeh rate nahi batata ki charge-sheet kitni mazboot hai. Time par file hui kamzor charge-sheet bhi trial mein gir sakti hai, jahan 2024 mein poore hue rape trials mein se sirf 24.4% conviction par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Teesri, jo sabse kam samjhi jaati hai: yeh rate sirf un cases par nikala jaata hai jinka kaam police khatam kar chuki hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo files ab bhi khuli hain, woh isme aati hi nahi. Jo police force apne sabse mushkil cases khule chhod de, woh bhi high charge-sheeting rate dikha sakti hai.

## 8,905 cases ab bhi investigation mein

Yahi khuli files hain: 2024 ke end mein 8,905 rape cases ab bhi investigation mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani us saal police ke paas investigation ke liye aaye saare rape cases mein se paanch mein ek se zyada.

Har khuli file late nahi hai. Mid-December mein register hua case 31 December ko sirf kuch din purana tha. Lekin jo case November se pehle register hua aur saal ke end tak khula raha, woh legal deadline paar kar chuka tha. NCRB ka saal ke end ka figure yeh ginta hai ki kitni files khuli hain, yeh nahi ki har file kitne time se khuli hai, isliye usse yeh pata nahi chal sakta ki kitni investigations do mahine ka rule poora karti hain.

Yahi deadline POCSO ke tehat kisi bhi gender ke bachche ke saath hue penetrative aur doosre sexual assault par bhi laagu hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 2024 ke end mein POCSO ke 21,256 cases ab bhi investigation mein the, yaani police ke paas investigation ke liye aaye cases ka 23.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Deadline hai, penalty nahi

2018 se pehle sirf bachchon ke rape ki investigation ka ek target tha, teen mahine ka, aur law bas itna kehta tha ki investigation us time mein poori "ho sakti hai" ("may") [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne ise har rape investigation ke liye do mahine kar diya, aur shabd badal ke "hogi" ("shall") kar diya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. BNSS ne yeh rule Section 193(2) mein le liya [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

"Shall" sunne mein pakka lagta hai. Lekin deadline miss hone par law koi consequence tay nahi karta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ab isse pehle wale step se compare karo. Jo police officer rape ki FIR record nahi karta, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 199 ke tehat chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Law us officer ko saza deta hai jo file kholne se mana karta hai. Jo file ko khula chhod deta hai, uska kuch nahi bigadta.

Ek state ne iska jawab chhoti deadline se diya hai. West Bengal ka Aparajita Bill, jise September 2024 mein President ke vichaar ke liye reserve kiya gaya, investigation ki deadline do mahine se ghata ke 21 din karna chahta tha, jise 15 din aur badhaya ja sake [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. Bina consequence ki chhoti deadline bhi bina consequence ki deadline hi hai.

## Survivor kya maang sakti hai

Jab tak investigation chal rahi hai, law survivor ko kuch saaf rights deta hai.

- **90 din mein progress report.** Police ko 90 din ke andar informant ya victim ko batana hoga ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi, kisi bhi tareeke se, electronic communication samet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Likhit mein maango, aur copy rakho.
- **Poochhtaachh wahin, jahan woh rehti hai.** Woh chaahe toh police station ja sakti hai, lekin use jaane par majboor nahi kiya ja sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Uske documents.** Shuru mein FIR ki free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], aur agar uska lawyer hai, toh accused ke court mein pehli baar pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar police report aur statements ki free copies [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Case wapas lene se pehle sunwaai.** Koi bhi court victim ki baat sune bina prosecution wapas lene ki ijaazat nahi de sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Compensation jo charge-sheet ka wait nahi karta.** Woh State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi na mile aur trial kabhi na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi; District Legal Services Authority ka lawyer survivor ko in rights ka istemaal karne mein madad kar sakta hai. Do mahine law ka apna paimaana hai ki rape ki ek theek-thaak investigation mein kitna time lagna chahiye. Police ko is deadline se baandhne ki shuruaat yeh jaanne se hoti hai ki woh date kab khatam ho rahi hai.

rape-is-not-big-city-problem.en:
India's most remembered rape cases carry city names: Delhi in 2012, Shakti Mills in Mumbai in 2013, RG Kar Medical College in Kolkata in 2024. They led to new laws and Supreme Court orders, and they left behind a picture of rape as a big-city danger. The police record does not support that picture. In 2024, India's 19 metropolitan cities registered 3,886 rape cases. The whole country registered 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The myth of the dangerous city

The myth has two halves. The first says rape belongs to the city: crowds, strangers, late nights. The second follows from it: keep a woman away from the city and she is safe. It shapes real decisions: a college seat in another city turned down, a job refused because the shift ends after dark. Rarely does anyone ask the same questions about the uncle, the neighbour or the husband at home.

Distance from a city is no measure of safety. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, the offender was someone the victim knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A pin code does not change who that person is.

## 3,886 out of 29,536

The 19 metros registered roughly one in eight of India's rape cases in 2024; nearly seven in eight came from everywhere else. Delhi alone accounted for 1,058, or 27.2% of the metro total, followed by Jaipur (497), Mumbai (411) and Hyderabad (358) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Child sexual abuse cases follow the same pattern: the metros registered 7,508 POCSO cases with girl victims out of 67,809 across India, about one in nine [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Know what the metro table covers. NCRB collects data for 53 cities that had more than 10 lakh people at the 2011 Census, but prints tables only for the 19 above 20 lakh; the other 34 appear only on its website [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. City rates use 2011 populations, so NCRB says they cannot be compared with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

None of this makes cities safe. Jaipur recorded the highest registered rape rate of the 19 metros, 34.2 per lakh women. Low numbers mislead too: Kolkata registered 12 rape cases and Chennai 44 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB itself warns that more registered crime in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A registered case measures who reached a police station, and whether the police wrote it down.

## Where the other cases are

Rajasthan registered the most rape cases of any state in 2024, 4,871, followed by Uttar Pradesh (3,209), Maharashtra (3,091) and Madhya Pradesh (3,061) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rajasthan alone accounted for 16.5% of India's total, at 12.2 cases per lakh women, nearly three times the national rate of 4.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jaipur, the state's only city in the printed metro table, registered 497 of those cases: about one in ten. In Madhya Pradesh, Indore, again the only printed metro, registered 195 of 3,061 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The rest came from smaller cities, district towns and villages; the printed report does not split them.

Consider how one of those cases begins. A woman in a Madhya Pradesh village is raped by a man from her own lane. The police station is several villages away. His family lives a few houses from hers. There is no camera crew, no candle march, no hashtag. If she reports at all, her case becomes one line in a state total.

## What the household surveys add

The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) goes door to door, in villages and cities alike. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 6% of women aged 18-49 said they had ever experienced sexual violence [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The survey points the same way as the police data: towards home, not the dark street. Among ever-married women who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Violence by husbands is also reported more often in villages: 24.4% of ever-married women in rural India and 17.5% in urban India reported physical or sexual violence by a husband in NFHS-6 (2023-24, provisional) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. And most women tell no one: 77% of those who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Why coverage follows cities

National newsrooms sit in the big cities, and so does the data: each metro gets a printed table; a district town or village gets none. Small-town cases do break through, but the best-known ones carried something more: a legislator as the accused in Unnao in 2017, later sentenced to life [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]; policemen convicted of destroying evidence in Kathua in 2018 [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]; a cremation by police in the middle of the night in Hathras in 2020 [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Money follows the same map. The Nirbhaya Fund's largest scheme, Safe City, covers eight cities: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow and Mumbai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. By July 2026, according to a Rajya Sabha reply, it had received Rs 1,686.73 crore, against Rs 1,299.10 crore for One Stop Centres and Rs 1,234.55 crore for fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases; together these three schemes took 63% of all the money released. The same reply listed a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men as "ongoing" with zero spending; CCTV cameras for village panchayats were still awaiting financial approval [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Wherever a survivor lives, she can report at any police station, whatever the area of the offence, and must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. As of July 2026, 985 One Stop Centres were operational [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]; in 2018 the Supreme Court asked for at least one in every district [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. When the next city case trends, ask what happened in your own district that month, and who there heard about it.
rape-is-not-big-city-problem.hg:
India ke sabse zyada yaad kiye jaane wale rape cases ke saath shehron ke naam jude hain: 2012 mein Delhi, 2013 mein Mumbai ka Shakti Mills, 2024 mein Kolkata ka RG Kar Medical College. In cases ke baad naye kaanoon aur Supreme Court ke orders aaye, aur saath hi logon ke mann mein ek tasveer chhod di ki rape bade shehron ka khatra hai. Police ka record is tasveer ka saath nahi deta. 2024 mein India ke 19 metropolitan cities mein 3,886 rape cases darj hue. Poore desh mein 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Khatarnaak shehar ka myth

Is myth ke do hisse hain. Pehla kehta hai ki rape shehar ki cheez hai: bheed, ajnabi, der raat. Doosra isi se nikalta hai: aurat ko shehar se door rakho, woh safe rahegi. Yeh soch asli zindagi ke faisle tay karti hai: doosre shehar ke college ki seat chhod di jaati hai, naukri se mana kar diya jaata hai kyunki shift andhera hone ke baad khatam hoti hai. Lekin ghar ke chacha, padosi ya pati ke baare mein yahi sawaal shayad hi koi poochta hai.

Shehar se doori safety ka paimaana nahi hai. 2024 mein India mein darj 96.8% rape cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Pin code badalne se woh insaan nahi badalta.

## 29,536 mein se 3,886

2024 mein India ke har aath rape cases mein se lagbhag ek 19 metros mein darj hua; har aath mein se lagbhag saat baaki jagahon se aaye. Akele Delhi mein 1,058 cases the, yaani metros ke total ka 27.2%. Uske baad Jaipur (497), Mumbai (411) aur Hyderabad (358) the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Child sexual abuse ke cases mein bhi yahi pattern hai: metros mein girl victims wale 7,508 POCSO cases darj hue, jabki poore India mein 67,809, yaani lagbhag nau mein se ek [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Samajh lijiye ki metro table mein kya aata hai. NCRB un 53 shehron ka data ikattha karta hai jinki aabaadi 2011 Census mein 10 lakh se zyada thi, lekin tables sirf 20 lakh se upar wale 19 shehron ki chhaapta hai; baaki 34 sirf uski website par milte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Shehron ke rates 2011 ki aabaadi par nikaale jaate hain, isliye NCRB kehta hai ki inhe state rates se compare nahi kiya ja sakta [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki shehar safe hain. 19 metros mein Jaipur ka registered rape rate sabse zyada tha, har lakh auraton par 34.2. Kam numbers bhi gumraah karte hain: Kolkata mein sirf 12 rape cases darj hue aur Chennai mein 44 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB khud chetaavni deta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada registered crime "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", yaani is baat ka saboot nahi ki woh shehar doosron se zyada asurakshit hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Registered case yeh naapta hai ki kaun police station tak pahuncha, aur police ne uski baat likhi ya nahi.

## Baaki cases kahan hain

2024 mein Rajasthan mein kisi bhi state se zyada, 4,871 rape cases darj hue. Uske baad Uttar Pradesh (3,209), Maharashtra (3,091) aur Madhya Pradesh (3,061) the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Akele Rajasthan mein India ke total ka 16.5% tha, yaani har lakh auraton par 12.2 cases, jo national rate 4.3 ka lagbhag teen guna hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Printed metro table mein Rajasthan ka sirf ek shehar hai, Jaipur, aur wahan inmein se 497 cases darj hue: lagbhag das mein se ek. Madhya Pradesh mein bhi sirf Indore printed metro hai, aur wahan state ke 3,061 mein se 195 cases darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Baaki cases chhote shehron, district towns aur gaon se aaye; printed report inhe alag-alag nahi batati.

Sochiye ki inmein se ek case kaise shuru hota hai. Madhya Pradesh ke ek gaon mein ek aurat ka rape uski hi gali ka ek aadmi karta hai. Police station kai gaon door hai. Us aadmi ki family uske ghar se bas kuch ghar door rehti hai. Na koi camera crew, na candle march, na hashtag. Agar woh report karti bhi hai, toh uska case state ke total mein bas ek line ban jaata hai.

## Household surveys kya jodte hain

National Family Health Survey (NFHS) ghar-ghar jaata hai, gaon mein bhi aur shehar mein bhi. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18-49 saal ki 6% auraton ne kaha ki unhone kabhi na kabhi sexual violence jheli hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Survey bhi wahi dikhata hai jo police data: khatra ghar ke andar hai, andheri sadak par nahi. Sexual violence jhel chuki ever-married auraton mein se 82% ne apne maujooda pati ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Pati ki hinsa bhi gaon mein zyada report hoti hai: NFHS-6 (2023-24, provisional) mein rural India ki 24.4% aur urban India ki 17.5% ever-married auraton ne pati ki taraf se physical ya sexual violence report ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Aur zyada tar auratein kisi ko nahi batatin: physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Coverage shehron ke peeche kyun chalti hai

National newsrooms bade shehron mein baithe hain, aur data bhi wahin hai: har metro ki apni printed table hai; district town ya gaon ki koi nahi. Chhote shehron aur gaon ke cases bhi national news bante hain, lekin sabse mashhoor cases mein kuch aur bhi tha: 2017 ke Unnao case mein accused ek MLA tha, jise baad mein umrqaid ki sazaa hui [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]; 2018 ke Kathua case mein policewalon ko saboot mitane ka doshi paaya gaya [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]; 2020 mein Hathras mein police ne aadhi raat ko antim sanskar kar diya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Paisa bhi isi naqshe par chalta hai. Nirbhaya Fund ki sabse badi scheme, Safe City, aath shehron ke liye hai: Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow aur Mumbai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Rajya Sabha ke ek jawaab ke mutaabik July 2026 tak ise Rs 1,686.73 crore mile the, jabki One Stop Centres ko Rs 1,299.10 crore aur rape aur POCSO cases ke fast-track courts ko Rs 1,234.55 crore; in teen schemes ko milakar release hue kul paise ka 63% mila. Usi jawaab mein mardon ko sensitise karne wala ek Panchayati Raj programme "ongoing" bataya gaya, jis par zero kharch hua tha; aur gaon ki panchayaton mein CCTV cameras lagane ka plan ab bhi financial approval ka intezaar kar raha tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Survivor kahin bhi rehti ho, woh kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hai, crime chahe kisi bhi ilaake mein hua ho, aur police ko use FIR ki copy free mein deni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. July 2026 tak 985 One Stop Centres chalu the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]; 2018 mein Supreme Court ne har district mein kam se kam ek centre banane ko kaha tha [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Agli baar jab shehar ka koi case trend kare, toh poochhiye ki usi mahine aapke apne district mein kya hua, aur wahan kisne uske baare mein suna.

rape-justice-audit-since-december-2012.en:
After the 2012 Delhi gang rape, India made three kinds of promise: a harsher law, money for women's safety and faster justice. The case itself ended with the harshest sentence Indian law allows: four men were hanged at Tihar Jail on 20 March 2020 [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. For every other survivor, the plainer test is this: when a rape case reaches trial, how often does it end in conviction? In 2012, courts convicted in about 24% of the rape trials they completed [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. In 2024, the figure was 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This is an audit of the twelve years in between.

## What India promised after 2012

The first answer came within weeks. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed in force from 3 February 2013, widened the legal definition of rape beyond penile-vaginal intercourse [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. It set a 20-year minimum for gang rape, and allowed the death penalty for rape that causes death or a persistent vegetative state and for repeat offenders [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. That month's Budget speech proposed a Nirbhaya Fund for women's safety, starting with Rs 1,000 crore [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

The second wave came in 2018. The minimum sentence for rape rose from seven to ten years, and raping a girl under 12 became punishable by death [[prs-cla-bill-2018]]. Police were told to finish rape investigations within two months, and appeals were to be decided within six [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

Each step made punishment heavier on paper or promised speed. The test is what happened in court.

## The conviction rate, year by year

NCRB's conviction rate is the share of completed trials that end in conviction. Across the 13 years from 2012 to 2024, the rate for rape crossed 30% only twice.

| Year | What else was happening | Rape trials ending in conviction |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 | Last year of the old definition | about 24% [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]] |
| 2017 | A year before the ten-year minimum | 32.2% [[ncrb-cii-2017-snapshots]] |
| 2018 | Ten-year minimum; death for raping a girl under 12 | 27.2% [[ncrb-cii-2018]] |
| 2020 | COVID-19; far fewer trials completed | 39.3% [[ncrb-cii-2020-snapshots]] |
| 2023 | Lowest of the series | 22.7% [[ncrb-cii-2023]] |
| 2024 | New penal code from 1 July | 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |

In the seven years not shown, the rate stayed between 25.5% [[ncrb-cii-2016-snapshots]] and 29.4% [[ncrb-cii-2015-figures-at-a-glance]]. Neither high can be credited to a reform. The 2017 peak came four years after the 2013 law and a year before the 2018 one. The 2020 record came in the lockdown year, when courts completed far fewer rape trials. Six years after the ten-year minimum, the results are back at the level of 2012.

Behind the 2024 rate are 5,032 convictions and 13,980 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: nearly three acquittals for every conviction. NCRB rounded the 2012 rate to a whole number, and the 2013 law changed what counts as rape, so the series is not perfectly like for like. But no reading of it shows a lasting rise.

## Money set aside, money unspent

By July 2026, according to a Rajya Sabha reply reported by ThePrint, Nirbhaya Fund allocations since 2013-14 had reached Rs 7,990.85 crore. Of that, Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) had been released and used, leaving about Rs 1,288 crore unspent [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Where the money went shows the priorities. Safe City projects in eight cities received Rs 1,686.73 crore, more than One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) or fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases (Rs 1,234.55 crore) [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Safer streets matter, but the rape data point closer to home: in 2024 the accused was known to the survivor in 96.8% of registered rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men was listed as ongoing, with nothing spent [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

The fund has bought real services. By July 2026, 985 One Stop Centres were operational and had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. What it has not bought is a better chance that a rape trial ends in conviction.

## Severity versus certainty

In January 2013, the Justice J.S. Verma Committee advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament kept adding it instead. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024, allows death for the gang rape of a girl under 18 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Severity is what the law threatens. Certainty is the chance that a case reaches a verdict and ends in conviction. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were waiting for trial, 89.8% of all rape cases before the courts that year, while courts completed 20,587 trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At that pace, clearing the queue would take about nine years even if no new case arrived. And the queue was more than a third longer than at the end of 2018, when 1,38,642 cases were pending [[ncrb-cii-2018]].

Deadlines have not closed the gap. Today's code asks police to finish a rape investigation within two months and courts to finish the trial within two months of the charge sheet, but sets no consequence when either deadline is missed [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. (This is general information, not legal advice.) At the end of 2024, 8,905 rape cases were still under investigation [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What would actually move the number

Consider this situation. A 19-year-old in Patna reports a neighbour for rape. Police will probably file a charge sheet: they did so in 81.3% of the rape cases they disposed of in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Then her case joins the queue. Every year it waits, she has to keep her account steady, her witnesses willing and her family behind her, while the man she accused lives a few doors away. A ten-year minimum does nothing to shorten that wait.

What would move the number is certainty, and certainty is unglamorous: enough judges and courtrooms to cut the queue, investigations finished on time, and support that keeps survivors in the process until a verdict. India had 779 Fast Track Special Courts, set up under a 2019 scheme, working in November 2026 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]], yet the scheme's courts disposed of 66,500 rape and POCSO cases in 2025, 22% fewer than in 2024 [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

The data needs fixing too. NCRB's tables count acquittals but give no reasons for them, so the national data cannot show how many trials fail on weak evidence, delay or pressure on the survivor. The next time a government answers a rape case with a harsher sentence, ask for three other numbers: trials completed, convictions, and cases still waiting.
rape-justice-audit-since-december-2012.hg:
2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad India ne teen tarah ke vaade kiye: sakht law, aurton ki safety ke liye paisa, aur tez insaaf. Khud us case ka ant Indian law ki sabse sakht saza par hua: 20 March 2020 ko Tihar Jail mein chaar aadmiyon ko phaansi di gayi [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Baaki har survivor ke liye kasauti zyada seedhi hai: jab rape ka case trial tak pahunchta hai, toh kitni baar woh conviction par khatam hota hai? 2012 mein courts ne rape ke jitne trials poore kiye, unmein se lagbhag 24% mein conviction diya [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. 2024 mein yeh figure 24.4% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh beech ke barah saalon ka audit hai.

## 2012 ke baad India ne kya vaade kiye

Pehla jawab kuch hi hafton mein aa gaya. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, jo 3 February 2013 se laagu maana gaya, ne rape ki legal definition ko penile-vaginal intercourse se aage badhaya [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Isne gang rape ke liye kam se kam 20 saal ki saza tay ki. Saath hi aise rape par death penalty ki ijaazat di jisse victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, aur baar-baar rape karne walon par bhi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Usi mahine ki Budget speech mein aurton ki safety ke liye Nirbhaya Fund ka prastaav aaya, Rs 1,000 crore se shuruaat ke saath [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]].

Doosri lehar 2018 mein aayi. Rape ki minimum saza saat saal se badh kar das saal ho gayi, aur 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape par death penalty di ja sakti thi [[prs-cla-bill-2018]]. Police se kaha gaya ki rape ki investigation do mahine mein poori kare, aur appeals ka faisla chhe mahine mein ho [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

Har kadam ne kaagaz par saza ko bhaari kiya ya raftaar ka vaada kiya. Asli test yeh hai ki court mein kya hua.

## Conviction rate, saal-dar-saal

NCRB ka conviction rate batata hai ki poore hue trials mein se kitne conviction par khatam hue. 2012 se 2024 tak ke 13 saalon mein rape ka yeh rate sirf do baar 30% ke paar gaya.

| Saal | Us waqt aur kya chal raha tha | Conviction par khatam hue rape trials |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 | Purani definition ka aakhri saal | lagbhag 24% [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]] |
| 2017 | Das saal wali minimum saza se ek saal pehle | 32.2% [[ncrb-cii-2017-snapshots]] |
| 2018 | Das saal ki minimum saza; 12 se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape par death | 27.2% [[ncrb-cii-2018]] |
| 2020 | COVID-19; bahut kam trials poore hue | 39.3% [[ncrb-cii-2020-snapshots]] |
| 2023 | Poori series mein sabse kam | 22.7% [[ncrb-cii-2023]] |
| 2024 | 1 July se naya penal code | 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]] |

Jo saat saal table mein nahi hain, unmein rate 25.5% [[ncrb-cii-2016-snapshots]] aur 29.4% [[ncrb-cii-2015-figures-at-a-glance]] ke beech raha. Dono oonche rates mein se kisi ka bhi credit kisi reform ko nahi diya ja sakta. 2017 ka peak 2013 ke law ke chaar saal baad aur 2018 ke law se ek saal pehle aaya. 2020 ka record lockdown wale saal mein aaya, jab courts ne bahut kam rape trials poore kiye. Das saal wali minimum saza ke chhe saal baad, results phir se 2012 ke level par hain.

2024 ke rate ke peeche 5,032 convictions aur 13,980 acquittals hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: har conviction ke muqable lagbhag teen acquittals. NCRB ne 2012 ka rate poore number mein round kiya tha, aur 2013 ke law ne badal diya ki rape kise maana jaata hai, isliye yeh series bilkul ek jaisi cheez nahi naapti. Par ise kaise bhi padhiye, koi tikau badhat nahi dikhti.

## Paisa rakha gaya, paisa bacha raha

ThePrint ki report ke mutabik, July 2026 ke ek Rajya Sabha jawab mein bataya gaya ki 2013-14 se Nirbhaya Fund ke allocations Rs 7,990.85 crore tak pahunch chuke the. Isme se Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) release aur use hue, aur lagbhag Rs 1,288 crore kharch hi nahi hue [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Paisa kahan gaya, isse priorities saaf dikhti hain. Aath shehron ke Safe City projects ko Rs 1,686.73 crore mile, jo One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) ya rape aur POCSO cases ke fast-track courts (Rs 1,234.55 crore) se zyada hai [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Surakshit sadakein zaroori hain, par rape ka data ghar ke kareeb ishaara karta hai: 2024 mein registered rape cases ke 96.8% mein accused survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Panchayati Raj ka aadmiyon ko sensitise karne wala ek programme 'ongoing' bataya gaya, par us par kuch bhi kharch nahi hua tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Fund ne asli services zaroor khadi ki hain. July 2026 tak 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se 15.20 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Jo yeh fund nahi khareed paaya, woh hai is baat ka behtar chance ki rape trial conviction par khatam ho.

## Sakht saza banaam pakki saza

January 2013 mein Justice J.S. Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di thi, yeh note karte hue ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani shayad isse logon mein darr paida na ho [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Iske ulat, Parliament death penalty jodti rahi. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, jisne 1 July 2024 ko IPC ki jagah li, 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape par death ki ijaazat deti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Severity woh hai jiski law dhamki deta hai. Certainty yeh hai ki case ke verdict tak pahunchne aur conviction par khatam hone ka chance kitna hai. 2024 ke end mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, jo us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare rape cases ka 89.8% hai, jabki courts ne poore saal mein 20,587 trials poore kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi raftaar se, agar ek bhi naya case na aaye, tab bhi yeh queue khatam hone mein lagbhag nau saal lagenge. Aur yeh queue 2018 ke end se ek-tihai se bhi zyada lambi thi, jab 1,38,642 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2018]].

Deadlines bhi yeh faasla kam nahi kar paayi. Aaj ka code police se rape ki investigation do mahine mein, aur court se charge sheet ke baad trial do mahine mein poora karne ko kehta hai, par koi deadline chhoot jaaye toh uska koi nateeja tay nahi karta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.) 2024 ke end mein bhi rape ke 8,905 cases ki investigation chal hi rahi thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Number ko asal mein kya badlega

Ek situation sochiye. Patna ki ek 19 saal ki ladki ek padosi ke khilaaf rape ki report karti hai. Police shayad charge sheet file kar degi: 2024 mein police ne rape ke jin cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 81.3% mein yahi kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir uska case queue mein lag jaata hai. Intezaar ke har saal mein use apna bayan pakka rakhna hai, apne gawahon ko taiyaar rakhna hai aur parivaar ko apne saath rakhna hai, jabki jis aadmi par usne aarop lagaya, woh kuch hi ghar door rehta hai. Das saal ki minimum saza is intezaar ko ek din bhi chhota nahi karti.

Number ko jo badlega, woh hai certainty, aur certainty glamorous nahi hoti: queue kam karne ke liye kaafi judges aur courtrooms, samay par poori hui investigation, aur aisa support jo survivor ko verdict tak process mein tika kar rakhe. November 2026 mein India mein 779 Fast Track Special Courts chal rahe the, jo 2019 ki ek scheme ke tahat bane [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Phir bhi 2025 mein is scheme ke courts ne rape aur POCSO ke 66,500 cases dispose kiye, jo 2024 se 22% kam hai [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

Data ko bhi theek karna hoga. NCRB ki tables acquittals ginti hain, par unki wajah nahi batati. Isliye national data yeh nahi dikha sakta ki kitne trials kamzor saboot, deri ya survivor par dabaav ki wajah se fail hue. Agli baar jab koi sarkar kisi rape case ka jawab ek aur sakht saza se de, toh teen doosre numbers maangiye: kitne trials poore hue, kitne convictions hue, aur kitne cases ab bhi intezaar mein hain.

rape-murder-cases-india-data.en:
In 2024 police in India registered 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape, with 274 victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is more than five women and girls raped and murdered every week. These cases sit at the most violent end of sexual violence in India's crime data, and they are among the easiest to miss: not one of them is part of the national rape count.

## 274 victims, 266 cases

The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) counts each FIR once, under the offence that carries the heaviest punishment [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When an FIR records both rape and murder, it leaves the rape table and goes to a separate head, murder with rape or gang rape. So the 29,536 rape cases of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]] include none of these 266. Our explainer on the principal offence rule shows what else that rule moves.

The 2024 figure is not a spike. NCRB recorded 284 such cases in 2021, 248 in 2022 and 230 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Year after year, the count stays in a narrow band. A few cases had more than one victim, which is why victims outnumber cases.

These are police registrations, not a full count of such killings. NCRB itself warns that registered crime is not the same as crime [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rape-murder enters this table only when police record the rape alongside the killing.

## The states at the top

Madhya Pradesh recorded the most cases in 2024, followed by Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Together, these four states account for just over half of the national total.

| State | Cases of murder with rape or gang rape, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Madhya Pradesh | 50 (55 victims) |
| Rajasthan | 38 |
| Maharashtra | 24 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 23 |
| India | 266 (274 victims) |

Read the ranking with care. NCRB advises against comparing states on its figures alone [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and with numbers this small, a handful of cases can move a state up or down the list. A high count can partly reflect police who record the rape charge alongside the murder; a low one can hide police who do not.

## A conviction rate three times rape's

Here the data turn. Courts convicted the accused in 76.4% of murder-with-rape trials completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For rape, the conviction rate was 24.4%, with 5,032 convictions against 13,980 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rape-murder trial that reached a verdict was about three times as likely to end in conviction.

Two cautions apply. The base is small: the 76.4% comes from just 55 completed trials, 42 of which ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so a few verdicts either way would move it sharply. And NCRB does not explain the gap. One possible reason, which these figures cannot test, is evidence: a murder case usually comes with a post-mortem, while a rape trial often turns on a survivor's testimony, given long after the event, and on whether she can hold out against pressure until then.

On these numbers, a trial in which the woman was killed was far more likely to end in conviction than a rape trial in which she lived to testify. That should trouble anyone who believes rape trials are tilted towards complainants.

## 1,574 cases still waiting

The verdicts that did come were few. At the end of 2024, 1,574 murder-with-rape cases were pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]], against the 55 trials completed in the year. On paper, the BNSS asks for trials under the rape sections, including the one for rape causing death, to finish within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Imagine a mother in a district town in Madhya Pradesh whose daughter was raped and murdered in 2022. The FIR and the charge-sheet came within months. The trial did not. Two years on, she travels to court for hearings that are adjourned, while the accused's relatives live a few lanes away. Hers would be one of the 1,574.

She does not have to wait for the verdict to claim support. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme, the family of a woman killed is entitled to Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh in compensation [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]], and the BNSS allows compensation even when the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Her daughter's identity stays protected after death too: the Supreme Court has ruled that it must not be disclosed even with the family's consent, unless a Sessions Judge allows it [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## What the law prescribes

Rape that causes a woman's death, or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, is a separate offence under Section 66 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). It carries at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. NCRB's head covers murder under Section 103 read with the rape sections [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The rape-causing-death offence is not new: the 2013 criminal law amendment created it as Section 376A of the IPC, with the same range of punishment [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

In January 2025 a Sealdah court in Kolkata applied Section 66, with the rape and murder sections, in the RG Kar Medical College case. It sentenced the convict to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life and refused the death penalty, holding that the crime was not "rarest of the rare" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The CBI, which prosecuted the case, was left to pursue its own appeal for a death sentence [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

The law already reaches the harshest punishment India allows. What the system fails to deliver is speed and, for survivors who live, anything close to the conviction rate it manages here.
rape-murder-cases-india-data.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne murder with rape ya gang rape ke 266 cases register kiye, jinmein 274 victims the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani har hafte paanch se zyada aurton aur ladkiyon ka rape karke murder. Yeh cases India ke crime data mein sexual violence ka sabse hinsak chhor hain, aur inhe nazarandaaz karna sabse aasaan bhi hai: inmein se ek bhi national rape count ka hissa nahi hai.

## 274 victims, 266 cases

National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, us offence ke naam par jiski saza sabse bhaari hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab kisi FIR mein rape aur murder dono darj hon, toh woh rape table se nikal kar ek alag head mein chali jaati hai: murder with rape ya gang rape. Isliye 2024 ke 29,536 rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]] mein in 266 mein se ek bhi shamil nahi hai. Principal offence rule par hamara explainer batata hai ki yeh rule aur kya-kya idhar se udhar karta hai.

2024 ka figure koi achanak aaya uchhaal nahi hai. NCRB ne aise 284 cases 2021 mein, 248 cases 2022 mein aur 230 cases 2023 mein darj kiye the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Saal dar saal yeh ginti ek patle daayre mein rehti hai. Kuch cases mein ek se zyada victim the, isliye victims ki sankhya cases se zyada hai.

Yeh police registrations hain, aisi hatyaon ki poori ginti nahi. NCRB khud warn karta hai ki registered crime aur asli crime ek cheez nahi hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Koi rape-murder is table mein tabhi aata hai jab police murder ke saath rape bhi darj kare.

## Sabse aage wale states

2024 mein sabse zyada cases Madhya Pradesh mein darj hue, uske baad Rajasthan, Maharashtra aur Uttar Pradesh mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh chaar states milkar national total ke aadhe se thoda zyada hain.

| State | Murder with rape ya gang rape ke cases, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Madhya Pradesh | 50 (55 victims) |
| Rajasthan | 38 |
| Maharashtra | 24 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 23 |
| India | 266 (274 victims) |

Is ranking ko dhyaan se padhiye. NCRB salah deta hai ki states ko sirf uske figures ke basis par compare na kiya jaaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur itne chhote numbers mein mutthi bhar cases kisi state ko list mein upar-neeche kar sakte hain. Zyada ginti ka ek kaaran yeh bhi ho sakta hai ki wahan police murder ke saath rape ka charge bhi darj karti hai; kam ginti ke peeche aisi police bhi chhupi ho sakti hai jo aisa nahi karti.

## Rape se teen guna conviction rate

Yahan data palat jaata hai. 2024 mein poore hue murder-with-rape trials mein courts ne 76.4% mein accused ko convict kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape mein conviction rate 24.4% tha, jahan 5,032 convictions ke saamne 13,980 acquittals hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo rape-murder trial verdict tak pahuncha, uske conviction par khatam hone ki sambhavna lagbhag teen guna thi.

Do saavdhaaniyan zaroori hain. Base chhota hai: 76.4% sirf 55 poore hue trials se aata hai, jinmein se 42 conviction par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye kuch faisle idhar-udhar hone se yeh figure tezi se badal sakta hai. Aur NCRB is farq ki wajah nahi batata. Ek mumkin wajah, jise yeh figures parakh nahi sakte, saboot hai: murder case ke saath aam taur par post-mortem hota hai, jabki rape trial aksar survivor ki gawahi par tika hota hai, jo ghatna ke kaafi baad di jaati hai, aur is baat par ki tab tak woh dabaav jhel paati hai ya nahi.

In numbers ke hisaab se, jis trial mein aurat ki hatya ho chuki thi, uske conviction par khatam hone ki sambhavna us rape trial se kahin zyada thi jismein woh gawahi dene ke liye zinda thi. Yeh baat har us insaan ko pareshan karni chahiye jo maanta hai ki rape trials complainants ke paksh mein jhuke hote hain.

## 1,574 cases ab bhi intezaar mein

Jo faisle aaye, woh kam the. 2024 ke aakhir tak 1,574 murder-with-rape cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki us saal sirf 55 trials poore hue. Kaagaz par BNSS kehta hai ki rape sections ke trials, jinmein rape se maut wala section bhi shamil hai, charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar poore hon [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Madhya Pradesh ke ek zila shehar ki ek maa ki kalpana kijiye, jiski beti ka 2022 mein rape karke murder kar diya gaya. FIR aur charge-sheet kuch mahinon mein aa gayi. Trial nahi aaya. Do saal baad bhi woh court ki un tareekhon par jaati hai jo aage khisak jaati hain, jabki accused ke rishtedaar kuch galiyan door rehte hain. Uska case un 1,574 mein se ek hota.

Madad paane ke liye use verdict ka intezaar nahi karna padta. NALSA ki 2018 scheme ke tahat maari gayi aurat ke parivaar ko Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh tak ka compensation milne ka haq hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]], aur BNSS tab bhi compensation ki ijaazat deta hai jab offender kabhi trace na ho aur koi trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Maut ke baad bhi uski beti ki pehchaan surakshit rehti hai: Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki parivaar ki marzi ho tab bhi use disclose nahi kiya ja sakta, jab tak Sessions Judge ijaazat na de [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## Law kya saza tay karta hai

Aisa rape jisse aurat ki maut ho jaaye, ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 66 ke tahat ek alag offence hai. Iski saza kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo baaki natural life tak ki qaid ya death tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. NCRB ka yeh head Section 103 ke murder ko rape sections ke saath padh kar ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape se maut wala offence naya nahi hai: 2013 ke criminal law amendment ne ise IPC ke Section 376A ke roop mein banaya tha, isi saza ke daayre ke saath [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

January 2025 mein Kolkata ki Sealdah court ne RG Kar Medical College case mein rape aur murder ke sections ke saath Section 66 lagaya. Usne convict ko baaki natural life ki qaid di aur death penalty se inkaar kiya, yeh kehte hue ki crime "rarest of the rare" nahi tha [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Case ko prosecute karne wali CBI ke paas death sentence ke liye apni alag appeal aage badhaane ka raasta bacha [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

Law pehle hi India ki sabse kadi saza tak pahunchta hai. System jo nahi de paata, woh hai raftaar, aur zinda bachi survivors ke liye is conviction rate ke aas-paas ka bhi kuch.

rape-trial-backlog-pending-cases.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Bhopal whose rape case is charge-sheeted this month. On paper, her trial should be over within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In practice, her file joins a queue. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were waiting for trial in Indian courts, 89.8% of all the rape cases before them that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. During 2024 the courts disposed of 20,992 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At that pace, if not one new case arrived, clearing the queue would take close to nine years.

## The queue in one number

Every year NCRB publishes the courts' rape list as a simple sum. For 2024 it reads like this [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Rape cases in Indian courts, 2024 | Number |
|---|---|
| Waiting from earlier years | 1,82,163 |
| Sent for trial during the year | 24,614 |
| Total before the courts | 2,06,777 |
| Disposed of during the year | 20,992 |
| Still waiting on 31 December | 1,85,785 |

Read the middle rows together. Police sent the courts 24,614 new rape cases; the courts disposed of 20,992. More came in than went out, so the queue grew again. Divide the year-end queue by a year's disposals and you get close to nine years.

That is not a forecast for any one case. Courts do not take cases strictly in order, and some trials move faster than others. It is a measure of how deep the hole is. And "disposed of" does not mean decided in the survivor's favour: of the 20,587 trials that actually ended, 5,032 ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## How it grew since 2018

The 2024 figure is not a bad year. It is a trend. At the end of 2018, 1,38,642 rape cases were pending trial, and the queue has grown in every year since [[ncrb-cii-2018]]: to 1,73,716 by the end of 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2021]], 1,78,485 by 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2022]], 1,82,163 by 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] and 1,85,785 by 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In six years it grew by about a third.

The share left waiting barely moves. At the end of 2018, 88.7% of the rape cases before the courts were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2018]]; at the end of 2024, 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Year after year, roughly nine in ten rape cases before a court end the year still waiting. Nor did the waiting buy better outcomes: courts convicted in 27.2% of rape trials completed in 2018 [[ncrb-cii-2018]], and in 24.4% of those completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Children's cases sit in a separate, longer queue. Most rape of girls under 18 is counted under POCSO, which also covers boys, and 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The two-month promise

The law's promise is exact. Under Section 346 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a rape trial must be completed within two months of the charge-sheet; under Section 415, an appeal against a rape sentence must be decided within six months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For children, the POCSO Act asks Special Courts to record the child's evidence within 30 days and to finish the trial, as far as possible, within one year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Set the promise against the queue. If every rape trial really ended two months after its charge-sheet, the only cases pending on 31 December would be those charge-sheeted in November and December: a few thousand, not 1,85,785.

The deadline fails quietly because nothing happens when it is missed. The law attaches no consequence to a trial that runs past two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A deadline cannot create judges, prosecutors, courtrooms or forensic reports. It can only say how fast a trial should be if those existed.

## Fast-track courts, slow numbers

Fast Track Special Courts were meant to drain exactly this queue. Since the scheme began on 2 October 2019 they have disposed of 4,02,457 rape and POCSO cases, and 779 of them were working in November 2026 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Their own list is growing anyway. About 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before them on 31 December 2025, up from 2,04,122 a year earlier, because new cases (1,43,936 in 2025) far outran disposals (66,500) [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

These Law Ministry figures mix rape and POCSO cases and come from a different system, so they cannot be added to NCRB's count. But they point the same way: courts built for speed have not yet produced it. We look at the fast-track scheme in detail in a separate piece.

## What waiting does to a case

A trial is where a survivor's account is tested, and time works against her. Memories blur. Witnesses move, marry, change jobs or stop answering calls. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024 the accused was someone the survivor knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so the years of waiting can be spent in the same family, street or workplace as him. Every adjournment means another day off work or college, and another chance for someone to suggest she "settle".

NCRB does not record why trials end in acquittal, so no table can show how many cases are lost to delay alone [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What the law does offer are rights that do not wait for a verdict. The trial must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A survivor with a lawyer is entitled to free copies of the police report, FIR and statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance, and to be heard before the prosecution is withdrawn [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation from the State or District Legal Services Authority does not depend on a conviction: it can be awarded when a trial ends in acquittal, and even when no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

Until courts decide more rape cases each year than police send them, the queue can only grow, whatever the statute says. Measure every promise of a speedy trial against that one sum.
rape-trial-backlog-pending-cases.hg:
Socho, Bhopal ki ek 19 saal ki ladki, jiske rape case mein is mahine charge-sheet file hui hai. Kaagaz par uska trial do mahine ke andar khatam ho jaana chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Asal mein uski file ek queue mein lag jaati hai. 2024 ke end mein Indian courts mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ka wait kar rahe the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare rape cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 mein courts ne 20,992 cases dispose kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi speed se, agar ek bhi naya case na aaye, tab bhi queue clear karne mein lagbhag nau saal lagenge.

## Queue, ek number mein

NCRB har saal courts ki rape list ko ek simple jod-ghataav ki tarah chhaapta hai. 2024 ke liye yeh aisa dikhta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Indian courts mein rape cases, 2024 | Sankhya |
|---|---|
| Pichhle saalon se pending | 1,82,163 |
| Saal ke dauraan trial ke liye bheje gaye | 24,614 |
| Courts ke saamne kul cases | 2,06,777 |
| Saal ke dauraan dispose hue | 20,992 |
| 31 December ko ab bhi pending | 1,85,785 |

Beech ki rows ko saath padho. Police ne courts ko 24,614 naye rape cases bheje; courts ne 20,992 dispose kiye. Jitne cases nikle, usse zyada aaye, isliye queue phir badh gayi. Saal ke end ki queue ko ek saal ke disposals se divide karo, toh lagbhag nau saal aata hai.

Yeh kisi ek case ka forecast nahi hai. Courts cases ko bilkul line se nahi uthate, aur kuch trials baaki se tez chalte hain. Yeh bas yeh naapta hai ki gaddha kitna gehra hai. Aur "dispose hua" ka matlab yeh nahi ki faisla survivor ke haq mein aaya: jo 20,587 trials sach mein poore hue, unme se 5,032 conviction par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 2018 se yeh kaise badhi

2024 ka figure koi ek bura saal nahi hai. Yeh ek trend hai. 2018 ke end mein 1,38,642 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, aur tab se har saal queue badhi hai [[ncrb-cii-2018]]: 2021 ke end tak 1,73,716 [[ncrb-cii-2021]], 2022 tak 1,78,485 [[ncrb-cii-2022]], 2023 tak 1,82,163 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] aur 2024 tak 1,85,785 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chhe saal mein yeh lagbhag ek-tihaai badh gayi.

Pending cases ka hissa lagbhag wahin ka wahin hai. 2018 ke end mein courts ke saamne wale rape cases ka 88.7% pending tha [[ncrb-cii-2018]]; 2024 ke end mein 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Saal dar saal, court ke saamne aaye har das mein se lagbhag nau rape cases saal ke end mein bhi wait hi kar rahe hote hain. Aur is intezaar se nateeje behtar bhi nahi hue: 2018 mein poore hue rape trials mein se 27.2% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2018]], aur 2024 mein poore hue trials mein se 24.4% mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bachchon ke cases ek alag, aur zyada lambi queue mein hain. 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke zyada tar rape cases POCSO ke under gine jaate hain, jo ladkon ko bhi cover karta hai, aur 2024 ke end mein POCSO ke 2,86,903 cases trial ke liye pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Do mahine ka promise

Law ka promise bilkul saaf hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 346 ke tehat rape trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye; aur Section 415 ke tehat rape ki saza ke khilaaf appeal ka faisla chhe mahine mein hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bachchon ke liye POCSO Act Special Courts se kehta hai ki bachche ka bayaan 30 din mein record ho, aur jahan tak ho sake, trial ek saal mein poora ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ab is promise ko queue ke saamne rakho. Agar har rape trial sach mein charge-sheet ke do mahine baad khatam ho jaata, toh 31 December ko sirf woh cases pending hote jinki charge-sheet November aur December mein file hui: kuch hazaar, 1,85,785 nahi.

Deadline chupchaap toot jaati hai, kyunki use todne par kuch hota hi nahi. Trial do mahine se lamba chale, toh law koi consequence tay nahi karta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Deadline judges, prosecutors, courtrooms ya forensic reports paida nahi kar sakti. Woh sirf itna bata sakti hai ki agar yeh sab hote, toh trial kitna tez hona chahiye tha.

## Fast-track courts, slow numbers

Fast Track Special Courts isi queue ko khaali karne ke liye bane the. 2 October 2019 ko scheme shuru hui, aur tab se in courts ne rape aur POCSO ke 4,02,457 cases dispose kiye hain; November 2026 mein inme se 779 chal rahe the [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Phir bhi inki apni list lambi hoti ja rahi hai. 31 December 2025 ko in courts mein rape aur POCSO ke lagbhag 2,45,579 cases pending the, ek saal pehle ke 2,04,122 se zyada, kyunki naye cases (2025 mein 1,43,936) disposals (66,500) se kahin aage nikal gaye [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

Law Ministry ke yeh figures rape aur POCSO cases ko milaate hain aur ek alag system se aate hain, isliye inhe NCRB ke count mein joda nahi ja sakta. Lekin dono ek hi taraf ishaara karte hain: speed ke liye bane courts abhi tak speed nahi la paaye. Fast-track scheme ko hum ek alag piece mein detail mein dekhte hain.

## Intezaar case ke saath kya karta hai

Trial woh jagah hai jahan survivor ki baat ko parkha jaata hai, aur waqt uske khilaaf kaam karta hai. Yaadein dhundhli hoti hain. Gawah shehar badal lete hain, shaadi kar lete hain, naukri badal lete hain ya phone uthana band kar dete hain. 2024 mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein accused koi aisa tha jise survivor jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye intezaar ke yeh saal usi family, usi gali ya usi workplace mein guzar sakte hain jahan accused bhi hai. Har adjournment ka matlab hai kaam ya college se ek aur chhutti, aur kisi ke liye ek aur mauka yeh kehne ka ki woh "settle" kar le.

NCRB yeh record nahi karta ki trials acquittal par kyun khatam hote hain, isliye koi table nahi bata sakti ki sirf deri ki wajah se kitne cases haath se nikle [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Haan, law kuch aise rights deta hai jo verdict ka wait nahi karte. Trial in camera hona chahiye, aur jahan tak ho sake, woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jis survivor ka lawyer hai, use accused ke pehli baar pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies milni chahiye, aur prosecution wapas lene se pehle uski baat suni jaani chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. State ya District Legal Services Authority se compensation conviction par depend nahi karta: trial acquittal par khatam ho tab bhi mil sakta hai, aur jab trial hua hi na ho tab bhi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Jab tak courts har saal utne rape cases decide nahi karte jitne police unhe bhejti hai, tab tak queue sirf badh sakti hai, statute chahe kuch bhi kahe. Speedy trial ke har promise ko isi ek hisaab se naapo.

rape-victims-by-age-india.en:
Every year, NCRB prints a small table that most people scroll past: the ages of the women and girls police recorded as rape victims. In 2024 it runs from 15 girls under six to 89 women aged 60 or over [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read band by band, it shows who reaches a police station, at what age, and where the record goes quiet. It also shows that the rape table is only part of the story, because most children are counted in a different table altogether.

## The age table, band by band

Police registered 29,536 rape cases in 2024, with 29,742 victims. NCRB's Table 3A.3 sorts those victims by age [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Age | Victims under the rape head, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Under 18 | 792 |
| 18 to 30 | 19,489 |
| 30 to 45 | 8,316 |
| 45 to 60 | 1,056 |
| 60 and over | 89 |

The under-18 line is small because most child rape is booked under the POCSO Act. In that table, police recorded 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault in 2024: 831 under six, 3,438 aged 6 to 12, 16,801 aged 12 to 16 and 23,497 aged 16 to 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Put the two tables side by side and one fact stands out. The two years between 16 and 18 produced more victims recorded under POCSO's penetrative-assault sections (23,497) than the twelve years between 18 and 30 did under the rape head (19,489). Part of that peak may come from relationships between teenagers that families take to the police. The law makes no exception for those: since 2013, sex with a girl under 18 has been rape whether or not she agreed [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. NCRB does not count such cases separately, so nobody can say how many there are.

## Why 18 to 30 dominates

Under the rape head, about two in three victims were aged 18 to 30. Part of this may be exposure to men they know. The largest group of known offenders in NCRB's 2024 table, 13,879 cases, is friends, online friends, live-in partners "on pretext of marriage" and separated husbands [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But NCRB prints age and relationship in separate tables, so the two cannot be matched case by case.

Another part may be access. An FIR needs a survivor who can reach a police station, be believed and keep going. In NFHS-5, 6% of women aged 18 to 49 said they had ever faced sexual violence. The share was 9% among women with no schooling against 3% among those with 12 or more years, and 10% in the poorest households against 3% in the richest [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. NCRB's rape tables have no column for schooling or income, so nobody can tell whether the women most likely to face violence are the ones reaching police stations. The bulge at 18 to 30 measures who reports, as well as who is attacked.

Age changes what happens in court, too. When the victim under the rape head was a girl, courts convicted in 31.4% of completed trials in 2024; when she was an adult woman, in 23.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. One possible reason: for a girl, consent is legally irrelevant, while at an adult woman's trial the defence can argue that she agreed.

## Older survivors and the silence around them

After 45 the numbers fall away: 1,056 victims aged 45 to 60, and 89 aged 60 or over [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It would be comforting to read that as safety. Nothing in the data supports it.

Consider what reporting asks of a 62-year-old widow in a small town. She may depend on her household for food, medicine and a roof. If the abuser is a relative, a caregiver or a neighbour her family relies on, an FIR can cost her all three. She may have no words for what happened, and may expect not to be believed by the people she would have to tell.

And the national survey offers nothing to check the police figure against: NFHS-5 did not ask women over 49 about sexual violence at all. For the oldest women, the police table is left to speak alone, and 89 is what it says.

## Who the national survey leaves out

NFHS-5 asked about sexual violence only of women aged 18 to 49 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Three groups fall outside it.

- **Children.** The NFHS does not ask them. The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, based on a purposive sample, found that sexual abuse reported by children began as early as age 5, gained momentum from age 10 and peaked at 12 to 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Police records peak later, at 16 to 18. Young children rarely disclose, so the 831 under six and 3,438 aged 6 to 12 are minimums.
- **Women over 49.** WHO's latest global estimates count women aged 15 and older: 8.2% of them have faced sexual violence by someone other than a partner since age 15 [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. But WHO's national estimate for India, 4.1%, covers only women aged 15 to 49, and WHO cautions that where stigma is high and services are scarce, the real level is likely much higher than its estimates [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].
- **Men, boys and transgender people.** Boys appear only in the POCSO table: 892 of the 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Adult men and adult transgender people appear in neither table. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman", and the BNS has no counterpart to IPC Section 377, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the new code [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The age table shows whom the system can see. A 70-year-old woman with no survey to speak for her, a man assaulted by another man, a five-year-old who cannot yet find the words: all of them sit at or beyond the edge of its frame. Each of them still deserves to be believed, treated and protected.
rape-victims-by-age-india.hg:
NCRB har saal ek chhoti si table chhapta hai jise zyada tar log bina padhe scroll kar dete hain: un auraton aur ladkiyon ki umar, jinhe police ne rape victims ke roop mein darj kiya. 2024 mein yeh table chhe saal se chhoti 15 bachchiyon se shuru hoti hai aur 60 saal ya usse upar ki 89 auraton tak jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ise age band ke hisaab se padho, toh pata chalta hai ki kaun police station tak pahunchta hai, kis umar mein pahunchta hai, aur kahan jaakar record chup ho jaata hai. Yeh bhi dikhta hai ki rape wali table poori kahani nahi hai, kyunki zyada tar bachche ek bilkul alag table mein gine jaate hain.

## Umar ki table, har band ka hisaab

2024 mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases darj kiye, jinmein 29,742 victims thin. NCRB ki Table 3A.3 in victims ko umar ke hisaab se baant'ti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Umar | Rape head ke tehat victims, 2024 |
|---|---|
| 18 se kam | 792 |
| 18 se 30 | 19,489 |
| 30 se 45 | 8,316 |
| 45 se 60 | 1,056 |
| 60 aur usse upar | 89 |

18 se kam wali line isliye chhoti hai kyunki bachchon ke rape ke zyada tar cases POCSO Act mein darj hote hain. Us table mein 2024 mein penetrative sexual assault (yaani POCSO ki bhasha mein bachchon ka rape) ke 44,567 bachche victims darj hue: 831 chhe saal se chhote, 3,438 6 se 12 saal ke, 16,801 12 se 16 saal ke, aur 23,497 16 se 18 saal ke [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Dono tables saath rakho toh ek baat saaf dikhti hai. 16 se 18 saal ke sirf do saalon mein POCSO ke penetrative assault wale sections mein 23,497 victims darj hue, jo rape head mein 18 se 30 ke poore baarah saalon (19,489) se bhi zyada hain. Is peak ka kuch hissa teenagers ke aapsi rishton se aa sakta hai, jinhe families police tak le jaati hain. Lekin law aise cases mein bhi koi chhoot nahi deta: 2013 se, 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe uski consent ho ya na ho [[prs-madhavan-sexual-offences-2013]]. NCRB aise cases alag se nahi ginta, isliye koi nahi bata sakta ki yeh kitne hain.

## 18 se 30 sabse upar kyun

Rape head ke tehat lagbhag teen mein se do victims 18 se 30 saal ki thin. Iski ek wajah shayad jaan-pehchaan ke mard hain. NCRB ki 2024 ki table mein jaan-pehchaan wale offenders ka sabse bada group, 13,879 cases, friends, online friends, "shaadi ke vaade" wale live-in partners aur alag reh rahe patiyon ka hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin NCRB umar aur rishte ko alag-alag tables mein chhapta hai, isliye dono ko case-by-case match nahi kiya ja sakta.

Doosri wajah shayad pahunch hai. FIR ke liye zaroori hai ki survivor police station tak pahunch sake, uski baat maani jaaye, aur woh aage ladti reh sake. NFHS-5 mein 18 se 49 saal ki 6% auraton ne kaha ki unhone kabhi sexual violence jheli hai. Jo auratein kabhi school nahi gayin, unmein yeh 9% tha, jabki 12 ya usse zyada saal padhi auraton mein 3%. Sabse gareeb gharon mein yeh 10% tha aur sabse ameer gharon mein 3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. NCRB ki rape tables mein padhai ya kamai ka koi column nahi hai, isliye koi nahi bata sakta ki jin auraton ko violence ka khatra sabse zyada hai, woh police station tak pahunch bhi rahi hain ya nahi. 18 se 30 wali bheed yeh bhi naapti hai ki kaun report kar paata hai, sirf yeh nahi ki kis par attack hota hai.

Court mein bhi umar se farak padta hai. 2024 mein rape ke jin cases mein victim ladki thi, unmein poore hue trials mein se 31.4% mein saza hui. Jahan victim adult aurat thi, wahan sirf 23.7% mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Iski ek mumkin wajah: ladki ke case mein consent ka legally koi matlab nahi hai, jabki adult aurat ke trial mein defence yeh daleel de sakta hai ki usne haan kaha tha.

## Badi umar ki survivors aur unke aaspaas ki chuppi

45 ke baad numbers tezi se girte hain: 45 se 60 saal ki 1,056 victims, aur 60 ya usse upar ki 89 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ise safety maan lena aasaan lagta hai. Lekin data mein aisa kuch nahi hai jo yeh baat saabit kare.

Sochiye, ek chhote shehar ki 62 saal ki widow ke liye complaint karne ka kya matlab hai. Ho sakta hai woh khaane, dawa aur sar par chhat ke liye ghar walon par depend karti ho.
