Agar abuse karne wala koi relative hai, dekhbhaal karne wala hai, ya aisa padosi hai jis par family tiki hai, toh ek FIR usse yeh teeno cheezein chheen sakti hai. Ho sakta hai jo hua, uske liye uske paas shabd hi na hon, aur use lage ki jinhe batana padega, woh yakeen hi nahi karenge.

Aur national survey bhi police ke number ko check karne ka koi zariya nahi deta: NFHS-5 ne 49 saal se upar ki auraton se sexual violence ke baare mein poochha hi nahi. Sabse badi umar ki auraton ke liye sirf police ki table bolti hai, aur woh bas 89 kehti hai.

## National survey kise chhod deta hai

NFHS-5 ne sexual violence ke baare mein sirf 18 se 49 saal ki auraton se poochha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Teen groups isse bahar reh jaate hain.

- **Bachche.** NFHS bachchon se nahi poochhta. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse chune hue sample par based thi. Usmein bachchon ne jo sexual abuse bataya, woh 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho gaya tha, 10 saal se badha, aur 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Police records mein peak baad mein aata hai, 16 se 18 saal par. Chhote bachche aksar bata hi nahi paate, isliye chhe saal se chhote 831 aur 6 se 12 saal ke 3,438 bachche minimum ginti hain.
- **49 se upar ki auratein.** WHO ke naye global estimates 15 saal aur usse upar ki sabhi auraton ko ginte hain, aur inmein se 8.2% ne 15 saal ki umar ke baad partner ke alawa kisi aur se sexual violence jheli hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Lekin India ke liye WHO ka national estimate, 4.1%, sirf 15 se 49 saal ki auraton ka hai, aur WHO warning deta hai ki jahan stigma zyada hai aur madad kam milti hai, wahan asli violence uske estimates se kahin zyada hone ki sambhavna hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].
- **Mard, ladke aur transgender log.** Ladke sirf POCSO wali table mein dikhte hain: 2024 mein penetrative assault ke 44,567 bachche victims mein 892 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Adult mard aur adult transgender log dono mein se kisi bhi table mein nahi dikhte. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 63 rape ko "a man" ka "a woman" ke khilaf kiya gaya crime batata hai, aur BNS mein IPC Section 377 jaisa koi provision nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath bina consent ka penetrative sex naye kanoon mein rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Umar ki yeh table dikhati hai ki system kise dekh paata hai. 70 saal ki woh aurat jisse koi survey kuch nahi poochhta, woh aadmi jis par kisi doosre aadmi ne attack kiya, woh paanch saal ka bachcha jiske paas abhi shabd nahi hain: yeh sab is table ke kinare par hain, ya uske bahar. In sabko bhi bharosa, ilaaj aur safety milni chahiye.

relatives-named-in-rape-data.en:
Consider this situation. A 17-year-old tells her mother that a relative who stays with them every summer has been abusing her. The mother's first thoughts are not about the police. They are about the family's name, the money this relative lends, and whether anyone will believe a teenager over an elder. She tells her daughter to keep away from him, and says nothing more. In India, that is often where it ends. The numbers below show how often sexual abuse comes from inside the family, and how rarely it leaves the house.

## What unmarried women told surveyors

The National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) asked women aged 18 to 49 whether they had ever faced sexual violence, and who did it. Among never-married women who said yes, the most common answer was a relative other than a father or brother: 39%. A current or former boyfriend came next at 16%, and a family friend at 12% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Fathers, brothers and their step-relations sit in separate rows, so the 39% does not even include them.

Two cautions: the group of never-married women who reported sexual violence is small, so the percentages are imprecise, and face-to-face survey answers are likely to undercount. Only 5% named a stranger, which is why "stranger danger" lessons miss most of this violence. Ever-married women who reported sexual violence mostly named their current husband (82%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]], and the marital rape exception in Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) keeps nearly all husbands out of police rape data [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That is a story of its own. This one is about the rest of the family.

## 2,134 cases in the police record

Police records show only a sliver of this. In 2024, family members were the accused in 2,134 rape cases. That is the smallest of NCRB's three groups of known offenders: friends, online friends, live-in partners and separated husbands accounted for 13,879 cases, and family friends, neighbours, employers and other known persons for 12,584 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The law treats rape by a relative as aggravated: under Section 64(2)(f) of the BNS, rape by a relative, guardian, teacher or anyone in a position of trust or authority is punishable with 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of the convict's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The number went up. In 2023, family members were the accused in 1,750 rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. In 2024 the figure reached 2,134, even though total rape cases fell slightly, from 29,670 to 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB warns that a rise in registered crime can reflect more reporting rather than more crime [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Either way, more cases against relatives reached a police station in 2024 than a year earlier.

Children are counted in a different table. Among 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under the POCSO Act in 2024, the offender was a family member in 3,658, or 8.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The survey and the police record measure different things and cannot be laid on top of each other. Still, relatives top the survey list for unmarried women, while family members are the smallest group of known accused in police data. The abuse closest to home appears least likely to become an FIR.

## Why the silence runs so deep at home

Abuse by a relative is hard to report for reasons unrelated to how serious it is. The accused may share the house, pay the school fees, or be the person the family depends on. Reporting him can split the family and turn other relatives against the survivor.

In NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone; only 14% sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Of those who did, 61% went to their own family and only 6% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The family is the main door to help. When the abuser is family, that door is his door too.

Children stay silent too. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, done before POCSO and on a sample that was not nationally representative, 72.1% of children who reported being sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had told the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Boys are abused too, and reported even less: police recorded 892 boys among the child victims of penetrative assault in 2024, a number that reflects how rarely boys are reported, not how rarely they are abused [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## When the abuser is family: first steps

If someone tells you a relative abused them, this is what helps. The legal points are general information, not legal advice.

- **Believe them, and say so.** Do not ask why they waited. Do not confront the accused in front of them.
- **Make them safe first.** If they share a home with the accused, find somewhere to stay where he has no access.
- **If they are under 18, report.** Under POCSO, anyone who knows or suspects a child sexual offence must tell the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit; failing to report is punishable with up to six months in jail [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Call 1098, the Child Helpline. Keeping it inside the family is not an option the law allows.
- **If they are an adult, the choice is theirs.** Offer to go with them to a hospital, a One Stop Centre or the police, and respect it if they are not ready.
- **Get medical care fast.** HIV prevention medicine (PEP) must start within 72 hours [[who-pep]], and emergency contraception works up to 5 days after [[who-ec]]. A separate guide on this site covers the full first 72 hours.
- **Know the abortion law.** The MTP rules notified on 12 October 2021 name survivors of "sexual assault or rape or incest" among the women who can end a pregnancy up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]; after 20 weeks, two registered doctors must agree [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. For a girl under 18, the Supreme Court said in 2022 that the doctor's mandatory police report need not reveal her identity if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The government wrote the word "incest" into a gazette notification. The law already names what many families still refuse to say aloud. Survivors need families that act on it.
relatives-named-in-rape-data.hg:
Is situation ke baare mein sochiye. Ek 17 saal ki ladki apni maa ko batati hai ki har garmiyon ki chhutti mein ghar aakar rukne wala ek relative uska sexual abuse kar raha hai. Maa ke mann mein pehla khayal police ka nahi aata. Khayal aata hai family ki izzat ka, us paise ka jo yeh relative udhaar deta hai, aur is baat ka ki bado ke saamne ek teenager ki baat kaun maanega. Maa beti se kehti hai ki usse door rehna, aur phir kuch nahi kehti. India mein aksar baat yahin khatam ho jaati hai. Neeche ke numbers dikhate hain ki sexual abuse kitni baar family ke andar se aata hai, aur kitni kam baar ghar se bahar nikal paata hai.

## Unmarried auraton ne survey mein kya bataya

National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne 18 se 49 saal ki auraton se poocha ki kya unhone kabhi sexual violence jheli hai, aur kisne ki. Jin auraton ki shaadi nahi hui thi aur jinhone 'haan' kaha, unka sabse common jawab tha: father ya brother ke alawa koi aur relative. Aisa 39% ne kaha. Uske baad current ya ex boyfriend (16%) aur family ka koi dost (12%) aata hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Father, brother aur step-father ya step-brother alag rows mein gine gaye hain, yaani 39% mein woh shaamil hi nahi hain.

Do baatein dhyan mein rakhiye. Sexual violence batane wali unmarried auraton ka group chhota hai, isliye yeh percentages ekdum precise nahi hain. Aur aamne-saamne survey mein diye jawab aksar asal se kam hote hain. Sirf 5% ne kisi stranger ka naam liya, isiliye "stranger danger" wali seekh zyada tar violence ko pakad hi nahi paati. Sexual violence report karne wali ever-married auraton ne zyada tar apne current pati ka naam liya (82%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]], aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 mein marital rape ki jo chhoot hai, woh lagbhag sabhi patiyon ko police ke rape data se bahar rakhti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Woh ek alag kahani hai. Yeh article family ke baaki logon ke baare mein hai.

## Police record mein 2,134 cases

Police record mein iska bas ek chhota sa hissa dikhta hai. 2024 mein rape ke 2,134 cases mein accused family member tha. NCRB jaan-pehchaan wale accused ko teen groups mein baantta hai, aur yeh unmein sabse chhota group hai. Friends, online friends, live-in partners aur alag reh rahe pati wale cases 13,879 the, aur family friends, padosi, employer aur doosre jaan-pehchaan walon ke cases 12,584 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Law relative ke kiye rape ko aggravated yaani zyada gambhir offence maanta hai: BNS ke Section 64(2)(f) ke hisaab se relative, guardian, teacher ya bharose ya authority ki jagah par baitha koi bhi insaan rape kare, toh saza 10 saal se lekar convict ki baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh number badha hai. 2023 mein rape ke 1,750 cases mein accused family member tha [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. 2024 mein yeh 2,134 ho gaya, jabki rape ke total cases thode ghate, 29,670 se 29,536 par aa gaye [[ncrb-cii-2023]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB warning deta hai ki registered crime badhne ka matlab yeh bhi ho sakta hai ki complaints zyada darj huin, zaroori nahi ki crime badha ho [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Wajah jo bhi ho, 2024 mein pichhle saal se zyada cases relatives ke khilaf police station tak pahunche.

Bachchon ke cases alag table mein gine jaate hain. 2024 mein POCSO Act mein bachchon par penetrative sexual assault, yaani bachchon ke rape ke 44,126 cases darj hue, aur inmein se 3,658 cases mein, yaani 8.3% mein, accused family member tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Survey aur police record alag-alag cheezein naapte hain, inhe ek doosre ke upar rakhkar nahi padha ja sakta. Phir bhi, survey mein unmarried auraton ki list mein relatives sabse upar hain, jabki police data mein jaan-pehchaan wale accused mein family members sabse chhota group hain. Lagta yahi hai ki jo abuse ghar ke sabse kareeb se hota hai, wahi sabse kam FIR tak pahunchta hai.

## Ghar mein chuppi itni gehri kyun hoti hai

Kisi relative ke khilaf complaint karna mushkil hota hai, aur iski wajah yeh nahi ki crime kam serious hai. Ho sakta hai accused usi ghar mein rehta ho, school ki fees bharta ho, ya poori family usi ke sahare chalti ho. Uski complaint karne se family toot sakti hai, aur baaki relatives survivor ke hi khilaf ho sakte hain.

NFHS-5 mein jin auraton ne physical ya sexual violence jheli, unmein se 77% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Sirf 14% ne help maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jinhone help maangi, unmein se 61% apni family ke paas gayin, aur police ke paas sirf 6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani help ka sabse bada darwaza family hai. Aur jab abuse karne wala family ka hi ho, toh woh darwaza bhi usi ka hota hai.

Bachche bhi chup rehte hain. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse POCSO se pehle hui thi, aur uska sample poore desh ki tasveer nahi tha. Usmein jin bachchon ne bataya ki un par sexual assault hua, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Ladkon ka bhi abuse hota hai, aur unke cases aur bhi kam darj hote hain. 2024 mein penetrative sexual assault ke shikar bachchon mein police ne 892 ladke darj kiye. Yeh number dikhata hai ki ladkon ke cases kitne kam darj hote hain, yeh nahi ki unka abuse kitna kam hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Jab abuse karne wala family ka ho: pehle kadam

Agar koi aapko bataye ki kisi relative ne uska abuse kiya hai, toh yeh baatein madad karti hain. Law se judi baatein general information hain, legal advice nahi.

- **Bharosa kijiye, aur yeh kahiye bhi.** Yeh mat poochhiye ki itni der se kyun bataya. Uske saamne accused se ulajhiye mat.
- **Pehle uski safety.** Agar woh accused ke saath ek hi ghar mein rehta hai, toh rehne ki aisi jagah dhoondhiye jahan accused na pahunch sake.
- **Umar 18 se kam hai, toh report kijiye.** POCSO kehta hai ki jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata ho ya shak ho, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko batana hi hoga. Report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye. Baat ko family ke andar daba dena law ke hisaab se koi raasta nahi hai.
- **Adult hai, toh faisla uska hai.** Hospital, One Stop Centre ya police tak saath chalne ki baat kahiye, aur agar woh abhi taiyaar nahi hai, toh uski baat ki izzat kijiye.
- **Ilaaj jaldi karaiye.** HIV se bachane wali dawa (PEP) 72 ghante ke andar shuru honi chahiye [[who-pep]], aur emergency contraception 5 din tak kaam karta hai [[who-ec]]. Pehle 72 ghanton ka poora plan is site par ek alag guide mein hai.
- **Abortion ka law jaaniye.** 12 October 2021 ko jaari MTP rules mein "sexual assault or rape or incest" ki survivors ka saaf zikr hai, aur aisi auratein 24 hafte tak abortion kara sakti hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. 20 hafte ke baad do registered doctors ki sehmati zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Agar ladki 18 se kam hai, toh doctor ko police ko report karni hoti hai, lekin Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki agar ladki aur uske guardian chahein, toh doctor ko us report mein uski pehchaan batane ki zaroorat nahi hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Sarkar ne "incest" shabd gazette notification mein likha hai. Jis baat ko kai families aaj bhi zubaan par nahi laatin, law use naam se pukaarta hai. Ab survivors ko aisi families chahiye jo is par amal karein.

rising-rape-numbers-can-mean-reporting.en:
Every year, when the crime data come out, the same headline appears somewhere: rape cases up in this state, up in that city. The opposition attacks, the government defends, and both assume the same thing: a higher number means more danger. Sometimes it does. But India's own crime bureau, and research spanning two decades of Indian data, say a rise can also mean the opposite. Women who once stayed silent are being heard.

## The myth: up means worse

The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) says it plainly in its guidance for Crime in India 2024: "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things. Higher numbers, it adds, may come from citizen-centric steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. It also warns that more crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Think of every registered case as the end of a chain. Violence happens. A woman decides to speak. Police write it down. A count can rise because there is more violence, because more women speak, or because police turn fewer of them away. It can fall for the same three reasons in reverse. The number alone cannot tell you which link moved.

## What happened when women entered panchayats

The 73rd Amendment reserved one-third of seats in local councils for women, and states brought it in at different times. Economists used that staggered timing to test what women's political voice does to crime data. Using NCRB figures from 1985 to 2007, they found that after the reservation, documented crimes against women rose 46% and recorded rapes rose 23% [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Their conclusion, published in the American Economic Journal: Applied Economics in 2012: "Our evidence suggests that this increase is good news, driven primarily by greater reporting rather than greater incidence of such crimes" [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Imagine a village in Madhya Pradesh where, for the first time, the pradhan is a woman. A mother whose daughter has been sexually assaulted no longer faces only a council of men telling her to settle it quietly. Someone with power will listen, and may walk with her to the thana. Nothing about the violence has changed. What has changed is whether it gets written down.

## Women's police stations and help desks

A second study tested the same idea inside police stations. Opening all-women police stations in Indian cities was associated with a 29% rise in police reports of crimes against women, driven mainly by domestic violence, with no change in femicide [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. The authors read the rise as more reporting, not more violence, because killings of women and survey-reported domestic violence did not move. The study is a working paper, but its logic is simple: the hardest violence to hide stayed level while complaints went up.

The government has backed the same idea. In December 2019 the Ministry of Home Affairs sanctioned Rs 100 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund to set up or strengthen Women Help Desks in police stations, staffed mainly by women officers, as the first point of contact for any woman walking in [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. By March 2025, 14,658 such help desks had been set up, 13,743 of them headed by women officers [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

Put those two facts together. If help desks work, a state that runs them well may see its registered numbers go up, not down. That would be the system doing its job.

## Fifty years of a rising line

NCRB began counting rape in 1971, when 2,487 cases were recorded [[ncrb-cii-2013-trends-1953-2013]]. By 2013 the count was 33,707, a rate of 5.7 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2013-figures-at-a-glance]].

That is more than thirteen times higher, and it does not mean rape became thirteen times more common. Over those decades the population grew, the legal definition changed and the climate for reporting changed. 2013 itself was the first year under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which widened the legal definition of rape from 3 February that year [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. A line that long mostly tells you about registration, not only about violence. Our story on India's rape count from 2012 to 2024 follows what the line did next.

## Questions for a low number

If a rise can be good news, a fall is not automatically good news. Before you celebrate a low or falling number, ask:

- **Are complaints being turned away?** Registering an FIR is mandatory when a complaint discloses a cognizable offence, as the Supreme Court held in *Lalita Kumari* (2013) under Section 154 of the old CrPC [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]; today Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) carries the duty to record such complaints [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A public servant who fails to record a rape complaint commits a crime under Section 199 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Did something stop women from moving or speaking?** In 2020, the lockdown year, police registered 28,046 rape cases, the lowest count of 2013-2024 [[ncrb-cii-2021]]. Fewer FIRs from a year of closed doors are not evidence of less violence.
- **Is the fall too steep to reflect violence alone?** Assam's registered crimes against women fell from 29,046 in 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] to 10,546 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], a drop of almost two-thirds in three years. NCRB does not explain state trends. A change that large deserves questions before applause.

The useful test of a state is not how small its count is, but what happens after an FIR: whether police file charge-sheets, whether courts convict, and how long survivors wait. A state whose numbers rise after it opens help desks may simply be the one that is listening. This is general information, not legal advice.
rising-rape-numbers-can-mean-reporting.hg:
Har saal jab crime data aata hai, kahin na kahin yahi headline banti hai: is state mein rape cases badhe, us shehar mein badhe. Opposition attack karta hai, sarkar safaai deti hai, aur dono ek hi baat maan kar chalte hain: number badha matlab khatra badha. Kabhi-kabhi aisa hota bhi hai. Lekin India ka apna crime bureau, aur India ke do dashakon ke data par hui research kehti hai ki number badhne ka matlab ulta bhi ho sakta hai: jo auratein pehle chup rehti thi, ab unki baat suni ja rahi hai.

## Myth: number badha matlab haalat bigde

National Crime Records Bureau, yaani NCRB, 'Crime in India 2024' ki apni guidance mein saaf kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag cheezein hain. Woh aage kehta hai ki figures badhne ki wajah citizen-friendly kadam bhi ho sakte hain, jaise e-FIR ki facility ya women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. NCRB yeh warning bhi deta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada crime register hona is baat ka "indicator nahi hai" ki woh shehar doosre se kam safe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Har registered case ko ek chain ka aakhri sira samjho. Pehle violence hoti hai. Phir aurat bolne ka faisla karti hai. Phir police use likhti hai. Number teen wajahon se badh sakta hai: violence zyada hui, zyada auratein boli, ya police ne kam auraton ko lautaya. Inhi teen wajahon se number ghat bhi sakta hai. Sirf number dekh kar tum nahi bata sakte ki kaunsi kadi hili.

## Jab auratein panchayat mein pahunchi

Constitution ke 73rd Amendment se local councils ki ek-tihai seats auraton ke liye reserve hui, aur alag-alag states ne ise alag-alag time par laagu kiya. Economists ne isi farq ka use karke check kiya ki auraton ki political awaaz ka crime data par kya asar hota hai. Unhone 1985 se 2007 tak ke NCRB figures dekhe, aur paaya ki reservation ke baad auraton ke khilaaf documented crimes 46% badhe aur recorded rapes 23% badhe [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

2012 mein American Economic Journal: Applied Economics mein chhapi is study ka conclusion tha: "Our evidence suggests that this increase is good news, driven primarily by greater reporting rather than greater incidence of such crimes", yaani yeh badhotri achhi khabar hai, aur iski main wajah zyada reporting hai, aise crimes ka zyada hona nahi [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Socho, Madhya Pradesh ka ek gaon hai jahan pehli baar koi aurat pradhan bani hai. Ek maa ki beti par sexual assault hua hai. Ab uske saamne sirf mardon ki panchayat nahi hai jo kahe ki maamla chupchaap nipta lo. Ab power wali kursi par koi hai jo sunegi, aur shayad uske saath thane tak bhi chalegi. Violence mein kuch nahi badla. Badla yeh hai ki ab woh kaagaz par darj hogi ya nahi.

## Women police stations aur help desks

Ek doosri study ne yahi baat police stations ke andar check ki. India ke shehron mein all-women police stations khulne ke baad, auraton ke khilaaf crimes ki police reports 29% badhi, zyada tar domestic violence ki, lekin femicide yaani auraton ki hatyaon mein koi badlav nahi aaya [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. Researchers ne is badhotri ko zyada reporting maana, zyada violence nahi, kyunki auraton ki hatyaein aur survey mein batayi gayi domestic violence, dono jaisi thi waisi rahi. Yeh abhi ek working paper hai, lekin iska logic seedha hai: jo violence sabse mushkil se chhupti hai, woh utni hi rahi, aur complaints badh gayi.

Sarkar ne bhi isi soch ko aage badhaya. December 2019 mein Home Ministry ne Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 100 crore manzoor kiye, taaki police stations mein Women Help Desks bane ya mazboot hon. In desks par zyada tar women police officers baithni thi, taaki thane aane wali har aurat ka pehla contact yahin ho [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. March 2025 tak aise 14,658 help desks ban chuke the, jinme se 13,743 ki command women officers ke haath mein thi [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

Ab in dono baaton ko saath rakho. Agar help desks kaam kar rahe hain, toh jo state inhe achhe se chalata hai, uske registered figures ghatne ki jagah badh sakte hain. Iska matlab hoga ki system apna kaam kar raha hai.

## Pachaas saal ki chadhti line

NCRB ne rape ki ginti 1971 mein shuru ki, jab 2,487 cases darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2013-trends-1953-2013]]. 2013 tak yeh ginti 33,707 ho gayi, yaani har ek lakh auraton par 5.7 cases [[ncrb-cii-2013-figures-at-a-glance]].

Yeh terah guna se bhi zyada hai, lekin iska matlab yeh nahi ki rape terah guna badh gaye. In dashakon mein aabadi badhi, kanoon mein rape ki definition badli, aur report karne ka mahaul badla. Khud 2013 pehla saal tha jab Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 laagu hua, jisne 3 February 2013 se rape ki legal definition ko bada kar diya [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Itni lambi line zyada tar yeh batati hai ki cases kitne register hue, sirf yeh nahi ki violence kitni hui. 2012 se 2024 tak India ke rape count par humari alag story batati hai ki iske baad line ne kya kiya.

## Kam number se kya poochein

Agar number badhna achhi khabar ho sakta hai, toh number ghatna apne aap achhi khabar nahi hai. Kam ya girte number par khushi manane se pehle yeh sawaal poocho:

- **Kya complaints lautayi ja rahi hain?** Supreme Court ne *Lalita Kumari* (2013) case mein purane CrPC ke Section 154 ke tahat kaha tha ki agar complaint se cognizable offence ka pata chalta hai, yaani aisa crime jisme police seedhe action le sakti hai, toh FIR register karna zaroori hai [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Aaj aisi complaint record karne ki zimmedari Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 mein hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur jo public servant rape complaint record nahi karta, woh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 199 ke tahat crime karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Kya kisi wajah se auratein bahar nikal ya bol nahi paayi?** 2020 ke lockdown wale saal mein police ne 28,046 rape cases register kiye, jo 2013 se 2024 ke beech ki sabse kam ginti thi [[ncrb-cii-2021]]. Band darwazon wale saal mein kam FIRs ka matlab kam violence nahi hai.
- **Kya giravat itni tez hai ki sirf violence ghatne se samjhaayi na ja sake?** Assam mein auraton ke khilaaf registered crimes 2021 mein 29,046 the [[ncrb-cii-2023]], aur 2024 mein 10,546 reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yaani teen saal mein kareeb do-tihai ki giravat. NCRB states ke trends ki wajah nahi batata. Itne bade badlav par taali bajane se pehle sawaal poochne chahiye.

Kisi state ko judge karne ka sahi tarika yeh nahi ki uski ginti kitni chhoti hai. Dekhna yeh chahiye ki FIR ke baad kya hota hai: police chargesheet file karti hai ya nahi, court conviction deta hai ya nahi, aur survivor ko kitna intezaar karna padta hai. Help desks kholne ke baad jis state ke figures badhte hain, ho sakta hai wahi state sach mein sun raha ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

sex-trafficking-india-convictions.en:
In 2024, 5,839 trafficking victims were rescued in India. The single biggest reason they had been trafficked was not forced labour, domestic servitude or marriage. It was sexual exploitation for prostitution: 2,347 people, or 40% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same year, courts finished 586 trafficking trials and convicted in 43 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Between those two numbers sits a crime the law treats as one of its gravest, and the system almost never punishes.

## 2,347: the largest purpose

The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) records why each rescued person had been trafficked. Of the 5,839 rescued in 2024, 2,347 (40%) had been trafficked for sexual exploitation for prostitution, 1,493 (26%) for forced labour, 105 for domestic servitude and 98 for forced marriage [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Almost all of the rest were filed under "other reasons". The rescued count also includes victims from cases registered in earlier years.

Strip away the official phrase, and "sexual exploitation for prostitution" describes people made to submit to sex they cannot refuse, again and again, while someone else takes the money. Sex without consent is rape. So 2,347 is not a vice statistic. It is a count of people raped repeatedly, for profit.

The law agrees on the central point. In deciding whether trafficking took place, Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says the victim's consent is immaterial [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A woman who "agreed" to travel for a job, or who was made to tell a raid team that she works willingly, is still a trafficked person.

## Who is trafficked

India recorded 6,018 people as trafficked in 2024. Of them, 2,297 (38%) were children: 1,384 boys and 913 girls [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But NCRB does not cross-tabulate the purpose of trafficking by age or sex [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so nobody can tell from the national tables how many of the 2,347 were children, or how many were boys or men. Sexual exploitation is not done only to women and girls, but the tables cannot show to whom else. Our separate analysis of trafficked children looks at why boys dominate that count.

Consider a hypothetical that follows a familiar pattern. A 19-year-old in a small town gets a message from an acquaintance: a job at a beauty parlour in a big city, a room to stay in, an advance for her family. At the other end there is no parlour. Her phone and documents are taken. She is told she owes money and will repay it with sex. Nothing about this began with a kidnapping, and almost nothing about it is visible to the people back home.

## 2,135 cases, 43 convictions

States' Anti-Human Trafficking Units recorded 2,135 trafficking cases in 2024, down 2.2% from 2,183 in 2023 and 2,250 in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Courts completed trials in 586 trafficking cases that year. Only 43 ended in a conviction, a conviction rate of 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than nine in ten ended in acquittal or discharge.

Set that beside rape, whose trials are already known for failing survivors: courts convicted in 24.4% of rape trials completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Trafficking trials did far worse.

Three cautions keep the figure honest. The 43 convictions cover trafficking for every purpose; NCRB does not say how many involved sexual exploitation. They are counted by case, not by the number of people convicted. And trials completed in 2024 include cases registered in earlier years, so 43 is not a share of that year's 2,135 cases. None of these cautions makes the number look better.

## What the law prescribes

Since 1 July 2024, when the BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], trafficking a person for exploitation, sexual exploitation included, has carried 7 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 143. Trafficking a child carries at least 10 years. If a police officer or public servant is involved, the sentence is imprisonment for the rest of that person's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 144 reaches the people who pay. Anyone who knowingly sexually exploits a trafficked child faces 5 to 10 years, and a trafficked adult 3 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for trafficking also commits a crime, under Section 199, punishable with six months to two years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

On paper, few crimes in the code carry heavier sentences. But a law is only as strong as the verdicts it produces, and a punishment that courts impose in a few dozen cases a year is a weak threat, whatever its length. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What the numbers cannot show

The national figures count only cases reported by Anti-Human Trafficking Units. Trafficking is often booked under other laws, such as kidnapping, child labour or the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, so the true number of cases is higher [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The purpose of trafficking is not split by age or sex. And the tables stop at rescue and verdict. They say nothing about whether a survivor found shelter, compensation or work, or was trafficked again by the same network.

The machinery to see more exists. By March 2025, the Nirbhaya Fund had paid for 827 Anti-Human Trafficking Units [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. What the public can see of their work fits in a handful of national tables, and the most important line in them reads 43.

For the 2,347, rescue was a first step, not an ending. The steps after it, a trial that reaches a verdict and a life that does not lead back to the same people, are where India's record is weakest. If you suspect that someone is being trafficked or held for sex, call 112. For a child, call the Child Helpline, 1098.
sex-trafficking-india-convictions.hg:
2024 mein India mein 5,839 trafficking victims rescue kiye gaye. Unhe traffic karne ki sabse badi single wajah forced labour, domestic servitude ya shaadi nahi thi. Woh thi prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation: 2,347 log, yaani 40% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal courts ne trafficking ke 586 trials poore kiye aur sirf 43 mein saza di [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In do numbers ke beech ek aisa crime hai jise kanoon apne sabse gambhir crimes mein ginta hai, aur jiske liye system lagbhag kabhi saza nahi deta.

## 2,347: sabse bada maksad

National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) har rescue hue insaan ke liye darj karta hai ki use kis maksad se traffic kiya gaya tha. 2024 mein rescue hue 5,839 logon mein se 2,347 (40%) ko prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation, 1,493 (26%) ko forced labour, 105 ko domestic servitude aur 98 ko forced marriage ke liye traffic kiya gaya tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Baaki mein se lagbhag sab "other reasons" mein darj hue. Rescue ki is ginti mein pichhle saalon mein darj cases ke victims bhi shaamil hain.

Sarkari shabd hata dijiye, to "prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation" ka matlab hai: logon ko aisa sex sehne par majboor karna jise woh mana nahi kar sakte, baar-baar, jabki paisa koi aur leta hai. Bina consent ke sex rape hai. Isliye 2,347 koi "vice" ka statistic nahi hai. Yeh un logon ki ginti hai jinka munafe ke liye baar-baar rape hua.

Kanoon bhi is asli baat par sahmat hai. Trafficking hua ya nahi, yeh tay karte waqt Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 143 kehta hai ki victim ki consent ka koi matlab nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jo aurat naukri ke liye jaane ko "raazi" hui thi, ya jisse raid team ke saamne kehlwaya gaya ki woh apni marzi se kaam karti hai, woh bhi trafficked person hi hai.

## Kise traffic kiya jaata hai

India ne 2024 mein 6,018 logon ko trafficked ke roop mein darj kiya. Inmein se 2,297 (38%) bachche the: 1,384 ladke aur 913 ladkiyan [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin NCRB trafficking ke maksad ko umar ya sex ke hisaab se cross-tabulate nahi karta [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye national tables se koi nahi bata sakta ki 2,347 mein se kitne bachche the, ya kitne ladke ya aadmi the. Sexual exploitation sirf auraton aur ladkiyon ke saath nahi hota, lekin tables yeh nahi dikha sakte ki aur kis-kis ke saath hua. Trafficked bachchon par hamara alag analysis dekhta hai ki us ginti mein ladke zyada kyun hain.

Ek hypothetical sochiye jo ek jaana-pehchaana pattern follow karta hai. Ek chhote shehar ki 19 saal ki ladki ko ek jaan-pehchaan wale ka message aata hai: bade shehar ke beauty parlour mein naukri, rehne ke liye kamra, aur family ke liye advance. Wahan pahunchkar pata chalta hai ki koi parlour hai hi nahi. Uska phone aur documents le liye jaate hain. Use bataya jaata hai ki us par paisa udhaar hai aur woh use sex se chukayegi. Isme se kuch bhi kidnapping se shuru nahi hua tha, aur ghar walon ko isme se lagbhag kuch bhi dikhta nahi.

## 2,135 cases, 43 convictions

States ki Anti-Human Trafficking Units ne 2024 mein trafficking ke 2,135 cases darj kiye, jo 2023 ke 2,183 se 2.2% kam the; 2022 mein yeh ginti 2,250 thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal courts ne trafficking ke 586 cases mein trial poora kiya. Sirf 43 mein saza hui, yaani conviction rate 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Das mein se nau se zyada trials acquittal ya discharge par khatam hue.

Ise rape ke saath rakhkar dekhiye, jiske trials survivors ko fail karne ke liye pehle se jaane jaate hain: 2024 mein poore hue rape trials mein courts ne 24.4% mein saza di [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Trafficking trials ka haal usse kahin bura tha.

Teen baatein is number ko imaandaar rakhti hain. Yeh 43 convictions har maksad ki trafficking ke hain; NCRB nahi batata ki inmein se kitne sexual exploitation se jude the. Yeh case ke hisaab se gine gaye hain, saza paane wale logon ki ginti ke hisaab se nahi. Aur 2024 mein poore hue trials mein pichhle saalon mein darj cases bhi shaamil hain, isliye 43 us saal ke 2,135 cases ka hissa nahi hai. In mein se koi bhi baat number ko behtar nahi banati.

## Kanoon kya saza kehta hai

1 July 2024 se, jab BNS ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], kisi insaan ko exploitation ke liye traffic karna, sexual exploitation samet, Section 143 ke tahat 7 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment wala crime hai. Bachche ki trafficking par kam se kam 10 saal ki saza hai. Agar koi police officer ya public servant shaamil ho, to saza us insaan ki baaki poori zindagi ki qaid hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 144 un logon tak bhi pahunchta hai jo paisa dete hain. Jo bhi jaante hue kisi trafficked bachche ka sexual exploitation kare, use 5 se 10 saal, aur trafficked adult ke case mein 3 se 7 saal ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jo police officer trafficking ki FIR darj nahi karta, woh bhi Section 199 ke tahat crime karta hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Kagaz par, code mein bahut kam crimes ki saza isse bhaari hai. Lekin koi bhi kanoon utna hi mazboot hota hai jitne uske verdicts, aur jo saza courts saal mein bas kuch darjan cases mein dete hain, woh kitni bhi lambi ho, ek kamzor dhamki hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Numbers kya nahi dikha sakte

National figures sirf Anti-Human Trafficking Units ke report kiye cases ginte hain. Trafficking aksar doosre kanoonon mein darj hoti hai, jaise kidnapping, child labour ya Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, isliye cases ki asli sankhya isse zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Trafficking ka maksad umar ya sex ke hisaab se nahi baanta jaata. Aur tables rescue aur verdict par ruk jaati hain. Woh yeh nahi batati ki survivor ko shelter, compensation ya kaam mila ya nahi, ya kya usi network ne use phir se traffic kar diya.

Zyada dekhne ki machinery maujood hai. March 2025 tak Nirbhaya Fund 827 Anti-Human Trafficking Units ka kharcha utha chuka tha [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Unke kaam ka jo hissa public dekh sakti hai, woh kuch national tables mein simat jaata hai, aur unmein sabse zaroori line par likha hai: 43.

Un 2,347 logon ke liye rescue pehla kadam tha, ant nahi. Uske baad ke kadam, ek trial jo verdict tak pahunche aur ek zindagi jo wapas unhi logon tak na le jaaye, wahin India ka record sabse kamzor hai. Agar aapko shak hai ki kisi ko traffic kiya ja raha hai ya sex ke liye band karke rakha gaya hai, to 112 par call kijiye. Bachche ke liye Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye.

sexual-offences-counted-outside-rape.en:
When India talks about sexual violence, it mostly talks about rape. Yet in police data, rape is not the largest sexual offence. In 2024 police registered 29,536 rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same year they registered 83,908 cases of five other sexual offences against women, from assault and harassment to stalking and voyeurism. That is about 230 cases a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]], on buses, in lanes and offices, at college gates and on phone screens.

## The offences behind the headline

Until 2023, the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) folded all five into one row, "assault on women with intent to outrage her modesty", under Section 354 of the old Indian Penal Code and its sub-sections. Its 2024 report lists them separately [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), in force since 1 July 2024, they are Sections 74 to 78:

- **Assault to outrage modesty (74):** force used on a woman to outrage her modesty, such as unwanted touching.
- **Sexual harassment (75):** unwelcome physical advances, demands for sexual favours, showing pornography against her will, or sexually coloured remarks.
- **Assault to disrobe (76):** force used to strip a woman or compel her to be naked.
- **Voyeurism (77):** watching or capturing images of a woman in a private act, or spreading them.
- **Stalking (78):** repeatedly following or contacting a woman despite her clear disinterest, or monitoring her online.

The rows include girls under 18 unless the case went under POCSO [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. By their wording, harassment and stalking can be committed only by a man [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and all five rows count only women and girls. A man who is harassed or stalked is not in them.

## 83,908 cases, offence by offence

| Offence (BNS section) | Cases in 2024 |
|---|---|
| Assault to outrage modesty (74) | 48,303 |
| Sexual harassment (75) | 15,609 |
| Stalking (78) | 9,865 |
| Assault to disrobe (76) | 8,409 |
| Voyeurism (77) | 1,722 |
| All five | 83,908 |

Assault alone, at 48,303 cases and 7.1 per lakh women, outnumbers rape [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two more groups sit outside even this total: 2,561 attempts to rape, which NCRB counts apart from rape, and 9,338 cases of words, gestures or acts meant to insult a woman's modesty under Section 79 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The rows say little about where. Of the 15,609 harassment cases, police recorded 388 at office premises and 459 in public transport; 12,592, or 81%, went under "other places" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Each figure is also a floor, because NCRB counts every FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Imagine a man who follows a 20-year-old student home from coaching for weeks, then assaults her on the stairs of her building. If her FIR names both offences, it is counted once, as assault. The weeks of stalking vanish from the stalking row.

## Nine years of the same number

The total barely moves: 84,746 cases in 2016, 86,001 in 2017 and 89,097 in 2018 [[ncrb-cii-2018]]; 88,259 in 2019, 85,392 in 2020 and 89,200 in 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2021]]; then 83,344, 83,891 and 83,908 from 2022 to 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In nine years it never fell below 83,344 or rose above 89,200.

Inside that flat line, the mix shifted. Recorded sexual harassment fell from 27,344 cases in 2016 [[ncrb-cii-2018]] to 15,609 in 2024, while stalking rose from 7,190 to 9,865 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Such shifts can reflect which section police choose as much as any change in behaviour.

A flat total means either that this violence is stable, or that the number mostly measures how many women reach a police station and get an FIR written. Survey evidence points to the second. In 2005, 12% of households in a national survey said unmarried girls in their neighbourhood were "sometimes" or "often" harassed; police records implied 0.06%, a gap of about 200 times [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. That comparison is old, but a count stuck at one level for nine years gives no sign the gap has closed.

## What each crime carries in law

Under the BNS, assault to outrage modesty carries one to five years in prison; sexual harassment up to three years, or up to one year for sexually coloured remarks; assault to disrobe three to seven years; voyeurism one to three years on a first conviction and three to seven on a repeat; stalking up to three years, five on a repeat; and words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

These ranges matter at the police station. For offences punishable with three to under seven years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering an FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Several of these offences can fall in that band; rape, with its ten-year minimum, does not. A woman reporting a stalker can be made to wait up to two weeks while police decide whether her complaint becomes a case.

## The court queue: 3,17,491 cases

Registration is the easy part. In 2024 courts completed 22,796 trials for assault to outrage modesty and convicted in 20.1% of them. At year's end, 3,17,491 such cases, 92.3% of those on trial, were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At 2024's pace, the cases already waiting would take more than a decade to clear.

The other offences show the same backlog. Courts convicted in 41.9% of completed sexual harassment trials, 25.2% of stalking trials and 15.4% of trials for insulting a woman's modesty, but more than nine in ten such cases were still pending: 1,22,888 harassment, 52,273 stalking and 53,210 insult cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

For the student in that hypothetical, this can mean years of hearings for an offence that carries at most five years in prison. The delay tells women that reporting is hard, not that it is pointless. A complaint can be made at any police station, wherever the offence happened, or online as an e-FIR, and a woman's account of a sexual offence must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
sexual-offences-counted-outside-rape.hg:
Jab India sexual violence ki baat karta hai, toh zyada tar baat rape ki hoti hai. Lekin police data mein rape sabse bada sexual offence nahi hai. 2024 mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal auraton ke khilaf paanch doosre sexual offences ke 83,908 cases register hue, assault aur harassment se lekar stalking aur voyeurism tak. Yaani roz lagbhag 230 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: buses mein, galiyon aur offices mein, college ke gate par aur phone screens par.

## Headline ke peeche ke offences

2023 tak National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) in paanchon ko ek hi row mein jodta tha: "assault on women with intent to outrage her modesty", yaani purane Indian Penal Code ka Section 354 aur uske sub-sections. 2024 ki report mein yeh alag-alag dikhaye gaye hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 1 July 2024 se laagu Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein yeh Sections 74 se 78 hain:

- **Assault to outrage modesty (74):** aurat ki modesty bhang karne ke iraade se us par force use karna, jaise bina marzi chhoona.
- **Sexual harassment (75):** unwelcome physical advances, sexual favours ki maang, uski marzi ke khilaf pornography dikhana, ya sexually coloured remarks.
- **Assault to disrobe (76):** aurat ke kapde utaarne ya use nanga hone par majboor karne ke liye force use karna.
- **Voyeurism (77):** kisi aurat ko private act mein dekhna ya uski images lena, ya un images ko phailana.
- **Stalking (78):** aurat ke saaf mana karne ke baad bhi baar-baar uska peecha karna ya use contact karna, ya online uski nigraani karna.

In rows mein 18 se kam umar ki ladkiyan bhi shaamil hain, jab tak case POCSO mein darj na hua ho [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kanoon ke shabdon ke hisaab se harassment aur stalking sirf koi aadmi hi kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur paanchon rows sirf auraton aur ladkiyon ko ginti hain. Jis aadmi ke saath harassment ya stalking hoti hai, woh in numbers mein kahin nahi hai.

## 83,908 cases, ek-ek offence

| Offence (BNS section) | 2024 mein cases |
|---|---|
| Assault to outrage modesty (74) | 48,303 |
| Sexual harassment (75) | 15,609 |
| Stalking (78) | 9,865 |
| Assault to disrobe (76) | 8,409 |
| Voyeurism (77) | 1,722 |
| Paanchon milakar | 83,908 |

Akele assault ke 48,303 cases hain, yaani har lakh auraton par 7.1. Yeh rape se zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Do aur groups toh is total ke bhi bahar hain: rape ki koshish ke 2,561 cases, jinhe NCRB rape se alag ginta hai, aur Section 79 ke 9,338 cases, yaani aise shabd, ishaare ya harkatein jinka maksad aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karna tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh rows yeh bhi bahut kam batati hain ki sab kahan hua. Harassment ke 15,609 cases mein se police ne 388 office premises par aur 459 public transport mein darj kiye; 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" mein daal diye gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Har number asal mein ek minimum hai, kyunki NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke neeche ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Socho, ek aadmi hafton tak 20 saal ki ek student ka coaching se ghar tak peecha karta hai, phir uski building ki seedhiyon par us par assault karta hai. Agar FIR mein dono offences hain, toh case ek hi baar gina jaayega, assault ke roop mein. Hafton ki stalking, stalking wali row se gayab ho jaati hai.

## Nau saal, wahi number

Total lagbhag hilta hi nahi: 2016 mein 84,746 cases, 2017 mein 86,001 aur 2018 mein 89,097 [[ncrb-cii-2018]]; 2019 mein 88,259, 2020 mein 85,392 aur 2021 mein 89,200 [[ncrb-cii-2021]]; phir 2022 se 2024 tak 83,344, 83,891 aur 83,908 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nau saal mein yeh kabhi 83,344 se neeche nahi gaya aur kabhi 89,200 se upar nahi gaya.

Is seedhi line ke andar mix zaroor badla. Darj sexual harassment 2016 ke 27,344 cases [[ncrb-cii-2018]] se gir kar 2024 mein 15,609 reh gaya, jabki stalking 7,190 se badh kar 9,865 ho gayi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aise badlaav utne hi is baat se aa sakte hain ki police kaun sa section lagati hai, jitne logon ke bartaav mein kisi asli badlaav se.

Seedhe total ke do hi matlab ho sakte hain: ya toh yeh violence stable hai, ya yeh number zyada tar yeh naapta hai ki kitni auratein police station tak pahunch kar FIR likhwa paati hain. Survey ka saboot doosri baat ki taraf ishaara karta hai. 2005 mein ek national survey mein 12% households ne kaha ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "kabhi-kabhi" ya "aksar" harass kiya jaata hai, jabki police records ke hisaab se yeh sirf 0.06% tha, yaani lagbhag 200 guna ka fark [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. Yeh comparison purana hai, lekin nau saal se ek hi jagah atka hua count is baat ka koi ishaara nahi deta ki yeh fark kam hua hai.

## Kis crime ki kitni saza

BNS mein assault to outrage modesty ki saza ek se paanch saal jail hai; sexual harassment ki teen saal tak, aur sexually coloured remarks ki ek saal tak; assault to disrobe ki teen se saat saal; voyeurism ki pehli baar mein ek se teen saal aur dobara karne par teen se saat saal; stalking ki teen saal tak, dobara karne par paanch saal tak; aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya ishaaron ki teen saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Yeh ranges police station par seedha asar daalti hain. Jin offences mein saza teen saal ya usse zyada, lekin saat saal se kam ho sakti hai, unmein police Deputy Superintendent ki permission se FIR register karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In mein se kai offences is daayre mein aa sakte hain; rape, jiski minimum saza das saal hai, nahi aata. Yaani stalker ki report karne wali aurat ko do hafte tak intezaar karwaya ja sakta hai, jab tak police tay kare ki uski complaint case banegi ya nahi.

## Court ki line: 3,17,491 cases

Register hona aasaan hissa hai. 2024 mein courts ne assault to outrage modesty ke 22,796 trials poore kiye aur unmein se sirf 20.1% mein conviction hua. Saal ke end mein aise 3,17,491 cases, yaani trial wale cases ka 92.3%, pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 ki speed se chalein, toh sirf pehle se ruke hue cases nipataane mein das saal se zyada lag jaayenge.

Baaki offences mein bhi wahi backlog hai. Courts ne poore hue sexual harassment trials mein se 41.9% mein, stalking trials mein se 25.2% mein aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale trials mein se 15.4% mein conviction diya, lekin aise das mein se nau se zyada cases abhi bhi pending the: harassment ke 1,22,888, stalking ke 52,273 aur apmaan ke 53,210 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Upar wali student ke liye iska matlab ho sakta hai saalon tak hearings, ek aise offence ke liye jiski zyada se zyada saza paanch saal hai. Yeh deri auraton ko batati hai ki report karna mushkil hai, yeh nahi ki bekaar hai. Complaint kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho, ya online e-FIR ke zariye, aur sexual offence ke baare mein aurat ka bayaan ek woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

survey-versus-police-sexual-violence-dat.en:
Two official numbers describe sexual violence in India, and they look as if they come from different countries. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 6% of women aged 18 to 49 said they had experienced sexual violence at some point in their lives [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In 2024, police registered 29,536 rape cases, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Neither number is wrong. They answer different questions, and the trouble starts when one is used to "disprove" the other.

## Two numbers, two questions

The survey asks a woman: has this ever happened to you, by anyone, at any time? The police number asks a register: how many rape FIRs were filed this year? One is a share of women, counted per hundred. The other is a count of cases, turned into a rate per lakh.

| | NFHS-5 survey | NCRB police data |
|---|---|---|
| Question | Has it ever happened to you? | How many rape FIRs this year? |
| Who | Women aged 18-49 in sampled homes | Complaints police registered as rape |
| Period | Whole life, asked in 2019-21 | One year, 2024 |
| A husband counts? | Yes | No, if the wife is 18 or older |
| Headline | 6% of women | 4.3 cases per lakh women |

The fourth row matters most. Under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, are not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The survey counts that violence. The rape law does not.

So resist the obvious shortcut. Dividing 4.3 per lakh by 6% does not give you a "reporting rate". It mixes a lifetime with a year, a woman with an FIR, and a survey definition with a legal one.

## What the survey asks, and whom

NFHS is a household health survey. Its questions on violence are a module inside it, asked face to face, and its answers are likely to be under-reported [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Even so, that design lets it see what police files cannot. Among ever-married women who had experienced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband as the perpetrator and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And 4.6% of ever-married women said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Most of this can never become a rape FIR. Our story on what NFHS-5 found behind India's front doors looks at that violence in detail.

The survey has edges too. The 6% describes women aged 18 to 49 only. It says nothing about girls who are still under 18, women over 49, men, boys or transgender people.

## Why surveys undercount too

If the police number is a floor, the survey is a higher floor, not a ceiling. WHO notes that dedicated violence-against-women surveys draw higher disclosure than short modules inside broader surveys [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS is exactly that kind of survey: a violence module inside a health survey. WHO also says women in more gender-equal societies are more likely to disclose sexual violence, while where stigma is high and services are few, the real level is likely much higher than the estimates [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

The global estimates show the pattern. WHO's 2023 figures put sexual violence by someone other than a partner, at any time since age 15, at 4.1% for women aged 15-49 in India, and at 4.7% for Southern Asia against 17.8% for Western Europe [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO warns that such gaps reflect disclosure, stigma and survey methods as well as real differences. Read the low South Asian figures partly as a measure of silence, not simply of safety.

Consider this situation. A surveyor sits in a two-room home in Gaya. The questions about forced sex are part of a long interview about health and children, and the mother-in-law is in the next room. Many women in that chair might say no. When NFHS-6 later reported a fall in violence by husbands, experts quoted by Deccan Herald questioned whether interviews were private and said women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. Our story on whether violence by husbands really fell in NFHS-6 weighs that debate.

## The 200-times gap

The sharpest measure of the gap comes from an older comparison. In 2005, 12% of Indian households told the India Human Development Survey that unmarried girls were "sometimes" or "often" harassed in their neighbourhood. NCRB records implied a figure of only 0.06% of households, a gap of about 200 times [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

This comparison is closer to fair, because both numbers sit on the same footing: a share of households. It is still imperfect, since the survey asked about harassment in the neighbourhood, not inside each home. The same researchers noted that theft was under-recorded too, but by a far smaller margin. Harassment of girls, like rape, is an offence where shame and fear decide who speaks, and the register shows it.

It is old data, and about harassment rather than rape, so do not stretch the ratio onto today's rape figures. Its lesson is about method: compare like with like, or do not compare at all.

## Using both numbers honestly

Use the survey for scale and pattern: how common sexual violence is, who commits it, which women face more of it. Quote it as a minimum: "at least 6% of women aged 18-49".

Use police data for the system: how many complaints reach a station, and what police and courts then do with them. NCRB itself warns that more crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

When you need both in one breath, write it like this:

> In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 6% of women aged 18 to 49 said they had ever experienced sexual violence. Police registered 29,536 rape cases in 2024. The first is a floor for how common sexual violence is. The second counts complaints that reached a police register.

Used for what each can do, the two numbers say more together than either says alone: sexual violence is common, and most of it never reaches the state. In NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].
survey-versus-police-sexual-violence-dat.hg:
Sexual violence par India ke paas do official numbers hain, aur dono ko saath rakho toh lagta hai jaise do alag deshon ki baat ho rahi hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 18 se 49 saal ki 6% auraton ne bataya ki unhone zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi sexual violence jheli hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Doosri taraf, 2024 mein police ne 29,536 rape cases register kiye, yaani har ek lakh auraton par 4.3 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se koi bhi number galat nahi hai. Dono alag-alag sawaalon ke jawab hain. Gadbad tab hoti hai jab ek number se doosre ko "jhootha" saabit kiya jaata hai.

## Do numbers, do sawaal

Survey ek aurat se poochta hai: kya tumhare saath kabhi aisa hua, kisi ne bhi kiya ho, kabhi bhi? Police ka number ek register se poochta hai: is saal rape ki kitni FIRs register hui? Pehla number auraton ka hissa hai, jo har sau par gina gaya. Doosra cases ki ginti hai, jise har lakh par rate mein badla gaya.

| | NFHS-5 survey | NCRB police data |
|---|---|---|
| Sawaal | Kya tumhare saath kabhi aisa hua? | Is saal rape ki kitni FIRs register hui? |
| Kiski ginti | Survey mein chune gaye gharon ki 18-49 saal ki auratein | Woh complaints jo police ne rape case mein register ki |
| Kitna time | Poori zindagi, sawaal 2019-21 mein poochhe gaye | Ek saal, 2024 |
| Pati ki violence gini gayi? | Haan | Nahi, agar wife 18 saal ya usse badi hai |
| Main number | 6% auratein | Har lakh auraton par 4.3 cases |

Chauthi line sabse zaroori hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke hisaab se, agar wife 18 saal se kam ki nahi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex ya koi sexual act rape nahi maana jaata [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Survey is violence ko ginta hai. Rape law ise nahi ginta.

Isliye aasaan shortcut se bacho. Har lakh par 4.3 ko 6% se divide karne se koi "reporting rate" nahi nikalta. Aisa karna poori zindagi ko ek saal se, ek aurat ko ek FIR se, aur survey ki definition ko kanoon ki definition se mila dena hai.

## Survey kya poochta hai, aur kisse

NFHS ghar-ghar jaakar kiya jaane wala health survey hai. Violence ke sawaal iske andar ka ek hissa hain, jo aamne-saamne baith kar poochhe jaate hain, isliye jawabon mein asal se kam violence saamne aane ki poori sambhavna hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Phir bhi, yeh tarika woh dekh leta hai jo police ki files nahi dekh paati. Jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi hui thi aur jinhone sexual violence jheli, unme se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya, aur 14% ne pehle pati ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi hui thi, unme se 4.6% ne bataya ki jab woh nahi chahti thi, tab pati ne zabardasti sex kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isme se zyada tar kabhi rape FIR nahi ban sakta. NFHS-5 ne gharon ke andar kya paaya, is par humari alag story is violence ko detail mein dekhti hai.

Survey ki bhi apni limits hain. 6% wala figure sirf 18 se 49 saal ki auraton ka hai. Isse 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon, 49 se upar ki auraton, aadmiyon, ladkon ya transgender logon ke baare mein kuch pata nahi chalta.

## Surveys bhi kam ginte hain

Police ka number "kam se kam" wali ginti hai. Survey bhi "kam se kam" wali ginti hi hai, bas thodi oonchi; yeh poori tasveer nahi hai. WHO kehta hai ki jo surveys khaas taur par auraton par violence ke liye hote hain, unme auratein zyada khul kar batati hain, aur kisi bade survey ke andar rakhe chhote hisse mein kam [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS bilkul aisa hi survey hai: health survey ke andar violence ka ek hissa. WHO yeh bhi kehta hai ki jahan aurat aur mard mein barabari zyada hai, wahan auratein sexual violence ke baare mein zyada batati hain, aur jahan stigma zyada hai aur madad kam milti hai, wahan asli violence estimate se kahin zyada hone ki sambhavna hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Duniya ke figures mein bhi yahi dikhta hai. WHO ke 2023 ke estimate ke hisaab se India mein 15-49 saal ki 4.1% auraton ne 15 saal ki umar ke baad kabhi pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur se sexual violence jheli. Poore Southern Asia mein yeh 4.7% hai, jabki Western Europe mein 17.8% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO khud warning deta hai ki yeh farq sirf asli violence ka nahi hai; isme bolne ki himmat, stigma aur survey ka tarika bhi shaamil hai. Isliye South Asia ke kam figures ko sirf safety ka nahi, kuch had tak chuppi ka naap bhi samjho.

Ek situation socho. Gaya mein do kamre ke ek ghar mein surveyor baithi hai. Zabardasti sex wale sawaal health aur bachchon ke baare mein ek lambe interview ka hissa hain, aur saas bagal wale kamre mein hai. Us jagah baithi bahut si auratein shayad "nahi" hi kahengi. Jab NFHS-6 mein patiyon ki violence kam dikhi, toh Deccan Herald se baat karne wale experts ne sawaal uthaya ki kya interviews sach mein akele mein hue the, aur kaha ki family ke saamne auratein surveyor ko abuse ke baare mein shayad na batayein [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. NFHS-6 mein patiyon ki violence sach mein ghati ya nahi, is debate par humari alag story hai.

## 200 guna ka gap

Yeh gap kitna bada hai, iska sabse saaf naap ek purane comparison se milta hai. 2005 mein India Human Development Survey mein 12% gharon ne bataya ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "kabhi-kabhi" ya "aksar" harass kiya jaata hai. NCRB records ke hisaab se yeh figure sirf 0.06% gharon ka banta tha, yaani kareeb 200 guna ka farq [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Yeh comparison kaafi had tak fair hai, kyunki dono numbers ek hi scale par hain: kitne percent ghar. Phir bhi yeh perfect nahi hai, kyunki survey ne mohalle mein harassment ke baare mein poochha tha, har ghar ke andar ke baare mein nahi. Isi comparison mein chori bhi records mein kam dikhi, par wahan farq isse bahut chhota tha. Ladkiyon ki harassment, rape ki tarah, aisa crime hai jisme sharm aur darr tay karte hain ki kaun bolega, aur police register mein yahi dikhta hai.

Yeh data purana hai, aur rape nahi, harassment ke baare mein hai. Isliye is 200 guna ko aaj ke rape figures par mat lagao. Iska sabak tarike ke baare mein hai: barabar cheezon ka comparison karo, warna comparison mat karo.

## Dono numbers ka imaandari se use

Survey ka use yeh samajhne ke liye karo ki sexual violence kitni common hai, kaun karta hai, aur kin auraton ke saath zyada hoti hai. Ise minimum ki tarah quote karo: "18-49 saal ki kam se kam 6% auratein".

Police data ka use system ko samajhne ke liye karo: kitni complaints police station tak pahunchti hain, aur phir police aur courts unke saath kya karte hain. NCRB khud warning deta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada crime register hona is baat ka "indicator nahi hai" ki woh shehar doosre se kam safe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Jab dono numbers ek saath batane hon, toh aise likho:

> NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18 se 49 saal ki 6% auraton ne bataya ki unhone kabhi na kabhi sexual violence jheli. 2024 mein police ne 29,536 rape cases register kiye. Pehla number batata hai ki sexual violence kam se kam kitni common hai. Doosra un complaints ki ginti hai jo police register tak pahunchi.

Har number ko uske sahi kaam ke liye use karo, toh dono milkar akele-akele se zyada batate hain: sexual violence common hai, aur iska zyada tar hissa kabhi system tak pahunchta hi nahi. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77% auraton ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

survivors-tell-family-not-institutions.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Indore who comes home from a family wedding and, late that night, tells her elder sister that a relative assaulted her. In that moment the sister is the police station, the hospital, the counsellor and the lawyer. India's national health survey suggests this is the most common scene: among women who sought help after physical or sexual violence, 61% went to their own family [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Who survivors actually tell

The National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) asked women aged 18 to 49 about violence and what they did afterwards. Of those who had faced it, 77% never sought help or told anyone; only 14% sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Help-seeking was highest, 26%, among women who had faced both physical and sexual violence [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Here is where the women who did seek help went [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Source of help (NFHS-5, 2019-21) | Share of women who sought help |
|---|---|
| Their own family | 61% |
| Police | 6% |
| A social service organisation | 3% |
| A doctor or medical staff | 2% |
| A lawyer | 2% |

Every institution built for this moment trails far behind the family. That does not make families the problem. It makes them the system, one nobody has trained.

## Doctors and lawyers: 2%

The doctor figure matters most, because medicine runs on a clock and family discussions do not. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception works up to 5 days after unprotected sex, and works better the sooner it is taken [[who-ec]]. Neither waits for an uncle to arrive or a family meeting to end.

The law has removed the excuse of cost. Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) obliges every hospital, public or private, to give survivors of rape, acid attack and POCSO offences immediate first aid or treatment free of cost, and to inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A hospital in-charge who refuses faces up to a year in prison under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A medical examination for evidence needs the survivor's consent under Section 184 BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The lawyer figure has a quieter cost. Decisions about an FIR, a separation or a "settlement" get made on whatever the family believes the law says, and that belief becomes the law the survivor lives under. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Children who tell no one

For a child, the family is not just the first responder. If anyone is told at all, it is usually the only one. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of children who reported being sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had reported it to the police; those who did tell mostly told a parent [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Among young adults in the same study who had been sexually assaulted as children, only 26.8% had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Boys were not spared: they made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse, in a sample that included many working and street children [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The sample, from 13 states, was not nationally representative and predates the POCSO Act of 2012; our story on the 2007 study explains its limits. But the shape is clear. A child who finally speaks usually speaks to a parent, and that first reaction can decide whether the child ever speaks again.

## When the family is part of the problem

Families are not neutral first responders. Sometimes the accused is one of them. In 2024 police registered 2,134 rape cases in which the accused was a family member [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of 44,126 POCSO penetrative-assault cases, the offender was a family member in 3,658, or 8.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are only the cases that reached a police station.

When the abuser shares the home, silence deepens. Only 11.3% of women who had faced violence solely from their current husband ever sought help, against 23.6% of women abused only by a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Even when the accused is an outsider, families feel pressure: a sister's wedding, the family's name, an offer of money to "settle". The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that a woman who delays reporting rape is lying, and the idea that marrying the rapist restores her honour: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. In Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2021), the Supreme Court ruled that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. If a judge may not suggest it, neither should an elder at a family meeting.

## If it's you they tell

Our guides to the first conversation and the first 72 hours go deeper. Here is the short order for a parent, sibling or friend.

- **Believe first.** Say "I believe you" and "It is not your fault." Questions about clothes, timing or why they did not shout help no one.
- **Hospital before the family meeting.** Any hospital, government or private, the same day. Treatment is free by law; ask about PEP within 72 hours [[who-pep]] and emergency contraception within 5 days [[who-ec]].
- **Let an adult survivor decide about the FIR.** Any police station must record it wherever the crime happened (Zero FIR), it can be sent electronically and signed within 3 days, and the FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. One Stop Centres bring support for women facing violence under one roof; 985 of the 1,033 approved were running in July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].
- **If the survivor is under 18, report.** POCSO requires anyone who knows of child sexual abuse to report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit; failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison, a fine or both [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. The Child Helpline 1098, which is linked to the 112 emergency system, can also help [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Tell the child before you call, and stay with them.
- **Look after yourself too.** Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline, answers on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

This holds whether the person who tells you is a daughter, a son, a brother or a transgender friend. For most survivors who ask for help at all, you are where it starts.
survivors-tell-family-not-institutions.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 19 saal ki ladki family ki ek shaadi se ghar lautti hai. Der raat woh apni badi behen ko batati hai ki ek rishtedaar ne us par sexual assault kiya. Us pal woh behen hi uska police station hai, hospital hai, counsellor hai aur lawyer bhi. Desh ka national health survey kehta hai ki yahi sabse common tasveer hai. Physical ya sexual violence ke baad jin auraton ne help maangi, unmein se 61% apni hi family ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Survivors asal mein kise batati hain

National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne 18 se 49 saal ki auraton se violence ke baare mein poocha, aur yeh bhi ki uske baad unhone kya kiya. Jinhone violence jheli thi, unmein se 77% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Sirf 14% ne help maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jin auraton ne physical aur sexual, dono tarah ki violence jheli thi, unmein help maangne wali sabse zyada thi: 26% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ab dekhiye ki jinhone help maangi, woh gayi kahan [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Help kahan se maangi (NFHS-5, 2019-21) | Help maangne wali auraton mein hissa |
|---|---|
| Apni family | 61% |
| Police | 6% |
| Koi social service organisation | 3% |
| Doctor ya medical staff | 2% |
| Lawyer | 2% |

Is waqt ke liye jitne bhi institutions bane, sab family se bahut peeche hain. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki family hi problem hai. Matlab yeh hai ki asli system family hi hai, aur us system ko kisi ne training nahi di.

## Doctors aur lawyers: 2%

Doctor wala figure sabse zyada matter karta hai, kyunki dawai ghadi dekh kar chalti hai, family ki discussion nahi. HIV se bachane wali dawai, yaani post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), jitni jaldi ho sake shuru karni hoti hai, aur har haal mein 72 ghante ke andar. Phir yeh 28 din tak leni hoti hai [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception unprotected sex ke 5 din baad tak kaam karti hai, aur jitni jaldi lo utna behtar [[who-ec]]. Yeh dawaiyan na kisi chacha ke aane ka wait karti hain, na family meeting khatam hone ka.

Kharche ka bahana kanoon pehle hi khatam kar chuka hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 397 kehta hai ki har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, rape, acid attack aur POCSO offences ke survivors ko turant first aid ya ilaaj free mein dega, aur police ko inform karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital in-charge ilaaj se mana kare, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 200 ke tahat ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Evidence ke liye medical examination sirf survivor ke consent se hoga, BNSS ka Section 184 yahi kehta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Lawyer wale figure ka nuksaan chupchaap hota hai. FIR karni hai ya nahi, alag rehna hai ya nahi, "settlement" karna hai ya nahi, yeh faisle is par hote hain ki family kanoon ko kya samajhti hai. Aur family ki yahi samajh survivor ke liye kanoon ban jaati hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Bachche jo kisi ko nahi batate

Bachche ke liye family sirf pehla sahara nahi hai. Agar bachcha kisi ko batata bhi hai, toh aksar bas family ko. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein jin bachchon ne kaha ki un par sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko report kiya tha. Jinhone kisi ko bataya, unhone zyada tar maa ya papa ko bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Isi study mein aise young adults bhi the jin par bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha. Unmein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Ladke bhi nahi bache: sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the, aur is sample mein kaam karne wale aur sadak par rehne wale bachche badi sankhya mein the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Yeh sample 13 states se tha, poore desh ki tasveer nahi deta, aur 2012 ke POCSO Act se bhi pehle ka hai. Is study ki limits humne 2007 study wale article mein samjhayi hain. Phir bhi pattern saaf hai. Jo bachcha aakhirkaar bolta hai, woh aksar maa ya papa se bolta hai, aur unka pehla reaction tay kar sakta hai ki bachcha dobara kabhi bolega ya nahi.

## Jab family hi problem ka hissa ho

Family har baar neutral first responder nahi hoti. Kabhi-kabhi accused family ka hi koi hota hai. 2024 mein police ne 2,134 aise rape cases register kiye jinmein accused family member tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO ke 44,126 penetrative sexual assault cases mein se 3,658 mein accused family member tha, yaani 8.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur yeh sirf woh cases hain jo police station tak pahunche.

Jab violence karne wala usi ghar mein rehta hai, toh chuppi aur gehri ho jaati hai. Jin auraton ne sirf apne current husband se violence jheli, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi help maangi. Jinhone sirf former husband se violence jheli thi, unmein yeh figure 23.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Accused bahar ka ho, tab bhi family par pressure hota hai: behen ki shaadi, family ki izzat, "matter settle" karne ke liye paison ka offer. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook is soch ko galat batati hai ki der se complaint karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai, aur is soch ko bhi ki rapist se shaadi karne se uski izzat wapas aa jaati hai. Handbook saaf kehti hai: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. 2021 mein Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki courts compromise ya shaadi ka suggestion nahi de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Jab judge yeh suggestion nahi de sakta, toh family meeting mein baithe kisi elder ko bhi nahi dena chahiye.

## Agar aapko bataya jaye

Pehli baatcheet aur shuru ke 72 ghanton par hamari guides mein zyada detail hai. Yahan maa-baap, bhai-behen ya dost ke liye ek chhota sa order hai.
